segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ, ᎠᏂ-Jackson ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᎳᏬᏗ Ꮒ,ᏓᏳᏂᎶᏒ quartet ᏧᏃᏢᏒ … ᏔᎵ, ᎠᎾᏝᏅᏟ, ᎨᎵ ᏦᎢ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎩᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏱᏓᏂ,ᏘᏲᎯ, ᏥᎨᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) while they were on the stage.
segments.transliteration: nahena, ani-Jackson tsigehv elawodi ni,dayunilosv quartet tsunotlvsv … tali, anatlanvtli, geli tsoi’le yigi, gila yigohida, yidani,tiyohi, tsigehv (uyetsi,sgv) while they were on the stage.
segments.translation: The Jacksons, from Cherokee, North Carolina used to have a quartet. There were two brothers, or three. They would all disagree about things sometimes, [laughs] while they were on the stage.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: You all can start whenever you’re ready.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Okay. Now…

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: To start, what are your two’s names in English?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: DJ McCarter.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Francis McCarter.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Usgiyug(i)

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Usgiyug(i)

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Nvts(i)

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Nvts(i) … What does that mean, “Usgiyug(i)?”

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏣᏩᏕᏅ’Ꮫ ᏔᎵ, ᏓᎩ,ᏍᎩᏳᎩ, ᎠᏯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏓᏬᎥ ᎤᏍᎩᏳᎩ, ᎠᏂᏌᎹᏗ ᎠᎾ,ᏗᎰ ᏔᎵ, ᏱᏚᏂᏍᎩᏳᎩ, Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏱᎩ,
segments.transliteration: tsawadenv’dv tali, dagi,sgiyugi, aya tsigehv sgi yusdi, elisi, dawov usgiyugi, anisamadi ana,diho tali, yidunisgiyugi, tla howa yigi,
segments.translation: When I was born, I had two crowns on my head. That’s what my grandma named me, Usgiyug(i). They say people with two crowns are intelligent… it’s not true. [laughs]

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: He’s talking about himself.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where were you all born?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ … ᎢᏲ ᏧᎨᏓᎵᏴ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ‘Ꮲ ᏑᏓᎵ, ᏱᏅᏓ, ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎣᎩᏂᎾᎷᏒ Briggs ᎣᎦᏕᏅ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᎤᎲ Ꮎ ᎦᏙᎯ, ᎠᏥᏁᎴ ᎫᏝ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎣᎩᎷᏨ
segments.transliteration: ayv, gehv … iyo tsugedaliyv awadenv ‘tlv sudali, yinvda, yawadetiyvda, gehv ogininalusv Briggs ogadenv elisi, uhv na gadohi, atsinele gutla tsigehv una ogilutsv
segments.translation: As for me, I was born in Pumpkin Hollow. I was about six months old when we went up the hill to Briggs. My grandmother had land given to her that was locked. That’s where we arrived.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And what about you, where were you born?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Claremore Hospital, I don’t know when. [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏗᏩᏛᏒ ᎨᎲ ‘ᏥᏣᏕᏅ’ ᏣᏗ “ᎢᎾᎨ’Ꮫ ᎤᎩᏂᏴᏗ,” ᎠᎾ,ᏗᏍᎬ, ᎮᎾ, ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: diwadvsv gehv ‘tsitsadenv’ tsadi “inage’dv uginiyvdi,” ana,disgv, hena, gehv
segments.translation: Where I grew up and you said, ‘when you were born,’ “You were caught in the woods,” that’s what they said.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏗᏇᏅᏒ’Ꮫ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ᎠᎩᏂᏴᏛ’Ꮽ yeah, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎨᎲ “ᏗᎦᏂᏱᏍᎩ,” ᏣᏃᎮᎰ Ꮎ “midwife” ᏍᎩᎾ Ms. Kelly ᏧᏙᎢᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏆᏞᏒ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ
segments.transliteration: diquenvsv’dv awadenv aginiyvdv’wu yeah, ahani, gehv “diganiyisgi,” tsanoheho na “midwife” sgina Ms. Kelly tsudoida, tsigehv sgina agi,squatlesv tsigehv awadenv
segments.translation: I was born in my house, I was delivered. The “Diganiyisg(i)”, the midwife, they call it. Ms. Kelly was her name. That’s who caught me when I was born.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎤᏠᏱᏍᎪ ᏂᎯ? ᏂᎯ,’Ꮫ ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ ᏣᏕᏅ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: utloyisgo nihi? nihi,’dv ganaga,ti tsadenv dohv?
segments.translation: Was it the same for you? Oh, you said you were born in the hospital, right?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ Ꮎ ᏗᏂᏂᏱᏍᎩ, ᏣᏁᎲ ᎠᏩᎵ,Ꭼ ᎥᏍᎩ ᏗᏢ, ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ ᎨᎲ … ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏳ, ᎥᎩᏙ’Ꮫ ᎥᏍᎩ ᎥᎬᏁᎸ ᎨᎲ “ᎠᏥᏂᏴᏛ,” ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv asesgini, aqua,dvganv na dininiyisgi, tsanehv awali,gv vsgi ditlv, aninohesgv yuli,stanidolv gehv … iga hena, doyu, vgido’dv vsgi vgvnelv gehv “atsiniyvdv,” tsana,dihv
segments.translation: Uh huh. But I heard about the midwives that were around. I couldn’t remember what they were saying happened. But really… My brother was born that way. “He was delivered,” they said.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᏥᎩ, ᎭᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᎾᎾ ᏥᏍᏗᏁᎳ ᏂᏍᏗᏁᎶ
segments.transliteration: nowu’nv tsigi, hala yigohida, nana tsisdinela nisdinelo
segments.translation: How about now? How long have you all lived where you all live now?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎡᏧᎳ ᎨᎲ ᎯᏍᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎤᎶᏒᏍᏗ, ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ‘Ꮲ ᎯᏍᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏌᏭ … ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ ᏑᏓᎵ, ᏱᏅᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ, ᏁᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏌᏭ’Ꮫ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎤᎾ --ᎬᏩᏕᏅ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎠᏩᏛᏒ
segments.transliteration: etsula gehv hisgi,sgohi, ulosvsdi, tsudetiyvda, ‘tlv hisgi,sgohi, sawu … ayv, gehv sudali, yinvda, tsigehv nowu, neli,sgohi, sawu’dv tsudetiyvda, una --gvwadenv ahani, awadvsv
segments.translation: Together, over 50 years, nearly 51. As for me, about six months ago, it was 81 years since I was born here, where I grew up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And how about you? Was it in Claremore?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: Uh… ᎠᎬᏱ’Ꮫ … ᎠᏆᏅ,Ꮫ ᎨᎲ … Kenwood ᏦᎦᏕᏅ ᎢᎪᎯᏗ no – ‘Ꮲ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎯᏍᎩ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᏎ ᏥᏙᎦᏓᏅᏒ’Ꮓ … Rose, OK ᏦᎩᎷᏨ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏤᎵᎪ -- --ᏦᎦ,ᏙᎵ,Ꮢ ᎤᎾ ᎣᏤᎲ ᏱᎪᎯᏗ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏣᏁᎳ, ᎠᏎ ᏍᎪᎯ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ, … ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏅᏒ ᏃᏭ, Teresita, OK ᎤᏂᎷᏤ ᎡᏚᏓ, ᎤᏤᎵᎪ ᎤᎾ … ᎦᏙ ᏣᏓ, Ꮎ
segments.transliteration: Uh… agvyi’dv … aquanv,dv gehv … Kenwood tsogadenv igohidi no – ‘tlv sgina, hisgi,’dv ase yawadetiyvda, gese tsidogadanvsv’no … Rose, OK tsogilutsv gilo utseligo -- --tsoga,doli,sv una otsehv yigohidi nowu’nv, tla yawanv,ta, tsanela, ase sgohi,’le yigi, yawadetiyvda, gehv nowu, … una,danvsv nowu, Teresita, OK unilutse eduda, utseligo una … gado tsada, na
segments.translation: Uh…at first, from what I know, we lived in Kenwood for a while. Wait, no, when I was five years old, we moved from there to Rose, OK. We were renting a house there for a while, from someone. When I was about eight or 10 years old, we moved to Teresita, OK. My grandfather had an allotment there. What was it you said before?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Land.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Land…

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: …allotted.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: …ᎫᏝ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, Ꮟ ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏄᏍᏗ, ᎣᎩᎭ, … ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ,…
segments.transliteration: …gutla squu sgihena, si hena, osda, nusdi, ogiha, … tali,sgohi,…
segments.translation: We still have the land, it was about 20…

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: …acres…

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: …ᏳᏟᎶᏓ, ᎢᎦ Ꭻ-ᎫᏝ Ꮟ Ꮟ ᎣᎦᏤᎵ ᎡᏚ--ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏥᏁᎸ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ, ᎣᎦᏤᎵ ᏦᎢ, ᏃᏥᎠ [ᎣᏣᏝᏅᏝ]
segments.transliteration: …yutliloda, iga gu-gutla si si ogatseli edu--edoda, tsigehv atsinelv vsgina, ogatseli tsoi, notsia [otsatlanvtla]
segments.translation: …acres, under allotment. My grandfather gave it to my dad, so it’s still ours. There’s three of us. [siblings]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ‘Ꮩ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎴ ᏍᏓᎵᎪ ᏕᏍᏓᏓᏩᏛᎮ ᎥᏍᎩᏴ ᎠᎨᎢ ᏗᏯᏍᏓᏓᎸ
segments.transliteration: ‘do nuli,stanidole sdaligo desdadawadvhe vsgiyv agei diyasdadalv
segments.translation: How did it happen that you all met after living so far apart?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Well … ᎠᎬᏱ, ᏥᏲᎵᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎯᎾ … ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏦᎩᎾ,ᏛᏒ ᎠᏂᏁᎸ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, car wreck ᏧᏢ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᎾ ᎦᎵ,ᏅᏛ ᏓᎵᏆ, Ꮎ Downing St. ᏣᏃᎮᎰ … ᏚᎾ,ᏓᏍᏆᎶᏍᏔᏅ big truck ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏥᏲᎵᎰ ᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᏃ … ‘Ꮲ ᏱᏥᎪᎥ ᏱᏥᎶᎬ ᎮᎾ, ᏃᏭᏅ, … ‘ᎸᏢ’Ᏼ ᏓᏩᎵ,ᏨᏯᏍᏔᏅ ᏥᏯᏛᏗ ᎣᎩᎾ,ᎵᎪ,Ꮧ … ᏙᏳ’Ꮓ ᎣᎩᏂᎵᎪᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᏓᎴᏅᎲ … ‘Ꮲ’Ꮫ ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎠᏰᏟ, ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᎣᎩᎾ,ᎵᎪᏅ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏥᏙᎩᎾ,ᏨᏍᏔᏅ
segments.transliteration: Well … agvyi, tsiyoligv tsigehv hina … etsulaha tsogina,dvsv aninelv tsigehv nowu’nv, car wreck tsutlv sgina una gali,nvdv daliqua, na Downing St. tsanoheho … duna,dasqualostanv big truck sgina, tsiyoliho gehv nowuno … ‘tlv yitsigov yitsilogv hena, nowunv, … ‘lvtlv’yv dawali,tsvyastanv tsiyadvdi ogina,ligo,di … doyu’no oginiligohv nahiyu udalenvhv … ‘tlv’dv sudetiyvda, ayetli, yigohida, ogina,ligonv nowunv tsidogina,tsvstanv
segments.translation: Well… I met her, me and her late husband grew up together. He got killed in a car accident in Tahlequah on Downing Street. He had a head-on collision with a big truck. And I already knew her. When I saw her somewhere, I said hello to her. Sometime later, I got brave enough to ask her to go with me. So, we started dating, and about a year and a half later, we got married.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You two have been married for about 50 years, right?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎦᎵ,ᏆᏍᎪᎯ, ᏔᎵ,’Ꮫ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏌᏗᏒ September ᎧᎸ … ᏙᎩᎾ,ᏨᏍᏔᏅ … ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎴ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏰᏟ, ᏥᏓᎾᏁᏍᎬ -- Housing Authority … September ᎧᎸ ᏙᎩᎾ,ᏨᏍᏔᏅ December ᎠᎬᏱ’Ꮽ, ᎣᎩᎾᏁᎳ ᏗᏢ … ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎪᏍᏗᏁᎶ ᎤᎾ ᎡᏧᎳ’Ꮫ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎠᎴ ᎯᏍᎩ--ᎯᏍᎩᏍᎪᎯ, ᏃᎩᎾᏕᏘᏴᏓ, (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏍᏊᏅ
segments.transliteration: vv gali,quasgohi, tali,’dv tsudetiyvsadisv September kalv … dogina,tsvstanv … sgina ale tsalagi, ayetli, tsidananesgv -- Housing Authority … September kalv dogina,tsvstanv December agvyi’wu, oginanela ditlv … gali,tsode nahiyu gosdinelo una etsula’dv gali,tsode ale hisgi--hisgisgohi, noginadetiyvda, (uyetsi,sgv) squunv
segments.translation: Uh huh. It was ’72, in September when we got married. And then Cherokee Nation Housing Authority, they were building houses. We got married in September, then, in December 1st, that’s when we moved into our house. And we’ve been living there since. Both our marriage and our house, that means we are both 50 years old. [laughs] That’s it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What kind of jobs did you all have?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,’Ꮫ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ … lumber yard ᎠᎴ concrete truck ᏥᎯᎵᏙᎯ, ᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎥᎩᎾᏢᏅ truck ᎠᎩᎯᎵᏓᏍᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎦᏂᎩᏍᎬ to Nebraska – Omaha, Nebraska. Iowa, Missouri, Kansas. ᎦᎵᏟᏙᎲ … ᏦᎢᏁᎢ, ᎢᎦ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎦᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᏃᏭᏅ, ‘Ꮲ ᏔᎵ, ᏦᏍᎪᎯ, ᏙᏓᏫᏕᎾ, ᏑᎾᎴ ᎥᏥᎷᎬ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏕᏥᏃᎩᏍᏓᏂᏙᎲ ᎤᎾᎵ,ᏍᎩᏍᏗ ᏍᏊ ᏙᏓᏫᏕᎾ, ᎤᏒ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ, ᏍᏊ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ, ᏥᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᎠᏕᎳ, Ꮭ ᎤᏟ ᎢᎦ ᎦᏗᏔᏍᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᎦᏗᏔᏍᎨ Ꮟ …ᏙᎩᎾ,ᏠᏒ ᏥᎨᎲ …
segments.transliteration: ayv,’dv gehv na … lumber yard ale concrete truck tsihilidohi, gehv nowunv vginatlvnv truck agihilidasdi ahani, ganigisgv to Nebraska – Omaha, Nebraska. Iowa, Missouri, Kansas. galitlidohv … tsoinei, iga, ahani, ganigisgv nowunv, ‘tlv tali, tsosgohi, dodawidena, sunale vtsilugv nowunv detsinogisdanidohv unali,sgisdi squu dodawidena, usv sdigida, squu sdigida, tsigotlvsgv adela, tla utli iga gaditasge tsigehv (uyetsi,sgv) iga hena, gaditasge si …dogina,tlosv tsigehv …
segments.translation: As for me, I worked in a lumber yard and drove a concrete truck. I got hired on to drive a truck. I left here to Nebraska. Omaha, Nebraska. And then Iowa, Missouri, Kansas. I was driving to these places. I would leave on a Wednesday and get home about 2:30 on a Saturday. I was playing music in dancehalls on Saturday nights. I was making a little bit of money, but not much. I was drinking then. [laughs] I was still drinking a lot when we met.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,Ꮕ … ᏛᎵ,Ꮟ ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ Sun Oil Company ᎪᎯᏗ ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏃᏭ, ᎠᎭᏂ ᎡᏍᎦᏂ, ᏣᎩᎷᏨ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᏓᏩ-- ᎠᏭ Ꮎ Tahlequah
segments.transliteration: ayv,nv … dvli,si dagilvwi,sdanehv Sun Oil Company gohidi dagilvwi,sdanelv nowu, ahani esgani, tsagilutsv tsuna,deloquasdi dawa-- awu na Tahlequah
segments.translation: I worked in Tulsa. Sun Oil Company, I worked there for a while. Then I came back this way to a school in Tahlequah.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: It was Briggs at first, wasn’t it?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎠᏎ ᏔᎵ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ Briggs ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᏃᏭᏅ, ᏓᎵᏆ, ᎤᎾ,ᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᎨᏒ Ꮎ ᏃᏭ Indian Education ᏫᎬᎩᎧᏅ ᏃᏅ ᎤᎾ … ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, … ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ Ꭲ-ᎢᏴ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏃᏭ, retire ᎾᏩ--ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ … 23 years ago ᎾᎯᏳ retire ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: sudetiyvda ase tali,’le yigi, yudetiyvda, dagilvwi,sdanelv Briggs tsuna,deloquasdi nowunv, daliqua, una,delahosv tsalagi, tsiwonisgi gesv na nowu Indian Education wigvgikanv nonv una … tali,sgohi, … tali,sgohi,’dv ase i-iyv yudetiyvda, dagilvwi,sdanelv tsanv,ta, nowu, retire nawa--nawadvnelv … 23 years ago nahiyu retire nawadvnelv
segments.translation: For one year, or maybe two years, I worked at Briggs School and then at Tahlequah. They figured out I was a Cherokee speaker. Then they put me in Indian Education. I worked there for 20 years. Then I retired. I’ve been retired for 23 years.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How many were in your family?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Your siblings and your brothers, how many were in your family?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎨᎲ ‘Ꮲ ᏣᏁᎳ, ᏃᏥᎥ … ᏦᏥᏲᏟ, ᏦᎢ ᎾᏂᎥ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ, ᏃᏭᏅ … ᎡᏠᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏲᎱᏒ ᏦᎢ ᎾᏂᎥ Ꮷ-ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᎡᏥ’Ꮓ ᏚᏘᎾᏫᏛᎲ ᏂᎦᏓ, Ꮩ-ᏙᎦᏛᏒ ᏌᏭ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᎾᏁᎳᏛ ᏌᏭ ᎯᎾ [Francis]. ᎤᏓᏂᎳᎨ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᏧᎾᏁᎳ,Ꮫ …
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv gehv ‘tlv tsanela, notsiv … tsotsiyotli, tsoi naniv tsuna,tana, nowunv … etlogi tsigehv uyohusv tsoi naniv tsu-tsuni,sdi etsi’no dutinawidvhv nigada, do-dogadvsv sawu gali,tsode sgina iga hena, sgina unaneladv sawu hina [Francis]. udanilage’dv tsigehv atsutsa, tsunanela,dv …
segments.translation: And us, there were about eight of us children. Then three adults. My aunt passed away and she had three little ones. My mom took them in. We all grew up in one house. It was one of them who married this one [Francis]. He was the oldest one, that’s who she married.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Me—

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ‘Ꮲ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ ᏦᎢ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎠᎨᎢ,-- ᎤᎾ Briggs-Ꭲ ᏦᎦᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎠᎭ,Ꮒ, ᎤᏂᎷᏨ ᏏᏉᏲ ᎠᏂᏐᎢ, … ᎤᎾ ᏚᎾ,ᏛᏒ … ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ Briggs school-ᎢᏭ ᏓᏩᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ ᎥᎩ,ᏛᏛᏁ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᎤᎾ ᎠᎩᎷᎯᏍᏗ “ᎭᏛ” (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏴᎩ,ᏍᏚᏅ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ‘ᎸᏢ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏯᏩᎵ,ᏘᏎ -- ᏯᏩᎵ,ᏘᏎ ᎮᎾ, ᏯᎩᎷᏨ ᎠᎭᏂ,
segments.transliteration: ‘tlv’dv ase tsoi tsudetiyvda, agei,-- una Briggs-i tsogadelo;quav nowunv aha,ni, unilutsv siquoyo anisoi, … una duna,dvsv … ayv, gehv Briggs school-iwu dawadelo,quav vgi,dvdvne yawaduli una agiluhisdi “hadv” (uyetsi,sgv) yvgi,sdunv hena, ahani, ‘lvtlv (uyetsi,sgv) yawali,tise -- yawali,tise hena, yagilutsv ahani,
segments.translation: It was about…It was about three or four years we went to school at Briggs. Then the others went to Sequoyah. That’s where they grew up. Me, I just went to school at Briggs. They did ask me if I wanted to go Sequoyah. "No,” [I told them.] [laughs] They probably would’ve thrown me in jail [laughs] for running away. I would’ve run away if I came here.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did they have to stay there?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: The others.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did all of them grow up nearby?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What do they call Briggs in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: I couldn’t tell you, I don’t know. I guess just “Briggsi-i” [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And how about you? How many were there of you all?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏅᎩ, ᎠᏂᏔᎵ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᎠᏂᏔᎵ, … ᏦᏍᏗ--ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ, … ᎡᏚᏚ ᎥᏍᎩ ᎤᏤᎵᎪ Ꮶ--ᏌᏭ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎣᏤᎲ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎡᎵᏏ, ᎡᏚᏚ, ᎡᏙᏓ,’ᎢᏅ, … Ꭱ-ᎡᏥ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏣᏘᏂ,’Ꮲ ᏫᎦᏁᎸ Ꮭ ᎤᎾ ᎤᏛᏒ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎡᏙᏓ,’Ꮽ, ᏙᎦᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ … ᏦᏥᏲᏟ, ᏃᏭᏅ, … ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ Sa—Rose ᏦᏥ-ᏦᏤᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ … ᏃᏭ Ꮎ ᎣᏍ--ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏙᎩᏂᎧᏂᏢ Daddy ᎠᏭ Sequoyah ᏙᎩᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ ᏞᎦ, about ᏅᎩ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, … ᏙᎩᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎡᎵᏭ ᎣᏥᎷᎬ ᎾᎮᎾ, ᏙᏆᎴᎳ, ᏣᏅ,Ꮨ Ꮎ ᏐᏈᎵ, Ꮧ--ᎥᏍᎩ’Ꮫ … Ꭳ-Ꭳ-ᎣᏨ,ᏗᏍᎬ ᎣᏤᎮ--ᎣᏤᏙᎲ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏃᏭᏅ, … ᎠᎭᏂ--ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏱᎣᎩᏂᎷᏣ, ᏍᎩ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᎣᎩᏁᏙᎸ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏙᎩᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, … ᏃᏭ … … ᎪᎩ ᏗᏟ, ᏱᎩ, ᏃᏭ ᏥᏓᏂᏲᎱ--ᏥᏓᏂ--ᏥᏓᏂᏲᏎᎰ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎤᎾ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎣᏍᏕᎬ … ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ Ꮎ … Teresita ᎣᏤᎲ ᎣᏥᏁᎸ ᎤᎾᎾ -- ᎤᎾ ᏬᏍᏕᏙᎲ ᏃᏭᎴ … ᏯᏂᎴᏂᎲ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎣᏍᏕᏙᎲ--ᎣᏍᏕᏙᎲ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᎥᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ ᏅᎩ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎠᏎ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏁ ᏃᏭᏅ, … ᏦᎩᏂ-ᏦᎩᏂᏑᎵ,ᎪᏨ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ … Teresita ᏙᎩᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ ᏂᎦᏓ, Teresita ᏙᎦᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ’Ꮓ ᎤᎾ … ᎣᎩᏍᏆᏛ, ᏃᏭᎴ Oaks—Oaks ᏃᏭ Oaks-Ꭲ … ᏙᎦᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ ᎤᎾ ᏓᎩ,ᏍᏆᏛ ᎠᏴ, ᎾᏍᏊ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ Ꮭ-Ꮭ ᏳᏍᏆᏕ ᎤᏁᎳ,Ꮫ--ᎤᏁᎳ,Ꮫ … ᏓᎳᏚ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏓᎦᏨᏍᏔᏅ, ᏃᏭ ᎤᏩᏌ, … ᏧᏪᏅᏒ ᎤᏬᏢᏅ
segments.transliteration: nvgi, anitali, anitsutsa, anitali, … tsosdi--anigeyutsa, … edudu vsgi utseligo tso--sawu gali,tsode otsehv nigada, elisi, edudu, edoda,’inv, … e-etsi gehv utsatini,’tlv wiganelv tla una udvsv yigehe edoda,’wu, dogadvhistanv … tsotsiyotli, nowunv, … una’dv Sa—Rose tsotsi-tsotsehe nahiyu … nowu na os--tsosdadalv ahani, doginikanitlv Daddy awu Sequoyah dogina,delo,quav tlega, about nvgi’dv ase yudetiyvda, yigohida, … dogina,delo,quav asesgini, eliwu otsilugv nahena, doqualela, tsanv,ti na soquili, di--vsgi’dv … o-o-otsv,disgv otsehe--otsedohv ‘lvtlv nowunv, … ahani--ahani, yioginilutsa, sgi yigohida, oginedolv ahani, dogina,delo,quav asesgini, … nowu … … gogi ditli, yigi, nowu tsidaniyohu--tsidani--tsidaniyoseho diniyotli, una nowule osdegv … nowu’dv na … Teresita otsehv otsinelv unana -- una wosdedohv nowule … yanilenihv tsuna,delo,quasdi ahani, nowule osdedohv--osdedohv yigohida, vsgi’dv ase nvgi yudetiyvda, ase nuli,stane nowunv, … tsogini-tsoginisuli,gotsv, ahani, nowu’dv … Teresita dogina,delo,quav nigada, Teresita dogadelo,quav’no una … ogisquadv, nowule Oaks—Oaks nowu Oaks-i … dogadelo,quav una dagi,squadv ayv, nasquu tsosdadalv tla-tla yusquade unela,dv--unela,dv … daladu’dv ase yudetiyvda, gehv dagatsvstanv, nowu uwasa, … tsuwenvsv uwotlvnv
segments.translation: Four. Two boys and two of us girls. We all lived at my grandfather’s house. It was my grandpa, grandma, and my dad. My mom lived somewhere else. She didn’t raise us, our dad did. Then, we still lived in Rose. Our daddy brought me and my sister here to Sequoyah; we went to school there for about four years. We went to school there for four years, but we were coming home. You know, back then the wagons were being pulled by horses, that’s what we used getting around. When we got here, we stayed that long, going to school. When it was summer, they would let the students go. We would go home, and then at that time we lived in Teresita, OK. And then when school started again, we went back. After about four years of learning here, we quit. Then we went to school in Teresita, we all went to school there. When we finished [8th grade] we went to Oaks. We went to school at Oaks. That’s where I graduated. My sister didn’t graduate; she got married. She was 16 when she got married. Then she made herself a home.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮝ-Ꮝ “Teresita ᏛᏲᏥᏁᎸ” ᏣᏗᏍ? ᏏᏍ, Ꮎ ᏐᏈᎵ, ᎠᏂᎾ,ᏌᏁᏍᎬ,? ᎤᎾ ᎢᏤᏙᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ
segments.transliteration: s-s “Teresita dvyotsinelv” tsadis? sis, na soquili, anina,sanesgv,? una itsedohv nahiyu
segments.translation: You said you all lived in Teresita? Did you all still have horse-drawn wagons when you all were there at that time?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And you all went that far?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏦᏥᎳᏫᏥᏙᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎠᏂ-Johnson-Ꭲ ᎡᎳᏗ, ᎣᏤᏙ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏥᎾᎷᏍᎬ ᏒᏃᏱ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎾᎮᎾ, -- ᎠᏨᏍᏗ ᎠᎯᎮ Daddy ᏥᎨᎲ ‘ᏍᎦᏍᏗ’Ꮫ --ᏙᏥᏲᏟ, ᎢᎦ ᎣᎦᏚᎵᏍᎬ ᎾᎥ ᎠᎢᏐ -- -- ᎣᎦᏂᎩᏍᏗ ᎣᏥᏍᎦᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv nowule tsotsilawitsidoho tsigehv … ani-Johnson-i eladi, otsedo gehv otsinalusgv svnoyi nowule nahena, -- atsvsdi ahihe Daddy tsigehv ‘sgasdi’dv --dotsiyotli, iga ogadulisgv nav aiso -- -- oganigisdi otsisgahv
segments.translation: Yeah. And then, we went to church at Johnson’s. We were walking. We went up a hill at midnight; my daddy would be carrying a light. We all wanted to walk beside dad, because we were afraid. [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᏍ-ᎾᏍ coal oil ᏣᏃᎮᎲ ᏍᎩᏍ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏟᏍᏛ, ᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: nas-nas coal oil tsanohehv sgis yusdi atlisdv, gehe?
segments.translation: Was it that coal oil, was that what was in the light?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Mhm.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Go(i) Uhyvtl(a), coal oil.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎢᎦ’Ꮫ … … --ᎾᏍᏊ … --ᎡᎵᏏ ᏍᎩᏂ ᏧᎵᏏ, ᏍᏊ ᎠᏁᎲ ᎤᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎣᏤᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏧᎾ,ᏔᏂᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ Ꮎ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ, ᎤᏂᏴᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᎠᏂᏯᎥ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏌᏭ ᏳᏂᎩᏌ, ᎤᎾᎵ --ᎠᎾᏂᎩᏍᎬ, ᎠᎭᏂ, Teresita ᏩᏂᎷᎪ ᎤᏙᏓᏆᏓ, ᎠᏎ ᎡᎳᏗ, ᎠᎾᏂᎩᏍᎨ ᏃᏭᏅ, ᏭᏂᎷᏣ, ᏃᏭᎴ … -- ᎤᎾ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ, --ᎥᏍᎩ ᏗᏢ, ᎡᏚᏚ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᎴ --ᏙᏗᏘᏁᎲ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏗᏢ, ᏙᎦᎧᎲᏍᎪ ᎤᏙᏓᏆᏓ, --ᎤᏙᏓᏆᏓ, --ᎠᎾᎢᏒ
segments.transliteration: iga’dv … … --nasquu … --elisi sgini tsulisi, squu anehv una nigada, otsehv una asenv, tsuna,tanida, tsigehv nahiyu na tsuna,tana, uniyvsdi anitsutsa, aniyav ahani, nowu’nv, sawu yunigisa, unali --ananigisgv, ahani, Teresita wanilugo udodaquada, ase eladi, ananigisge nowunv, wunilutsa, nowule … -- una doqualela, --vsgi ditlv, edudu, tsigehv nowule --doditinehv ahani, ditlv, dogakahvsgo udodaquada, --udodaquada, --anaisv
segments.translation: Really… My grandmother’s grandkids were all living there. We all lived there. But the bigger boys were in the Big Boy’s place. When one would go home, he would bring a friend with him, they would walk all the way to Teresita. They would walk all day. When they would get there, my grandfather would take them back, this way, in the wagon. He was bringing them back all day. They were going all day.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What were your parents’ names?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏃᏱ .. ᏃᏱ ᏔᎵ ᎠᏃᏎᎲ Williams … --ᎡᏥ Sally
segments.transliteration: noyi .. noyi tali anosehv Williams … --etsi Sally
segments.translation: Noyi. They called my dad Noyi Williams and my mom Sally.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Sel(i) in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Sali?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: No? What was your mom’s name?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎭᏗ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎠᏮᎨᏩ,ᏍᎪ … ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎬ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏃᏱ ᏍᎩᏂ, ᎡᏙᏓ,
segments.transliteration: hadi yawanv,ta, awvgewa,sgo … naniwesgv etsi tsigesv noyi sgini, edoda,
segments.translation: I don’t know, I forget what they called her. But Noyi was my dad.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Oh. And what about you, DJ, what were your parents’ names?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Well, ᎡᏙᏓ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᏂ, ᏦᎳ, ᎾᎮ ᏣᏃᎮᎲ
segments.transliteration: Well, edoda’dv tsigehv tsani, tsola, nahe tsanohehv
segments.translation: Well, they called my dad Tsan(i) Tsol(a).

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Was it Tsola?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏣᏂ, ᏦᎳ, ᏂᏗᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏛ ᏦᎳ ᎠᏚᎳᏗᏍᎬ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ
segments.transliteration: vv tsani, tsola, nidigali,sdodv tsola aduladisgv nigohilv
segments.translation: Yeah, Tsan(i) Tsol(a) because he was always asking for tobacco.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: But they also called him Tsan(i) Wusgaliyvd(a)

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Wusgaliyvd(a)

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᎡᏥ ᏅᏥ, ᏚᏙᎥ … ᏌᏭ ᎣᎦᏝᏫ,ᏍᏛ ᏗᎫᏖᏍᎩ, ᏚᏙᎥ ᏍᏊ ᎥᏍᎩ ᎤᎪᏛ ᏥᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎲ … ᏗᎫᏖᏍᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎭᏢᏭ’Ꮫ ᏱᎪᎲ ᎠᏴ,’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎪᏩ,ᏘᏍᎬ, ᏍᎩᎾ … ᏂᎦᏓ,Ꮽ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏗᎫᏖᏍᎩ, ᎤᎾᎵᎪᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎠᏥᎳ, ᏅᏃᎯ, ᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎮ --ᏗᎫᏖᏍᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ,’ᎢᏅ, ᎨᎲ ᎦᏓ, ᏗᎦᎶᎩᏍᎪ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏭ’Ꮕ ᏄᏍᏙᏭ, ᏗᏩᏛᏒ ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏓ, ᏙᏥᏍᏆᎵ,ᏍᎬ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ,
segments.transliteration: nowu’nv etsi nvtsi, dudov … sawu ogatlawi,sdv digutesgi, dudov squu vsgi ugodv tsisdawadidohv … digutesgi, tsigehv hatlvwu’dv yigohv ayv,’dv squu sgigowa,tisgv, sgina … nigada,wu edoda, digutesgi, unaligohv asenv, atsila, nvnohi, dulvwi,sdanehe --digutesgi, tsigehv edoda,’inv, gehv gada, digalogisgo hena, tsigehv sgiwu’nv nusdowu, diwadvsv ayv, gehv ada, dotsisquali,sgv’le yigi,
segments.translation: And my mom’s name was Nvts(i). One was staying with us, named Digutesg(i), Pickup. That’s who I was with, mostly, Digutesg(i). Wherever you saw him, you also saw me. My dad and Digutesg(i) rode together. Digutesg(i) was working on the railroad and my dad worked as a farmer. That’s how I grew up just cutting wood.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you all help with the farming?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Uh-uh, no.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Was it just for you all? Or was he selling it, too?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Well, ᏱᏚᎶᎦᏅ,’ᏛᎮ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏝᏙ ᏍᏗᏭ, ᏔᎵ, ᏳᏟᎶᏗ, ᏦᎢ, ᏳᏟᎶᏓ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, --ᎠᏫᏒᏍᎬ ᎣᎦᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ;ᏙᏗ ᎠᎴ ᏨᎩᏚᏥ, ᎠᎴ ᎡᏠᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏙᏣᎵ,ᏍᏕᎵᏍᎬ ‘Ꮲ ᏅᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏑᏓᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, … ᏳᏟᎶᏓ, --ᏓᏂᏓᎷᎩᏍᎬ ᎡᏚᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏙᏗ’Ꮕ ᏎᎷ ᎠᏂᏫᏍᎬ ᏏᏆ ᏗᎨᏠ;ᏍᏙᏗ, ᏐᏈᎵ, ᏗᎨᏠ;ᏍᏙᏗ, and ᏥᏔᎦ, ᏗᎨᏠ;ᏍᏙᏗ, ᏍᏊ’ᎢᏅ ᏂᎦᏓ,’Ꮓ ᏙᏣᎵ,ᏍᏕᎵᏍᎬ … ᏧᏂᎵᏏ, ᎠᎴ ᏨᎩᏚᏥ, … ᎣᏣᏓᏅᏅᏍᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ -- --ᏗᎦᏓᎷᎦᏅ ᎨᎲ … laid off them rows. ᏎᎷ ᏙᏥᏫᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏫᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ, ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ roasterneers ᏥᏓᏃᎮᎰ ᏙᏥᎴᏍᎬ field corn. Ꮭ … ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ Ꮎ sweet corn ᎡᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, field corn-ᎢᏭ … ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᏥᏍᏗᎩᏍᎬ ᎦᏚ ᏙᏦᏢᏗᏍᎬ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ and ᏱᏓᎩᏩ,ᏛᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏎᎷ sweet Ꮎ field corn ᎦᏚ ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: Well, yiduloganv,’dvhe edoda, tlado sdiwu, tali, yutlilodi, tsoi, yutliloda,’le yigi, --awisvsgv ogali,sdelv;dodi ale tsvgidutsi, ale etlogi, tsigehv nigada, dotsali,sdelisgv ‘tlv nvgi,sgohi, sudali,sgohi,’le yigi, … yutliloda, --danidalugisgv eduda, tsigehv edodi’nv selu aniwisgv siqua digetlo;sdodi, soquili, digetlo;sdodi, and tsitaga, digetlo;sdodi, squu’inv nigada,’no dotsali,sdelisgv … tsunilisi, ale tsvgidutsi, … otsadanvnvsgv tsigehv -- --digadaluganv gehv … laid off them rows. selu dotsiwisgv nowu’nv osda, winuli,stanv, sgina na roasterneers tsidanoheho dotsilesgv field corn. tla … aqua,dvganv yigehe na sweet corn ehe nahiyu ayv, hena, field corn-iwu … sgina dotsisdigisgv gadu dotsotlvdisgv squu sgina and yidagiwa,dvdi, sgina selu sweet na field corn gadu degotlvsgo squu
segments.translation: Well, when my dad worked a field, he didn’t do it small. He would plant about two or three acres for our own use. My uncles and my aunt, all of us would be helping. They were plowing 40 or 60 (yu-tli-lo-da) my late grandpa and my dad. They were planting corn to feed hogs, horses, and chickens. Then we would all help. Their grandkids, my nephews, and we would all line up for them to plow. Lay out those rows. We were planting corn. When they were ready, “The Roasterneers” they call it. We were picking field corn. I hadn’t heard that there was sweet corn, it was just field corn. That’s what we were eating, also, we made cornbread with them. When I find some, the field sweet corn, I make bread with them too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do you grind it yourself?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: ...butter…

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: ...it’s like a mailbox with holes in them.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Oh, I know it, I’ve seen it.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎾᏃ ᏧᎦᎶᎦ, Ꮎ ᏎᎷ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎠᎹ, ᎠᏓᏟᏍᏛ
segments.transliteration: nano tsugaloga, na selu nowule ama, adatlisdv
segments.translation: And the corn shucks, then there’s water in them.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: Ꮟ’Ꮫ ᎤᏩᏯ ᏍᎩ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, Ꮎ … ᏎᎷ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏗᎬᏁᏗ ᎩᎶ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ Ꮎ … ᎢᎸᏍᎪ ᏄᏒ ᎤᏲᎱᏒ DJ ᎠᏥᏕᎳᎥᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ --ᎠᏍᏙᏍᎬ, --ᎠᏍᏙᏍᎪ ᎬᏗ, ᎦᏙ’Ꮫ ᏴᏓ,? … Ꮎ ᏎᎷ ᏳᏓᎭ Ꮟ ᏍᎩ ᎾᏛᏁᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ Ꮟ
segments.transliteration: si’dv uwaya sgi iyusdi, na … selu osda, digvnedi gilo agayvlige na … ilvsgo nusv uyohusv DJ atsidelavsgv, tsigehv --asdosgv, --asdosgo gvdi, gado’dv yvda,? … na selu yudaha si sgi nadvneho yudaha si
segments.translation: He’s still got one of those, that fixes cornmeal. There was an old lady, she passed away not long ago, and she gave it to DJ. He mashes the corn with it. What do you say? He still does that sometimes.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎦᏙ’Ꮫ ᏴᏓ, Ꮎ Ꮭ’ᎮᎾ ᎠᏍᏛᎪᏒ ᏱᎩ,
segments.transliteration: gado’dv yvda, na tla’hena asdvgosv yigi,
segments.translation: How would you say that? Cause it’s not grinding, is it?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎠᏍᏛᎪᏒ ᏱᎩ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎪᎸᏍᎪ ᎠᏴ … ᏃᏭ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏩᏂ,Ꮜ, ᎪᎢ,’Ꮫ ᎦᏚ ᎠᎹ,’ᎢᏅ
segments.transliteration: hesdi, asdvgosv yigi, sgina golvsgo ayv … nowu sgina yuwani,sa, goi,’dv gadu ama,’inv
segments.translation: It’s not asdvgosv. I make that. When it gets done, I put grease and salt on top of it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Next time we meet, bring that!
[laughter]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Yeah --ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ,’Ꮫ ᎤᏠᏱ ᎮᎾ, ᏂᎬᏁᎰ ᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: Yeah --agi,sdayvhvsgi,’dv utloyi hena, nigvneho gotlvsgo squu sgina
segments.translation: Yeah, my wife makes it the same way too.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎩᎳᏭᏍᎩᏂ --ᏱᏚᎾ,ᏦᏍᏙᏒ, ᏍᎩᎾ icebox-Ꭲ ᏗᎦᏢᏗ, … ᏍᎩ ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ freezer-Ꭲ ᏓᎩᏢᏅ … Ꮟ ᎠᎩᎭ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏛᎪᏒ bag-Ꭲ ᎠᎩᏝ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎣᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ, “ᏓᎦᏁᎵ,ᏔᏂ,” ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᏳᏓᎵᎭ ᎥᏍᎩᏭ’Ꮕ … ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏗᏩᏛᏒ, Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎣᎩᎭ, ᏱᎩᎮ just ᎦᏙ’Ꮫ ᏴᏓ, just the essential things. … ᏔᎵ, ᏗᎦᏂᏟ, ᏕᎦᏂᏢ ᏕᎧᏅᏑᎸ ᎾᏅᏅ ᏗᏤᏍᏙ ᏧᎩᏓᏟ,…
segments.transliteration: gilawusgini --yiduna,tsosdosv, sgina icebox-i digatlvdi, … sgi nawali,sdanelv freezer-i dagitlvnv … si agiha, agi,sdvgosv bag-i agitla, tla yawanv,ta, osdi yigi, “daganeli,tani,” gelisgo yudaliha vsgiwu’nv … ayv’dv diwadvsv, tla gohusdi, ogiha, yigihe just gado’dv yvda, just the essential things. … tali, diganitli, deganitlv dekanvsulv nanvnv ditsesdo tsugidatli,…
segments.translation: It can get spoiled right away, when you put them in the ice box. That’s what happened to me, so I put them in the freezer. I still have some that I grinded up, in a baggie. I don’t know if it’s still good. “I should try it,” I think sometimes. … As I was growing up, we didn’t have store-bought things. We just had… how would you say it? The essential things. We had two beds in the rooms. Our mattresses…

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: …stuffed…[made with]

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Yeah… --ᏚᎾ,ᏓᏱᏏᏙᎲ ᏙᎩᎦᏴᎵᎨ Ꮭ’ᎮᎾ, ᏗᎦᎭᎴᎲᎦ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᏱᏣᏂ,ᏏᏅ, ᎩᎶ ᏱᎳᏍᏛᎥᎦ,’Ꭱ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎣᎩᏥ,ᏈᏍᏛ Ꮎ ᎮᎾ, ᎡᏚᏥ, … ᎤᏪᏥ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎦᎷᎬ ᎣᎦᏝᏫ,ᏍᏗᏍᎬ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, … ᎩᏄᏗᏭ ᏍᏗ ᎤᎶᏒᏍᏗ, ᎠᏂᏁᎸ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎦᎷᎬ ᏦᎢ’Ꮫ ᏱᏧᏒᎯᏓ, ᏃᏭ --ᎠᏥᏯᏅᎯᎰᎢᎰ ᎠᏥᎸᏂᎰ’Ꮫ --ᎠᎦᏘᎾᏫᏗᏍᎬ … ᏔᎵ, ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏧᏪᏅᎲ ᎢᎦᏅᎪᏨ ᏃᏭ ᏦᎢ ᏧᏒᎯᏓ, ᏃᏭ ᎠᏥᏯᏅᎯᎲ ᏍᎩᏭ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, … --ᎣᎦᎵ,ᏍᎦᏍᏙᏗ’Ꮫ ᎬᏩᏄᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎤᏁᎳᏅ ᎤᏓᏁᏝᏅ ᏌᎶᎵ, ᏥᏍᏚ, ᎬᏟ, ᎣᎦᎾ, ᏙᏥᎯᎲ ᎠᎴ ᎠᏣᏗ, ᏍᎩᏭ’Ꮕ ᏄᏍᏙ ᏗᏆᏛᏒ ᎣᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ … ᏏᏆ’ᎢᏅ, ᏙᏣᏛᎯᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᏱᏙᏥᎸ’ᎮᎾ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏏᏓᏁᎸ’Ꮓ ᏨᎩᏚᏥ, ᎡᏠᎩ’Ꮕ, ‘Ꮲ’ᏛᎮ ᏅᎩᏍᎪᎯ, ᏃᏥᎥ ᏦᎢᎭ’Ꭱ ᏙᏥᎯᎲ … ᏙᏥᏁᎳᏬᏍᎬ … ᏧᎵᎩ,Ꮟ’Ꮓ ᏂᏓᏅᏁᎮ … Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏳᏂ,ᏕᎨ Ꮟ ᎪᎯ, ᏥᎩ, ᏗᎦᎴᏗ ᎢᎦ ᏗᎩᎾᏝ Ꮟ ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ ᏕᎨᏰᏍᎬ ᏗᏣᏯᎥᏍ?
segments.transliteration: Yeah… --duna,dayisidohv dogigayvlige tla’hena, digahalehvga, yigehe yitsani,sinv, gilo yilasdvvga,’e sgina, ogitsi,quisdv na hena, edutsi, … uwetsi, atsutsa, galugv ogatlawi,sdisgv tla yawanv,ta, … ginudiwu sdi ulosvsdi, aninelv asenv, galugv tsoi’dv yitsusvhida, nowu --atsiyanvhihoiho atsilvniho’dv --agatinawidisgv … tali, yuwaga,da, tsuwenvhv iganvgotsv nowu tsoi tsusvhida, nowu atsiyanvhihv sgiwu nusdv ayv, hena, … --ogali,sgasdodi’dv gvwanunv,ta, unelanv udanetlanv saloli, tsisdu, gvtli, ogana, dotsihihv ale atsadi, sgiwu’nv nusdo diquadvsv otsali,sdayvhvsgv … siqua’inv, dotsadvhisdisgv yidotsilv’hena, nigada, sidanelv’no tsvgidutsi, etlogi’nv, ‘tlv’dvhe nvgisgohi, notsiv tsoiha’e dotsihihv … dotsinelawosgv … tsuligi,si’no nidanvnehe … tla gohusdi, yuni,dege si gohi, tsigi, digaledi iga diginatla si ayv, gehv degeyesgv ditsayavs?
segments.translation: Yeah. Our parents were throwing them around; you couldn’t get up after you laid down or you would step on somebody. There were so many of us. My uncle, his son came and we took him in. They lived a little over a quarter of a mile away, but he still came. He stayed for three days, then he came after him. He was whooping him while he took him away. He would come again for about three days, then they would come get him. That’s how it was. We were depending on the Lord and His blessings. We hunted squirrels, rabbits, raccoons, groundhogs, and fish. That’s how it was when we grew up, that’s what we ate. We raised hogs. We’d kill them and the whole family––my uncles, my aunts, here were about 40 of us––we’d kill three hogs and we’d skin them. They’d fix the guts. They didn’t throw anything away. Still, today, the hog ears I like to eat. Have you eaten them?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Huh uh, Ꮭ’Ᏺ -- ᎾᎮᎾ, ᏧᎵᎩ,Ꮟ,’Ᏺ ᏗᎩᏯᎥ, ᏍᏓᏱ ᏗᎬᏂᏍᏔᏅ,
segments.transliteration: Huh uh, tla’yo -- nahena, tsuligi,si,’yo digiyav, sdayi digvnistanv,
segments.translation: No, I haven’t. But I’ve eaten the guts. If they’re cooked real hard.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ, ᏗᎦᎴᏂ, ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏗᎦᏰᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: nahena, digaleni, iga hena, osda, digayesdi,
segments.translation: The ears, though, they’re really good to eat.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏓ, Ꮎ ᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᎤᏂᏓᏛᏅ ᏙᎲ? ᏣᏂᏰᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: igada, na squu na unidadvnv dohv? tsaniyesgo tsigehv
segments.translation: And some would eat the tails, too, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Yeah, some. It was funny.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏝᏗ’Ꭷ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏳᏂᏕᎨ --ᏯᏂ,ᏗᏅᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᏓ, --ᎠᏅᏂᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎾᏅᏁᎰ
segments.transliteration: tladi’ka gohusdi, yunidege --yani,dinvsdi nigada, --anvnisdisgv gohusdi,’le yigi, nanvneho
segments.translation: They didn’t throw anything away. They fixed it all up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you grow up the same way?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎨᏒ … ᎠᎹᏱ ᎣᏤᏙᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ --ᎠᎹᏱ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ … ᎾᎮᎾ, … ᎦᏙ’Ꮫ ᏱᎪᏌ, Spring Creek ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎮᎾ, ᎾᏂᏪᏎᎰ Spring Creek ᎠᏮᎨᏩ,Ꮢ anyway, ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᎾᎥ ᎣᏤᎲ Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᎦᏙᎯ, ᎣᎩᎲ Ꮎ ᏓᏐᏍᎬ ᎤᎾ … ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ … ᏃᏭ … ᏙᏓᏫᏕᎾ, ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ ᎤᎾ ᎣᏤᎪ ᏬᎩᏒᎯᎰ ᎠᎹᏱ, ᎠᎹᏳᎵ,Ꮧ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᎣᎩᎪᏓ, ᎨᎲ --ᏬᏤᏙᎲ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏦᎬᏂ,Ꮧ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎣᏤᏙᎲ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᎢᎦᏓ, ᎠᎾ,ᏑᏂᏙᎲ, ᎠᎴ --ᏗᏂᏘᏍᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁᎰ --ᎤᎵ,ᏨᏓᏩᏓ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏑᎾᎴ ᏗᏢ, ᏗᎥᎾᎢ,--ᏗᎥᎾᎢ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎬᏂ, ᎨᏒ --ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏛᎾᎢᏒ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏱᏚᏂᏃᏝ, ᎠᏣᏗ, ᏥᏍᏛᎾ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏂ,ᏙᏨᏁᎲ --ᏃᏭᎴ ᎣᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᏚᏯ’Ꮕ, ᎩᎶ ᏧᏮᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᏓᏲᎯᎰ ᏍᎩᏛ ᎥᏍᎩᏭ’Ꮫ --ᎠᏩᏛᏒ ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎢᎦ ᏲᏣᏛᏁᎲ, “ᎤᏓᏈᏍᏗ,” ᎠᏪᎵᏒ’Ꮓ … ᎠᏩᏛᏐᏅ “Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᏂᏓᎦᏛᏁᎵ” ᎠᏪᎵᏒ Chad-ᎢᏅ,--Chad-ᎢᏅ ᏃᏭ Ꮲ ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏁ ᏃᏭ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎣᎩᏁ ᎣᎩᎾ,ᏤᎵ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎹᏱ, ᏲᏤᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv gesv … amayi otsedohv tsigehv --amayi, nigohilv … nahena, … gado’dv yigosa, Spring Creek tsalagi, hena, naniweseho Spring Creek awvgewa,sv anyway, una’dv nav otsehv na squu gadohi, ogihv na dasosgv una … una’dv … nowu … dodawidena, yinuli,stana, nowu’dv una otsego wogisvhiho amayi, amayuli,di, nigada, iga hena, ogigoda, gehv --wotsedohv gohu,sdi, tsogvni,di, nigada, otsedohv nowu’nv, igada, ana,sunidohv, ale --dinitisgi, tsigehv vsgi’dv nana,dvneho --uli,tsvdawada, nowu’nv, sunale ditlv, divnai,--divnai, nowule gvni, gesv --aniwonisgv dvnaisv nowu’nv, yiduninotla, atsadi, tsisdvna,’le yigi, una’dv osda, yini,dotsvnehv --nowule otsali,sdayvhvsgo duya’nv, gilo tsuwvnistanv dayohiho sgidv vsgiwu’dv --awadvsv sgi’dv iga yotsadvnehv, “udaquisdi,” awelisv’no … awadvsonv “tla ilvhiyu yinidagadvneli” awelisv Chad-inv,--Chad-inv nowu tlv tsinuli,stane nowu atsutsa, ogine ogina,tseli tla squu amayi, yotsedohv
segments.translation: When I was growing up, we were always at the water. How do you say, Spring Creek? I know they call it something in Cherokee, I forgot. Anyway, we lived nearby there. We had land and the water went through it. When it was Saturday, we went there and spent the night by the water. There were a lot of us kinfolk all over there. Some of them fished and others were gigging all through the night. Then in the morning, they’d come back. You could just hear them talking as they walked back. If they brought back any fish or crawdads, we’d fix them right there by the water. Then we’d eat. Somebody brought beans they’d cooked before. That’s how I grew up, that’s all we did. It’s bothersome, I think now. But I’m grown, I think I’m not ever going to do that again. [laughs] When Chad was born, our son, we still didn’t go to the water.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You all didn’t have hogs?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏏᏆ, … ᎥᎥ ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮭ ᏯᏆᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ ᏓᏂᎯᎮ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᏂ, Kenwood ᏦᏤᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎮᎾ, “C.C. Camp” ᎠᏃᏎᎲ ᎪᎯᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᏍᎩ’Ꮫ … --ᎠᏎ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏯᎾᏈᏴᏍᎬ, ᎤᎾ ᎣᏤᎲ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᏂ, ᏩᎧ, ᏥᏓᏥᎧᏁᎸ Daddy ᎾᎯᏳ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏫᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎾᎯᏳ --ᏗᏲᎦᏂᎩᏌ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ Ꮎ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎦᎾᏝ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, -ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎮᎾ, ᏃᏍᏕᎲ Sequoyah, ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ Teresita ᏧᏂᎷᏣ, ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᏦᏍᏕᎲ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏦᎩᎾᏂᎩᏒ,’Ꮓ ᎤᎾ Teresita ᎣᎩᏂᎷᏨ
segments.transliteration: siqua, … vv asenv, tla yaquanv,ta, ase’dv ase danihihe na sgini, Kenwood tsotsehv una hena, “C.C. Camp” anosehv gohidi, tsigehv vsgi’dv … --ase tla yawanv,ta, yanaquiyvsgv, una otsehv gali,tsode na sgini, waka, tsidatsikanelv Daddy nahiyu nowu’nv, winuli,stanv, tla yawanv,ta, nahiyu --diyoganigisa, tla yawanv,ta, nuli,stanv na gohu,sdi, ganatla tsigeho gayu,la, -gayu,la, ahani, hena, nosdehv Sequoyah, nowu’nv Teresita tsunilutsa, gayu,la, tsosdehv nowu’nv, tsoginanigisv,’no una Teresita oginilutsv
segments.translation: Hogs? Yeah, not really. I don’t remember them killing hogs. When we lived in Kenwood, they called it “C.C. Camp” a long time ago. It was there. I don’t know if they were paying rent living in that house. Daddy was given some cows then. I don’t know what happened to them. That’s when we [my sister] left. I don’t know what happened to my dad’s livestock. We [my sister] were already here at Sequoyah. Then they moved to Teresita. We were already here [Tahlequah] and then we left and came to Teresita.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏗ ᏩᎩᏂᏱ,ᏔᏅ ᎥᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏳᎾ,ᏛᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏏᏆ, ᏗᏂᎯᎲ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏴ’Ꭱ ᏦᎩᎾᏁᎳ,Ꮫ ᏏᏆ ᎮᎾ, ᏕᏥᎾᏝᎥ ᎤᎾ ᏩᎧ, ᏍᏊ ᏕᏥᎾᏝᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ --ᎣᏍᏓᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ;ᏗᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ᎠᎩ,ᏠᏯᏍᏔᏅ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏙᏳ, Ꮎ ᎠᎩᏫᏒᏗ,’Ꭱ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ’Ᏼ ᏥᏌᎹᏗ, ᏱᎩ, ᎦᏁᎵ,ᏗᎰ Ᏺ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎨᎲ Ᏺ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎡᏲ ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏂᏫᏒᏍᎨ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv, hena, sdi waginiyi,tanv vsgi yusdi, yuna,dvne tsigehv siqua, dinihihv, tsigehv ayv’e tsoginanela,dv siqua hena, detsinatlav una waka, squu detsinatlav sgina --osdali,sdelv;dihv squu sdi’e agi,tloyastanv gehv tla sgina, doyu, na agiwisvdi,’e tla sgi’yv tsisamadi, yigi, ganeli,diho yo sgina, gehv yo sgina, eyo iga osda aniwisvsge nahiyu tsigehv
segments.translation: I barely remember them killing hogs. When we got married, I got hogs and cows. That’s what we depended on. I got in on it a little, by owning hogs. I’m not smart enough to plant a garden but I try. Back then, they made really good gardens.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎥᎾ’Ꮫ ᏥᏕᎶ;ᏆᎡᎸ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏏᏆ, ᏗᏛᎯᏍᏙᏗ ᎠᎴ ᏗᎯᏍᏗ … ᏗᎦᏁᎳᏬᏍᏗ .. ᏍᎩᎾ --ᏥᏕᎶ;ᏆᎡᎸ ᏓᎩᏲᎯᏎᎸ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭ ‘to gut it you know’ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏓᎩᏲᎯᏎᎸ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᎠᎴ ᏕᏥᏲᎯᎲ … ᎠᎬᏱ’Ꮫ “Ꭷ ᎯᏲᎢ!” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᎦᎵ,ᏆᏚ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, --ᏥᏲᎸ ᏥᎦᏨᏏᏰᏍᎬ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎤᏪᏡᎪ’Ꮫ “Ᏺ ᏕᏍᎩᏗᏏ!” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᎢᎦ’Ꮫ … ‘Ꮲ’Ꮫ ᏂᎦᏚ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᎨᎮ… ᏥᏍᎦᏰᎮ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ, ᏍᏊ ᏥᏲᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏥᏁᎳᏬᎥ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏱᎨᎵᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᏃᏭ ᏍᎩ “ᎯᏲᎢ!” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ ᏄᏓᎴ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ ᎠᏓᏅ,ᏖᏗ, ᏃᏭ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏁᎸ … ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏍᏊ ᏥᏕᎶ;ᏆᎡᎸ ᎬᏂᏍᏙᏗ ᎭᏫᏯ ᎠᎴ ᎡᏥ’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ “Ꭷ ᎢᏥᏧᏣ” ᎣᎪᎮᎸ “ᎢᏣᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᏗᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴ,ᏗᎢ! … ᏱᏅᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᏱᏙᏣᏓᏩᏔ, ᎾᏂᎦ,ᏔᎲᎾ, ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴ,ᏗᎢ ᎠᏂᎨᏯ ᎠᎴ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏱᏕᏣᏕᏁᎸ -ᏱᏕᏣᏕᏁᎸ ᎡᏍᎦ,’Ꭱ ᏳᏢᏣ, Ꮳ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᎦᎪ’Ꮕ ᏙᏛᎨᏠ;ᏍᏔᏂ,?” (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎯᎢᎾ ᏃᎩᏪᏎᎲ ᎡᏥ “ᏞᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏗᏣ,ᏘᏃᏢ” ᏥᏃᎩᏪᏎᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎪ ᎢᎦ ᎦᏁᎵ,ᏗᏍᎪ ᏄᏍᏙᏭ --ᏗᏩᏛᏒ ᎠᎩᎩᏍᏗ Ꮎ’Ꭱ --ᎠᎹᎨ ᏌᎶᎵ,’Ꮕ, ᎠᏑᏱ ᏥᏕᎶ;ᏆᎡᎸ -ᎦᏥᏕᎶ;ᏆᎡᎸ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᎡᏚᏓ, in November ᎧᎸ ᎤᏕᏘᏱᏍᎬ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏳᏁᎦ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᎡᎵᏏ, … ‘Ꮲ’Ꮫ October ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏔᎾ, “a hungry squirrel!” ᎣᎪᎮᎰ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏥᏧᏣ, “ᎢᏥᏃᎭᎷᎦ!” ᎣᎪᏎᎲ ᎯᏍᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ’Ꮫ ᏑᏓᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏙᏥᎯᎲ ᏌᎶᎵ ᏙᏥᏁᎦᎵᏍᎬ ᎠᎴ ᎡᏚᏓ, ᎦᎾᏬᏍᏗ ᏕᎦᎸᏍᎬ ᏓᎧᏲᏗᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ’ᏅᏃ November ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᏂᎬ’Ꮫ ᏕᎦᏛ ᏌᎶᎵ, ᎧᏅᏑᎸ Ꮎ kitchen-Ꭲ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ November ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏔᎾ, … ᎥᎾ’Ꮫ … cast iron pots ᏅᎩᎭ’Ᏼ ᏚᏃᏛᏅ ᎠᎹ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏟᏍᎪ ᏌᏭ ᎠᎹᎨᎢ ᏚᏅᏂᏍᏗᎲ ᏓᏂᎸᎥᏍᎬ ᎤᏗᏞᎬ, ᎠᎹ, ᎾᏃ --ᎣᏣᏅᎥᏍᎬ’Ꮓ ᎭᏫᏯ Ꮒ,ᏙᏨᏂ,ᏕᏍᎬ ᎪᎶ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏭᏂ,ᏕᎬ ᎠᎹᎨ ᎾᎯᏳ’Ꮫ ᎠᎩᎾᏏᏌᏅ--
segments.transliteration: vna’dv tsidelo;quaelv edoda, siqua, didvhisdodi ale dihisdi … diganelawosdi .. sgina --tsidelo;quaelv dagiyohiselv nigada, gohusdi, nowu ‘to gut it you know’ sgina dagiyohiselv edoda, ale detsiyohihv … agvyi’dv “ka hiyoi!” awohelv edoda, gali,quadu yuwaga,da, --tsiyolv tsigatsvsiyesgv (uyetsi,sgv) uwetlugo’dv “yo desgidisi!” awohelv iga’dv … ‘tlv’dv nigadu yawadetiyvda, nahiyu gehe… tsisgayehe sdigida, squu tsiyosdi asenv, hena, otsinelawov tla gohusdi, yigelisgesdi nowu sgi “hiyoi!” tsawohelv’dv nowu nudale’dv nowu adanv,tedi, nowu gehv aginelv … sgi’dv edoda, squu tsidelo;quaelv gvnisdodi hawiya ale etsi’e tsigehv “ka itsitsutsa” ogohelv “itsadelo;quasgesdi, ditsadasdayv,dii! … yinvgali,sdodi yidotsadawata, naniga,tahvna, una,dasdayv,dii anigeya ale diniyotli, yidetsadenelv -yidetsadenelv esga,’e yutlvtsa, tsa,sdayvhvsgi, gago’nv dodvgetlo;stani,?” (uyetsi,sgv) hiina nogiwesehv etsi “tlesdi, hena, ditsa,tinotlv” tsinogiwesehv tla yawanv,ta, asesgini, doyu,’nv iga hena, galieligo iga ganeli,disgo nusdowu --diwadvsv agigisdi na’e --amage saloli,’nv, asuyi tsidelo;quaelv -gatsidelo;quaelv elisi, eduda, in November kalv udetiyisgv elisi tsigehv tla yunega, gawonisgi, yigehe elisi, … ‘tlv’dv October yinulistana, “a hungry squirrel!” ogoheho’dv tsigehv otsitsutsa, “itsinohaluga!” ogosehv hisgi,sgohi’dv sudali,sgohi,’le yigi, dotsihihv saloli dotsinegalisgv ale eduda, ganawosdi degalvsgv dakayodisgv nowu’nvno November yinuli,stana, nigv’dv degadv saloli, kanvsulv na kitchen-i nowu’nv November yinulistana, … vna’dv … cast iron pots nvgiha’yv dunodvnv ama,’dv atlisgo sawu amagei dunvnisdihv danilvvsgv uditlegv, ama, nano --otsanvvsgv’no hawiya ni,dotsvni,desgv golo sgina wuni,degv amage nahiyu’dv aginasisanv--
segments.translation: I learned a lot from my dad about raising and killing hogs. And skinning them. That’s who I learned from. He turned it all over to me y’know, to gut it. He turned it all over to me. And shooting them. The first time, “Alright, you shoot it!” he told me. I shot it 17 times. [laughs] The hog was still walking around. It was screaming. “Give it [the gun] here!” he told me. I was probably about 14 years old. I was a little scared to shoot it, but I didn’t mind skinning them. But then he told me to shoot it. He gave something to think about. I also learned to fry hog from my dad. And then my late mother, she’d say, “Alright, you boys!” she’d call us. “You all need to be learning to cook! It might happen. You’ll marry one and might not know how to cook. And when you all have children. If your wife is sick, who’s going to feed them?” That’s what our mom would tell us. “Don’t bring them here,” she’d tell us. I don’t know. But I really do appreciate it now. And I try to live the way I grew up. Like, hominy with squirrel meat mixed in. I learned that from my grandparents. My grandmother’s birthday was in November. She didn’t speak English. But when it was October, she would say, “I hungry squirrel!” That’s what she’d tell us boys. “Y’all go hunt it!” We would kill about 50 or 60 squirrels. We would skin them and Grandpa would put them in the stove to dry them. Then in November there’d be squirrels hanging all over the kitchen! Then in November, they’d get those cast-iron pots, about four of them, they’d build a fire, then they had water boiling. They had hominy cooking and they put the squirrels in with it. We’d be sitting there taking the meat off of the bones, then they’d throw it in the hominy. That was when you’d get full.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: I guess they were eating good!

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: That’s when I got really full.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,’Ꭱ ᎢᎸᏍᎩ, ᏄᎲ ᏬᎩᏃᎭᎵᏙᎸ ᏌᎶᎵ, ᏙᏥᏲᎯᎲ Ꮭ ᏱᏙᏥᏩᏛᎮ ᎾᏍᎩᎾ, ᎥᎩᎵᏏ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᏥᏍᏚ ᎤᏢ ᎠᏭ, ᎨᎢ, ᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ Winterhawk Grimmett ᏧᏙᎢᏓ, Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎤᏁᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏍᏚ ᎠᏍᎪᎵ, ᎤᏂᏴᎲ ᏍᏓᏱ ᎤᏐᎾ,ᏍᏔᏅ gut ᎾᎬᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: ayv,’e ilvsgi, nuhv woginohalidolv saloli, dotsiyohihv tla yidotsiwadvhe nasgina, vgilisi, atsutsa, tsisdu utlv awu, gei, dulvwi,sdanehv Winterhawk Grimmett tsudoida, na’e unesv sgina tsisdu asgoli, uniyvhv sdayi usona,stanv gut nagvnelv
segments.translation: A few nights ago, some of us went hunting for squirrels. We didn’t find any. My grandson killed a rabbit. He works just right over here, his name is Winterhawk Grimmett. He took the rabbit. He grabbed the head real hard and pushed it down and gutted it. Without cutting it, he gutted it. Then with one pull, not even five minutes, he already had it gutted and cut up.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Well, I’ll be!

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᏥᏰᏝᎸᎾ, gut ᎾᎬᏁᎸ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏌᏭ -ᏌᏭ ᏱᎦᏂ,ᏌᏁ ᏃᏭᎴ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏎ 5 minutes ᏱᎨᎮ gut ᏱᎬᏁᎸ ᎠᏥᏁᎦᎸᎲ ᎠᏥᏂᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: natsiyetlalvna, gut nagvnelv nowule sawu -sawu yigani,sane nowule tla squu ase 5 minutes yigehe gut yigvnelv atsinegalvhv atsinidohv
segments.translation: Without cutting it, he gutted it. Then with one pull, not even five minutes, he already had it gutted and cut up.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᎠᏴ, ᏲᏥᏃᎭᎵᏙᎸ ᏲᏥᏢ, ᎨᎲ ᏥᏍᏚ, ᎣᏣᎳᏍᏛᏍᎬ ᎠᏍᎪᎵ, ᎣᏥᏂ,ᏌᏁᏍᎪ -- … ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᏲᎩᏃᎭᎴᎾ, ᎨᎲ Ꮭ’Ꮓ ᎣᎬᏌ, ᏱᎨᎮ ‘Ꮲ ᏦᎦᏚ ᏂᎦᏚ ᏃᏥᎡ ᎣᏣᏓᏅᏅᏍᎬ’Ꮕ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᎩᏟ, ᏓᏂᎨᎯᏙᎲ ᏃᏭ, ᎩᎳᏭ’ᎢᏴ’Ꮫ ᏱᏧᏃᏴᏟ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᎤᏒᏕᎾ, “Ꭷ” ᎣᏣᏗᎲ’Ꮫ -- ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏝᏅᏟ,’Ꭱ --ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏣᎯᎵᏒ ᎤᏅᏪᎥ ᏩᎩᎦ,ᏐᏒ ᎩᏟ ᏓᏳᏂᎨᎲᏍᏔᏅ ᏥᏍᏚ, “ᎭᏢ ᏃᏭ?” ᎠᏪᎵᏒ leather cap-Ꭲ’Ꮕ ᎠᏩᎵ,ᏍᏚᎸ … ᎠᏩᎵ,ᏌᎳ,ᏓᏅ over that bank, ᎠᏗ,ᏟᏒ ᏥᏍᏚ ᎤᏒᏕᏂ, ᏚᏃᏴᏒ *garble* ᎤᏛᏅ … bb’s-‘Ꮫ ᏕᎦᏯᎸ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) -- ᎥᎾ’Ꮫ ᎭᎴ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᎪᏒ ᎤᏢᏫ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏎᎦᏨ ᎧᏬᎵ,ᏕᏍᎬ “You’re alright, you’re alright, you’re alright,” ᎠᏬᎮᎲ’Ꮫ … ᎢᎦ’Ꮫ ᏥᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎾᎨᎢ ᎡᎯ, --ᎣᏥᎩᏍᎨ Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏕᎳ, ᏲᎩᏞ ᎣᎩᎷᎯᏍᏗ ᏏᏆ, ᎮᎾ, ᏕᎦᏛᎯᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᎤᎾ ᏙᏳ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ, -- Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏱᏙᏥᎯᎮ ᏔᎵᏥ,ᏍᏊ ᎯᏍᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏳᏓᎨᏓ, ᏅᎩᏥ,ᏍᏊ’Ꮫ ᏅᎩᏥ,ᏍᏊ ᎯᏍᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏳᏓᎨᏓ, Ꮎ’Ꮫ … ᎤᎵ,ᏦᎯᏓ, ᎠᎢ ᏄᎭᎬ
segments.transliteration: na’dv ayv, yotsinohalidolv yotsitlv, gehv tsisdu, otsalasdvsgv asgoli, otsini,sanesgo -- … iga hena, yoginohalena, gehv tla’no ogvsa, yigehe ‘tlv tsogadu nigadu notsie otsadanvnvsgv’nv nowu’nv gitli, danigehidohv nowu, gilawu’iyv’dv yitsunoyvtli,stana, usvdena, “ka” otsadihv’dv -- tsosdadatlanvtli,’e --tsigehv otsahilisv unvwev wagiga,sosv gitli dayunigehvstanv tsisdu, “hatlv nowu?” awelisv leather cap-i’nv awali,sdulv … awali,sala,danv over that bank, adi,tlisv tsisdu usvdeni, dunoyvsv *garble* udvnv … bb’s-‘dv degayalv (uyetsi,sgv) -- vna’dv hale agi,sgosv utlvwi,stanv segatsv kawoli,desgv “You’re alright, you’re alright, you’re alright,” awohehv’dv … iga’dv tsisgasdanelv ayv’dv agi,sgasdanelv sgi hena, inagei ehi, --otsigisge tla hena, adela, yogitle ogiluhisdi siqua, hena, degadvhisdisgv una doyu tsuna,tana, -- tla hena, yidotsihihe talitsi,squu hisgi,sgohi, yudageda, nvgitsi,squu’dv nvgitsi,squu hisgi,sgohi, yudageda, na’dv … uli,tsohida, ai nuhagv
segments.translation: When we would go hunt and would kill a rabbit, we would step on its head and we’d pull it. Skinning it. When we went hunting, it wasn’t just us, there were about 13 or 14 of us. We’d be in a line. Then the dogs would be chasing. Then when somebody would shoot their shotgun, we would say, “Ka!” My late brother, the .44 he was going with was too heavy. I went down the hill. The dogs chased a rabbit. “Where’d it go?” I thought. I was wearing a leather cap. When I raised up over the bank, the rabbit ran by and I heard the gun go off. [garble] it said. There were bb’s stuck in it. I almost dug a hole. My brother ran to me and was barely breathing. “You’re alright, you’re alright, you’re alright,” he was saying to me. I really scared him. It also scared me. We just ate things from the woods, we didn’t have any money to get to town. I raised hogs, they were really big, but we didn’t kill them. The fat weighed 250lbs or 400lbs, 450lbs. It was this [gestures] thick.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: You all were making lard.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎪᎢ -ᎪᎢ’Ꮫ ᎠᏃᏢᏗᏍᎨ ᎾᏅ Ꮎ … cracklings-Ꮫ ᎣᏣᏛᏅᎥᏍᎪ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ Briggs-Ꭲ ᏱᏬᎨᎾ, biscuits and cracklings … ᎭᏫᏯ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏱᏬᎩᎲ, ᏍᏊ --ᎣᏥᏫᏗᏍᎬ ᎾᏅ ᎠᏂᏳᏁᎦ, ᎠᏂᏲᎯᎰ’Ꮫ bologna sandwich white bread “Ooh ᎢᎦ ᏙᏳ ᎤᏖᏗ, ᎡᎵᏍᏗ, ᎠᎩᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ” ᎠᎢ ᏬᏣᏗᏍᎦᏢᏍᎪ ‘ᎸᏢ biscuits ᏄᎦᎾᏬᏒᎾ ᏱᏙᏥᏰᏍᎪ … ᏱᏬᎦᎵ,ᏒᎾ, ᏁᎳᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎭᏫᏯ … biscuit-Ꮫ ᎪᎢ’Ꮫ ᎣᏥᏅᎵᏰᏍᎬ ᎠᎴ ᏗᏆᏲᏗ, ᎠᎹ’Ꮕ ᏍᎩᏭ’Ꮕ ᎣᏥᎩᏍᎬ ᎢᎦ, ᏱᎩ, ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, … … ᎣᎩᏁᏥ,’Ꭱ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏕᎸᎲ ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏂ ᏔᎵ, ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮫ ᏦᎢ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏙᏍᏗᏢᎢ ᏏᏆ ᎡᏙᏗ ᏚᎾᏝᎥ “Ꭷ --“ -ᏌᏭ ᏙᏥᏢ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᎦᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸᎮ ᎡᏙᏓ, … ᎠᏴ ᎣᎩᏁᏥ, ᎠᏧᏣ, … Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎩᎯ,ᏐᏓᏁᎰ ᏍᎩ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ,
segments.transliteration: goi -goi’dv anotlvdisge nanv na … cracklings-dv otsadvnvvsgo’dv tsigehv Briggs-i yiwogena, biscuits and cracklings … hawiya’le yigi, yiwogihv, squu --otsiwidisgv nanv aniyunega, aniyohiho’dv bologna sandwich white bread “Ooh iga doyu utedi, elisdi, agisdi gehv” ai wotsadisgatlvsgo ‘lvtlv biscuits nuganawosvna yidotsiyesgo … yiwogali,svna, nelagi, tsigehv hawiya … biscuit-dv goi’dv otsinvliyesgv ale diquayodi, ama’nv sgiwu’nv otsigisgv iga, yigi, iga hena, … … oginetsi,’e atsutsa, agi,sdelvhv hena, oni tali, yuwaga,dv tsoi’le yigi, yuwaga,da, dosditlvi siqua edodi dunatlav “ka --“ -sawu dotsitlv sgina dogali,sdelvhe edoda, … ayv oginetsi, atsutsa, … tla yawanv,ta, yudelo;quav asesgini, iga hena, agihi,sodaneho sgi yuli,sdodi osda,
segments.translation: They were making lard out of it. And then we made cracklings. We would take the cracklings for lunch at Briggs. We had biscuits and cracklings. If we had meat, we took that too. Then the white people would bring bologna sandwiches with white bread and we’d think, “Ooh! That looks good to eat!” We would go hide and eat our biscuits. We’d eat them without them being warm. If we ran out of meat, then we would put grease, salt, and pepper on our biscuits. That’s what we ate for lunch. Our son, he helped the last few times we killed a hog that my dad had. “Kam! Y’all!” We killed one. We helped my dad, me and our son. I don’t know if he learned it, but… I miss those times.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,’Ꭱ ᎣᏂ Rudy, AR ᏥᏫ,ᏥᏯᎧᏅ ᏥᏛᏴᎨᎸ ᏏᏆ, ᎯᏍᎩᏥ,Ꮚ ᎤᎶᏒᏍᏗ, ᏄᏓᎬ ᎮᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏯᎩᎸᏉ,ᏔᏅ ᎭᏫᏯ --ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, smoked ᎮᎾ, ᏄᏅᏁᎴ “Do you want it smoked?” ᎬᏬᎮᎸ … “ᎭᏩ” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎮᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏯᎩᎸᏉ,ᏔᏅ
segments.transliteration: ayv,’e oni Rudy, AR tsiwi,tsiyakanv tsidvyvgelv siqua, hisgitsi,quu ulosvsdi, nudagv hesdi,’e yagilvquo,tanv hawiya --gohu,sdi, smoked hena, nunvnele “Do you want it smoked?” gvwohelv … “hawa” gatsiyohelv hesdi,’e yagilvquo,tanv
segments.translation: The last time, I went to Rudy, AR where they killed my hog. It weighed over 500lbs. I didn’t like the meat. It was smoked; he smoked it. “Do you want it smoked?” he asked me. “Okay,” I told him. I didn’t like it.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏥᏄᏍᏙ’Ꮽ, ᏏᏆ, ᏣᏂᏬ ᏍᎩᏭ’Ꮫ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏲᏥᏝ,’Ꭱ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏥᎬᎭᎷᏍᎬ Ꮎ’Ꮫ tenderloin … ᎦᎬᎭᎷᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ chunks ᎤᎵ,ᏦᎯᏗ’Ꮕ … --ᎦᎧᎰ’Ꮫ Ꮎ cast iron pot. ᏳᏬᏙᎾ, ᎠᎹ, ᎠᏟᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᎭᏫᏯ ᏭᏕᎪ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ … ᎪᎢ, ᏫᎦᏢᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎢᎾ ᏳᎵ,ᏒᎾ ᎠᎹ, ᏳᎵᏢᎭ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᎬᏂᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᎴᏂᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᎸᎳᏗ,--ᎤᏗᏞᎦ, ᏄᏮᏃ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᎭᏫᏯ ᎠᎬᏍᎬ ᏳᎴᏅᎭ, ᏃᎴ ᎦᎴᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎠᏥᎳ, to slow cook it. ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏳᏩᏂ,Ꮜ, ᏃᏭ ᎡᎵᏏ,--ᎡᏥ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ pan ᎠᎯᎰ ᎠᎫᎩᏍᎬ ᎭᏫ:Ꮒ, ᎪᎢ, brown gravy ᎪᏢᏍᎪ biscuit ᏚᏝ’Ꭳ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv tsinusdo’wu, siqua, tsaniwo sgiwu’dv edoda, hena, yotsitla,’e gehv otsigvhalusgv na’dv tenderloin … gagvhalusgo tsigehv na chunks uli,tsohidi’nv … --gakaho’dv na cast iron pot. yuwodona, ama, atlisgo tsigehv nowu’nv, hawiya wudego nowu’nv … goi, wigatlvsgo tsigehv ina yuli,svna ama, yulitlvha, nowu’dv na gvnisdisgv yusdi, alenisgo tsigehv galvladi,--uditlega, nuwvno nowu’nv hawiya agvsgv yulenvha, nole galesgv na atsila, to slow cook it. sgi’dv yuwani,sa, nowu elisi,--etsi’dv nowu pan ahiho agugisgv hawi:ni, goi, brown gravy gotlvsgo biscuit dutla’o
segments.translation: Me, I just like it the way it was. My dad, when we killed one, we’d cut up the tenderloin. He’d cut it up into chunks and the fat. There was a cast-iron pot there. He’d build a fire and fill the pot with water and throw the meat in it. Then he’d put the lard in there. When the water evaporated then it would start cooking. He would put it high—or make it real hot, the water. When it started cooking then he would take the coals out and it did slow-cooking. When it got done, Mom would go with a pan and dig out grease from way out of the bottom. She would make brown gravy and had biscuits.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏥᎩ, ᏥᏓᎾ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᏧᏂᎲ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ, ᏙᏱ’Ᏼ ᎤᎾ ᏣᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᎢᎦᏓ, ᎤᏠᏱ ᏃᎦᏛᏁᎸ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏴ, ᏙᏳ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, … ᎠᏫ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏯᏩᏅ,ᏓᏗ ,--ᏱᎦᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᎣᎩᏯᎥ
segments.transliteration: doyu’dv tsigi, tsidana,sdayvhvsgo tsunihv adasdayv,di, doyi’yv una tsana,dasdayvhvsgo igada, utloyi nogadvnelv squu ayv, doyu asesgini, … awi gehv tla ilvhiyu yawanv,dadi ,--yiganv,dadisgo ogiyav
segments.translation: They cooked outside. They had a stove to cook on. We did the same thing, but it was a deer, I don’t remember ever eating it.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Me too.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ … ᎠᏣᏗ, ᏃᏭᎴ … ᏥᏍᏛᎾ, … … ᎤᏍᏗᏭ Ꮎ ᎡᎯ, -- ᏌᎶᎵ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᏥᏍᏚ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, --ᎦᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᎪ … ᎣᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: nowule … atsadi, nowule … tsisdvna, … … usdiwu na ehi, -- saloli, nowule tsisdu sgi yusdi, --ganv,dadisgo … otsali,sdayvhvsgv
segments.translation: We had fish and crawdads … then small game; squirrels and rabbits. Things like that, that’s what I remember us eating.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ -ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏥᏧᏣ, ᎡᎵ ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎬᎩᏃᎭᎵᏓᏍᏗ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎰᏩ ᏯᏁᎮ ᎠᏫ,
segments.transliteration: ayv -ayv’dv tsitsutsa, eli iga osda, gvginohalidasdi, yudetiyvda, hesdi, hena, howa yanehe awi,
segments.translation: When I was old enough to hunt, there were hardly any deer here.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Nope.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎢᎦ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᏍᎪ ᎢᎦ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎤᏣᏘᏂ,’Ꮲ ᏗᎦᎶᏍᎬ, ᎦᎷᎬ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎠᏎ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ,
segments.transliteration: iga’dv ase sgina, nigali,sdisgo iga gohu,sdi, utsatini,’tlv digalosgv, galugv, ahani, sgina, ase nuli,stanv,
segments.translation: I guess that’s what happens, something comes from somewhere else. I guess that’s what happened.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Yeah, ᏎᎦᏨ ᎠᎪᏛᏗ ᎨᏒ ᎠᏫ, ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, …
segments.transliteration: Yeah, segatsv agodvdi gesv awi, iga hena, …
segments.translation: Yeah, you rarely saw one then.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Something is about to happen.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It wasn’t until later that the population built up.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ ᎮᎾ, … Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, -- -- ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏍᏕᏙᎲ ᏱᎨᎮ Stilwell Ᏹ-ᏱᏍᏕᏙᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏱᏍᏓᏅ,ᏓᏗ Reed’s Hardware ᏥᎪᏢᏒ
segments.transliteration: ayv hena, … tla yawanv,ta, -- -- sgi iga sdedohv yigehe Stilwell yi-yisdedohv tla yawanv,ta, yisdanv,dadi Reed’s Hardware tsigotlvsv
segments.translation: Well, I don’t know if you all came around Stilwell that much. If you all were there, I don’t know if you all remember Reed’s Hardware that was there?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ Briggs School ᎣᏣᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᎬ Ꮎ ‘Ꮲ October ᎠᎾᎴᏂᏍᎬ ᎨᎵᏍᎩ, ᏓᏂᏂ,ᏕᎬ ‘Ꮩ ᏴᏓ, ᏓᏂᏍᏓᏲᎯᎲᎢ, ᎤᎬᏩᏟ, … ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ ᏭᎷᏨ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏓᏂᏍᏓᏲᎯᎲᎢ, Mrs. Baker ᎮᎾ -- Bill John ᎤᎵᏏ, ᏓᏕᏲᎲᏍᎬ … ᏱᏣᏃᎯᏏ’Ꭱ ᏍᏊ Bill John. … ᎠᎭᏂ,’Ꭱ ᏥᏂ,ᎦᏛ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᎦ, ᏂᎨᎰ Bill John Tim-ᎢᏅ, but anyway, … ᎦᏳᎵ’Ꮕ ᎤᎾᏅ,Ꮫ ᏗᎾ,ᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏧᏂᏩᎯᏎᏗ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᎦᏂ’Ꮫ ᎣᏍᏓᏝᏅᏟ, ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏒᏕᎾ, ᎠᎴ ᏅᎩ, -ᏅᎩᏥ,ᏍᏊ, ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎪᏪᎳ, “ᏕᎯᏔᏲᏢᎢ ᎠᏴ,’Ꮕ, ᏔᎵ ᏦᎢᏁᎢ,” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏃᏍᏓᏛᏁᎮ ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᏙᎩᏩᎯᏎᎲ … Ꮭ ᎠᏎ ᏦᎩᏂᏩᎯᏍᏗ ᏱᎨᏎ no ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, … ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ᎦᏂ, --ᏳᏂᏩᏛᎲ ᎦᏂᏙᎯ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎡᎵ’Ꮫ ᏯᏥᏍᏚᎲᎦ,
segments.transliteration: na’dv Briggs School otsadelo;quasgv na ‘tlv October analenisgv gelisgi, danini,degv ‘do yvda, danisdayohihvi, ugvwatli, … doyu,’nv wulutsv agvyi danisdayohihvi, Mrs. Baker hena -- Bill John ulisi, dadeyohvsgv … yitsanohisi’e squu Bill John. … ahani,’e tsini,gadv gatsiyoliga, nigeho Bill John Tim-inv, but anyway, … gayuli’nv unanv,dv dina,deyohvsgi, yusdi, tsuniwahisedi anitsutsa, gani’dv osdatlanvtli, hena, usvdena, ale nvgi, -nvgitsi,squu, sgohi, gowela, “dehitayotlvi ayv,’nv, tali tsoinei,” udvnv sgi yinosdadvnehe sudetiyvda, sgina tsuna,deloquasdi dogiwahisehv … tla ase tsoginiwahisdi yigese no sudetiyvda, yigohida, … gohi tsigi, gani, --yuniwadvhv ganidohi, atsutsa, eli’dv yatsisduhvga,
segments.translation: We were going to school at Briggs; they started in October. They would sell pies for Christmas. And the first Christmas came, Mrs. Baker, she was teaching. Bill John’s grandmother. He’ll tell you this, too. I’ve known Bill John since he was just so [gestures] tall. Also, Tim. Anyway, the teachers, they already knew what to buy for the boys. Bullets. Shotgun shells .410. “Ask for that! And I’ll ask for the .22!” That was what we were going to get, bullets every year. The school was buying them for us. We didn’t have to buy any for a year. Nowadays, when they find a boy with a bullet, they put him jail.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎢᎾ ᏥᏚᏅᏴ ᎦᎶᏇ Ꮭ ᎠᏴ, ᎡᎵ ᎢᎦ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᎩᏩᎯᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᏅ, “Layaway ᏱᏅᎬ, ᎡᎵᏭ ᏣᏕᏘᏱᏍᎬ ᏣᏈᏴᏗ, ᏱᎩ,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ layaway ᏥᎾᏮᏅ ᏍᏗ ᏥᏝᏁᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏌᏭ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ’Ꮓ ᎩᎳᏫ ᏣᎩᏕᎸ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏃᏭ, 30-30
segments.transliteration: ina tsidunvyv galoque tla ayv, eli iga yawadetiyvda, yigehe agiwahisdi asenv, “Layaway yinvgv, eliwu tsadetiyisgv tsaquiyvdi, yigi,” tsawohelv sgi tsinawadvnelv layaway tsinawvnv sdi tsitlanego tsigehv nowu tali,sgohi, sawu yudetiyvda, tsigehv tsinawali,stanv’no gilawi tsagidelv nahiyu nowu, 30-30
segments.translation: They had guns there. I wasn’t old enough to buy one. “You could put it on layaway and have it out by your birthday,” he [the storekeep] told me. And that’s what I did. I had it on layaway and I was paying just a little bit at a time. When I turned 21, that’s when he gave me the gun. 30-30.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,’Ꮫ ᏗᏩᏛᏒᏗᏒ -ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᏒ Ꮶ’ᎩᏚ ᎮᎾ, ᏌᏚ’Ꮫ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᏧᏂᎩᏎ ᎡᏥ ‘Ᏺ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎣᎩᎨᏳᏗᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᎶᏇ ᎣᎩᏂᏓᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ’Ꮕ, -ᎠᎬᏱ ᎠᏁᎯ, ᎭᏰᎵ,ᏍᏗᏭ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ --ᎣᎩᎨᏳᏗᏍᎬ, ᎨᎲ ᎣᎩᏂᏓᏍᏗ … ᏲᎨᎾ, ᎣᎦᎶᏍᎩᏗ, ᎠᎬᏱ’Ꭱ ‘Ᏺ single-shot ᏌᏭ ᎦᎳᏗᏍᎩ ᏔᎵ ᏦᎢᏁᎢ, … ᏲᎨᎾ, ᎣᎩᏃᏍᎩᏗ, ᎣᏥᏁᎬ … ᏲᎦᏕᎳᎯᏎᎸ ᏃᏭ ‘ᏍᎦᏍᏗ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ … Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏌᏭ Ꮎ ᏥᏯᏛᏛᏅ ᎢᎸᏍᎩ, ᏄᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ “Ꮭ ᎠᎩᏃᎮᏗ” ᏱᎬᏬᎮᎸ ‘Ᏺ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏗᎨᏍᏗᎦᏴᎵ, ᏂᎯ?
segments.transliteration: ayv,’dv diwadvsvdisv -etsi tsigesv tso’gidu hena, sadu’dv yudetiyvda, gehv gayu,la, tsunigise etsi ‘yo sgina, ogigeyudisgv, tsigehv galoque oginidasdi anitsutsa’nv, -agvyi anehi, hayeli,sdiwu, tsigehv squu --ogigeyudisgv, gehv oginidasdi … yogena, ogalosgidi, agvyi’e ‘yo single-shot sawu galadisgi tali tsoinei, … yogena, oginosgidi, otsinegv … yogadelahiselv nowu ‘sgasdi’dv tsigehv … tla yawanv,ta, sawu na tsiyadvdvnv ilvsgi, nuhv tsigehv “tla aginohedi” yigvwohelv ‘yo ‘do usdi digesdigayvli, nihi?
segments.translation: Me, when I was growing up, my mom, she was 13 or 11 years old when she left. They didn’t let us have a gun, but the older ones had one. They didn’t even let us handle a knife. When we went, we had to steal one to take with us. At first, we had a single-shot .22 But when they found out… [laughs] I don’t know, I asked someone a few days ago. He said not to talk about it. What are y’alls clans?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Right now… I think I’m Long Hair.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Long Hair.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Long Hair.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮕ, … ᏥᎬᏃᏎᎲ … ᏧᏟ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ Is that one of them?
segments.transliteration: ayv’nv, … tsigvnosehv … tsutli’dv ase Is that one of them?
segments.translation: And me, what I was telling you… Is Fox one of them?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Huh uh. Maybe Wolf?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Wolf! Yeah, wolf.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: That’s why you’re not afraid, ‘cause you’re mean.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Yeah, I think it’s “galilo”, “anigalilo”

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Do you mean, “anigiloh(i)?”

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Anigiloh(i), yeah. Really…

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎡᏚᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎦᏪᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᏒ … ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏤᎵ Ꮎ … Ꮎ ᎪᏪᎳ, ᎡᏚᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ … ᏚᏙᎥ ᎪᏪᎳ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, … Daddy ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎩᏍᏔᏅ Ꮎ ᏗᏎᏍᏗ, ᎡᏚᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏤᎵ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, Ꮭ ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏱᎨᎲ 1907’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏧᏕᏅ Daddy. ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᏧᏂᏍᏚᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: eduda, tsigehv sgi yigawesdi, tsigesv … sgi hena, utseli na … na gowela, eduda, tsigehv … dudov gowela, nowu’nv, … Daddy tsigehv squu ugistanv na disesdi, eduda, tsigehv utseli sgi yusdi, tla uwasa, yigehv 1907’dv tsigesv tsudenv Daddy. gayu,la, tsunisdunv tsigehv
segments.translation: My grandpa used to say that. It was my grandpa’s, his name was written on the paper, my grandpa. And my dad took it over his [roll number?] He didn’t buy it. My dad was born in 1907. They had already closed it [the rolls.]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏗᎨᏍᏗᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎤᎾ’ᏭᏍ ᎤᎾ DJ, ᎤᎾ’ᏭᏍ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾ,ᏕᏅ ᎨᎲ?
segments.transliteration: digesdigayvlige una’wus una DJ, una’wus squu una,denv gehv?
segments.translation: Your parents, is that where they were born, too?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Well, yeah, – ᎡᏥ’Ꭱ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎡᏙᏓ,’Ꮕ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ Chewey-Ꮫ ᎤᎾ ᎢᏲ ᏧᎨᏓᎵᏴ - Pumpkin Hollow ᎢᎾ ᏧᏕᏅ ᎢᎾ ᎦᏙᎯ, ᏧᏂᎲ ᎠᎾᏝᏅᏢ ᎠᎴ ᎤᏙ ᏍᎪᎯᏥ,Ꮚ ᏑᏓᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏳᏟᎶᏓ, Bonner—Bonner Ranch ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏦᎢᏥ,ᏍᏊ ᎠᏕᎵ ᎨᎦᏈᏴᎡᎸ … Ꮟ ᏳᎮ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᎤᎾ ᏯᏩᏁᏍᎨᎮᏞ … ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ,
segments.transliteration: Well, yeah, – etsi’e gehv una edoda,’nv, sgina, sgi’e tsigehv Chewey-dv una iyo tsugedaliyv - Pumpkin Hollow ina tsudenv ina gadohi, tsunihv anatlanvtlv ale udo sgohitsi,quu sudali,sgohi, yutliloda, Bonner—Bonner Ranch tsigehv nahiyu sgina tsoitsi,squu adeli gegaquiyvelv … si yuhe edoda, una yawanesgehetle … asesgini,
segments.translation: Well, yeah, that’s where my mom was born. Dad, he was born in Chewey at iyo tsukedaliyv, Pumpkin Hollow. That’s where he was born. They had land there. His brother and sister, 160 acres. It used to be Bonner Ranch, they got paid $300 for it. If he still had that land, that’s where I was going to build my house. But…

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Back then, $300 was a lot of money.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎤᏃᏍᏓ’Ꮽ, ᎤᎪᏛ ᎨᎲ … ᎯᏍᎩ, ᎢᏯᏓᏅ,Ꮫ Ꮎ Baby Ruth candy bars ᎯᏍᎩ, ᎢᏯᏓᏅ,Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ *ᎯᎢ’Ꮫ* ᏥᎦᏅᎯᏒ ᏥᏂ,ᎦᏛ … ᏦᏣᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᎬ ᎮᎾ, Briggs-Ꭲ ᏦᎦᏂᎩᏓ, ᎣᏥᏧᏣ, … ᎣᏥᏟᏏᏍᎬ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᎯᏍᎩ, ᎢᏯᏓᏅ,Ꮧ, ᎾᏅ donut shop ᎪᏢᏒ ᎢᎾ … on the north end of town…
segments.transliteration: unosda’wu, ugodv gehv … hisgi, iyadanv,dv na Baby Ruth candy bars hisgi, iyadanv,dv tsigehv *hii’dv* tsiganvhisv tsini,gadv … tsotsadelo;quasgv hena, Briggs-i tsoganigida, otsitsutsa, … otsitlisisgv adela, hisgi, iyadanv,di, nanv donut shop gotlvsv ina … on the north end of town…
segments.translation: Even a dollar was a lot. Baby Ruth candy bars were five cents. They were this [gestures] long and this [gestures] big. We were learning at Briggs school, us boys, when we’d leave, we were gather up at least five cents. There was a doughnut shop on the north side of town…

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: …In Tahlequah…

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏓᎵᏆ, ᎠᎭᏂ, high school ᏕᎦᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᎬ … ᏦᎢ’Ꮫ ‘Ᏺ donuts ᎯᏍᎩ ᎢᏯᏓᏅ,Ꮧ, ᎨᎲ pepsi-Ꮕ, ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏯᏓᏅ,Ꮧ, ᏦᎢ, ᏲᏥᎠ, ᎣᏥᏟᏏᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎦᏚ ᎢᏯᏓᏅ,ᏖᏗ, ᎣᏥᏟᏏᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ’ᏛᏲ donuts ᏙᎩᏩᏒ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, pop-ᎢᏭ, ᎣᏣᏚᎩᏍᎬ y’know that was our lunch. … ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, … ᎠᎴ ᎦᎳᏍᎦᎵᏍᎬ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ baseball. Number 8 bus-Ꮫ ᎦᏣᎥᏍᎬ from home to high school. ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᏳᏓᎴ ᎦᏳᎳ, ᎤᏢᏍᏔᏁ ᎨᎲ bus. ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ ᎡᎳᏗ, -ᎦᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᎦᎵ,ᏉᎩ, ᏳᏟᎶᏓ, ᏳᏓᎵᎭ Ꮟ ᎾᎩᏅᎪᏨᎾ, ᏓᎵᏆ, ᎩᎶ ᎠᏬᎵ,Ꭼ, ᏥᏯᏣᏁᎲ boy, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎯᎳ ᏍᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, every step of the way, I went home. No ride. ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎩ,’Ꮕ ᏃᏭ but, that was…ᏍᎩ’ᏭᏅ ᏄᏍᏙ’Ꮽ, ᏗᏩᏛᏌ, … ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎪ,Ꮧ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎩᏰᎸᏐ ᏦᎩᎦ,ᏛᎴᏏᏙᎸ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, … ᏗᎦᎳᏫᏥᏙᎯ, ᎨᎲ ᎯᎢᎾ ᎠᏴ,’Ꮕ, Ꮭ … ᎦᏴᎵᏙᎯ ᎨᎲ ᏗᏩᏛᏒ ᎠᎴ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᎡᏥ ᏂᎦᏓ, Chewey ᎦᏘᏲ ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᎣᏣᏓᏟᏏᏍᎬ ᎠᏆᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ ᎠᎩᏴᎵᏓᏍᏗ ᎠᎴ ᏥᎸᏮᏂᏍᎩ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ
segments.transliteration: daliqua, ahani, high school degadelo;quasgv … tsoi’dv ‘yo donuts hisgi iyadanv,di, gehv pepsi-nv, sgohi, yadanv,di, tsoi, yotsia, otsitlisisgv sgigadu iyadanv,tedi, otsitlisisgv sgina’dvyo donuts dogiwasv nowu’nv, pop-iwu, otsadugisgv y’know that was our lunch. … iga hena, … ale galasgalisgv awalenvhv baseball. Number 8 bus-dv gatsavsgv from home to high school. nowu’nv yudale gayula, utlvstane gehv bus. nowu’dv eladi, -ganigisgv gali,quogi, yutliloda, yudaliha si naginvgotsvna, daliqua, gilo awoli,gv, tsiyatsanehv boy, asesgini, hila squu yuwaga,da, every step of the way, I went home. No ride. uli,sigi,’nv nowu but, that was…sgi’wunv nusdo’wu, diwadvsa, … usquanigo,di hena, agiyelvso tsogiga,dvlesidolv asesgini, … digalawitsidohi, gehv hiina ayv,’nv, tla … gayvlidohi gehv diwadvsv ale edoda, etsi nigada, Chewey gatiyo una’dv otsadatlisisgv aquadelo;quav agiyvlidasdi ale tsilvwvnisgi, sgi yuli,sdodi
segments.translation: …Tahlequah. I was learning at high school. Three donuts were five cents. And Pepsi was 10 cents. There was three of us and we gathered up 15 cents to buy donuts. And we were sharing the pop. That was our lunch. Then I started playing baseball. I would ride the #8 bus from home to high school. Sometimes the bus would have already taken off, then I’d have to walk seven miles. Sometimes before I’d got out of Tahlequah, somebody that knew me would pick me up. But, I don’t know how many times I had to walk home every step of the way, no ride, and it would get dark. But that’s how it was when I grew up. It was interesting the way I grew up, but I feel good about it. She was in church, but not me. My dad was a leader (singer) at the Stomp Ground. All of us, Dad, Mom, we all gathered at the Stomp Ground at Chewey. I learned to lead dances and to play the drum.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What is that?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: I was playing (hitting) the drum.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What is that?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᏏᏴᏫ, ᎠᏗᎴᏂᏍᎩ, ᎦᏙᎪ ᎾᏅ ᎠᏂᎨᏯ, Ꮎ ᏓᎦ,Ꮟ, ᎦᏙ ᏴᏓ, ᏣᎳᎩ?
segments.transliteration: na’dv siyvwi, adilenisgi, gadogo nanv anigeya, na daga,si, gado yvda, tsalagi?
segments.translation: It’s the person that leads and then the women wear shackles. How do you say it?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Dinanvsatvsg(i)

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏚᎾᏅᏌᏛ ᏃᏭᏅ *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᎦᏙᎪ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎦᎸᏩᎵᏍᎩ, “Ᏺ..Ᏺ” ᏳᏛᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎦᎸᏩᎵ,ᏗᏍᎬ ᏂᎦᏪᏍᎬ … ᏬᎪᎵ,Ꮸ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᏃᏥᏪᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᎾᎮᎾ, “ᏱᎰᏩ ᏣᎬᏫᏳ” ᎠᏗᏍᎬ, ᎧᏃᎩᏓ, ᎦᎸᏉᏙᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ … to repeat, … ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᎣᏥᏃᎩᏍᎪ ᏳᏓᎵᎭ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎦᏥᏃᏎᎳ, … Woody Hair ᎤᏬᏢ “Ꭷ Ꮎ ᎦᎸᏩᎸ;ᏙᏗ ᎢᏗᏃᎩ!” – “ᎦᏙ ᎤᏍᏗ’Ꭹ?” ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏅ … Woody ᏧᏬᏢ -- grinning away! “ᎯᎦ,ᏔᎭ’Ꮫ ᏥᏂ,ᏥᏪᏍᎬ ᏙᎲ?” ᎤᏛᏅ … ᎦᏥᏃᏎᎴ … ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, … ‘Ꮲ ᏂᎦᏚ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ, … ᎠᏩᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ guitar ᏗᎩᏃᎩᏍᏙᏗ ᏧᎾ,ᏗᏔᏍᏗ’Ꮓ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ Ꭼ,ᏝᏗᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎫᏔᏂ’Ꮕ ᏃᏥᏅ … Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏱᏕᎧᏃᎩᏍᎨ … ᎠᏟᏰᏍᎬ’Ꮽ, Ꭼ,ᏝᏗᏍᎩ,
segments.transliteration: dunanvsadv nowunv *hii* tsigadogo squu sgi’dv galvwalisgi, “yo..yo” yudvna, tsigehv sgi’dv galvwali,disgv nigawesgv … wogoli,tsv’dv squu notsiwesgv sgihena, nahena, “yihowa tsagvwiyu” adisgv, kanogida, galvquododi sgina … to repeat, … sgihena, otsinogisgo yudaliha agvyi gatsinosela, … Woody Hair uwotlv “ka na galvwalv;dodi idinogi!” – “gado usdi’gi?” una,dvnv … Woody tsuwotlv -- grinning away! “higa,taha’dv tsini,tsiwesgv dohv?” udvnv … gatsinosele … iga hena, … ‘tlv nigadu yawadetiyvda, gehv nowu, … awadelo;quav guitar diginogisdodi tsuna,ditasdi’no deganelohvsgv awalenvhv ayv’dv gv,tladisgi tsigehv digutani’nv notsinv … tla gilo yidekanogisge … atliyesgv’wu, gv,tladisgi,
segments.translation: Dunanvsatv, yeah. The one that stands in front and when he says “yo yo!” that’s what galvwal(i)disgv was saying, then the rest of us would repeat it. Then when they say “yihowa tsagvwiyu” the song. It’s also that galvwal(v)dod(i) To repeat. That’s what we used to sing. The first time I told them about it, Woody Hair was sitting there. “Alright, let’s sing galvwal(v)dodi!”, “What is that?!” they said. Woody was sitting there just grinning away. “You know what I’m saying, don’t you?” he said. That’s when I told them. When I was 14 years old, I learned to play the guitar. Then I started playing in bars. It was me and g(v)tladisgi and digutani playing. But nobody was singing. G(v)tladisg(i) was playing the fiddle.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Who is that?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: G(v)tladisg(i) is the late Jim Dick.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And who was the other one?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: DJ Smith … Ꮎ’Ꭱ Jim Dick that’s George Dick’s daddy. No? Right? Yeah. George Dick, ᎯᏲᎵᎦ,’Ꮫ George Dick. ᎤᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: DJ Smith … na’e Jim Dick that’s George Dick’s daddy. No? Right? Yeah. George Dick, hiyoliga,’dv George Dick. udoda, tsigehv sgina
segments.translation: DJ Smith. That Jim Dick, that’s George Dick’s daddy. No? Right? Yeah. George Dick, you know him. That was his dad.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᏅᎲ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᏗᏣᏁᎵ;Ꮧ, ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ ᏦᎯᏳᏅᎢ,
segments.transliteration: nanvhv nowu’nv ditsaneli;di, nowu tsigi, sginana sginohisi nuli,stanidolv tsohiyunvi,
segments.translation: How about now, you’re Christian. Tell me what happened when you joined the church.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Well ᏍᎩᎾ … ᏦᎩᎾ,ᏓᏁᏤᎸ ᎮᎾ, ᏦᎩᎾ,ᏨᏍᏙᏗ … “revival-Ꭲ ᎢᏁᎾ” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ Ꮎ … ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏬᏍᎩ, ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏟᏐᏗ … ᏃᏭᎴ ᏥᏍᏓᏩᏛᏒ ᏅᎩᏁ ᎤᏒ ᎨᎲ … ᏙᏳ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᎮ ᎠᏪᏅᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᏥᏍᏓᏩᏛᏒ … Ꮎ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᎠᎵ,ᏣᏙᎲᏍᎬ Ꮟ … ᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎬ Ꮟ … Ꮎ ᎤᎾᎵ,ᏍᎩᏍᏗ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ Ꮟ ᏥᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎬ ᎤᎬᏫᏳᏒ … ᏍᎩᎾ J.R. Stodsdill … Missionary ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᎤᏔᎾ, ᏗᎦᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎣᏥᏯᎥ ‘Ꮲ ᏑᏓᎵᏍᎪᎯ, ᏳᎳᏏᏗ ᏗᎦᏙᎬ Boy! ᏕᏥᎧᎾ ᎠᏴ,’Ꮕ, ᏕᎩᎧᎾ ᏃᏭ ᎡᎵᏍᏛ ᏑᏓᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏳᎳᏏᏗ, ᏛᎦᏙᎬ … ᏓᎦᎷᏥ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᎠᎴ ᏥᏃᏎᎸ Ꮭ ᏯᏆᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎠᏩᏗᏍᏔᏅ’Ꮫ Boy! … ‘ᏍᎦᏍᏗ’Ꮫ ᎠᎩᏂᏴᏒ Ꮎ ᎦᏍᎩᎶ he put his arm around me. Gah lee! … ᎢᎦ ᎠᎩᎾᎸᏍᏔᏅ … ᎢᎦ’Ꭱ --ᏗᏥᏍᎩᎾᏓ ᏕᏥᎶᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ … … ᎠᏆᏄᎩᏢᏂᏢ … ᏕᏥᎧᎾᏅ Boy, ᎮᎵ ᏕᏥᏍᎩᎾᏓ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, … “Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏛᏅᏍᏔᏃᏅ - I ain’t ready it,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ - “Get outta here!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ … *patting sound* “ᎬᏓᏙᎵᏍᏓᏁᎮᏍᏗ” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᎩᎳ, ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ Ꮎ gospel ᎦᎶᏁᏗ ᏥᏌ ᎤᏲᎱᏒ ᏓᏓᎾᏫ,ᏍᏛ ᎠᏴ, ᎤᎬᏩᏟ, ᎠᎴ ᎤᏲᎱᏒ ᏓᎦᎴᏔᏅ ᎠᏴ, ᎤᎬᏩᏟ, ᎩᎳ, ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ “ᎯᏑᎵ,ᎪᏨ ᏥᎿᏛᏁᎠ” y’know? “Quit doing this, quit doing that,” ᎥᏬᎮᎸ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᎨᏯ, ᎠᏁᎲ ᏧᎾᏁᎵ;Ꮫ’Ꮕ … ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᎩᎾᏂᎩᏒ pickup-Ꭲ ᏬᎩᎾ,ᏣᏅ ᏕᏥᎧᎾᏅ “ᏞᏍᏗ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ: ᏥᏍᎩ,ᏛᏛᏅ ᏗᎩᎳᏫᏥᏓᏍᏗᎢ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎢᎦ ᎠᎩᎾᎸᏦᏅ ᎨᎲ Ꮩ ᏃᏭ ᎢᎣᎩᎾᏂᎩᏒ ᏫᏥᏯᎧᏅ … ᏃᏭᏅ ᏙᎩᎾ,ᏨᏍᏔᏅ September ᎧᎸ … ᏍᎪᎯᏁ’Ꮫ ᎨᎲ … No, ᎦᎵ,ᏆᏚᏏᏁ --ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎦᎵ,ᏉᎩᏁ’Ꮫ ᏫᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, September … ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᎬᏁᎲ Ꮎ pickup ᎭᏫᏂ, ᎠᏩᏛᏄᎵ;Ꮫ ᎭᏫᏂ, … “ᏗᏂᎳᏫᏥ’ᎤᎦ” ᎤᏛᏅ … ᏛᎩᏅᎪᏨ’Ꮫ … ᎡᏧᎳ’ᏛᎭᏛ ᎠᏥᎳᎭ -ᏱᏗᏍᎩᎴᏱ,ᏔᎾ, ᏗᏩᎳᏏᏖᎾ, … “ᏞᏍᏗ ᏥᎬᏃᏎᎴ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏞᏍᏗ, ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᏍᎩ,ᏛᏛᏅᎢ” … “ᎦᏙ ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅᏍᎦ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ -- “ᎠᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗ ᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎯ,” - ᎯᎢ ᎾᎩᏪᏎᎲ “ᎦᏙ ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏓ, ᎠᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗ, ᏚᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎯ,?” ᎠᏩᏛᏅ “What can happen at a prayer meeting?” … Ꮩ’Ꮕ ᏥᏍᏓᏩᏛᏒ Scale Wilson ᏥᎨᎲ --ᏗᎦᏘᏯ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏥᎳ, ᏗᏡ,Ꭺ … ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎠᎵ,ᏣᏙᎲᏍᎬ … Ꮭ ᏱᏥᏯᏛᏓᏍᏓᏁᎮ Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᎤᎾᎵ,ᏍᎩᏍᏗ Ꮟ ᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎬ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᎲ ᎠᏩᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ --ᎠᏆ,ᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ … ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ … ᏃᏭ, … ᎤᎵᏍᏆᏓ, ᏓᏂᏃᎩᏍᎬ --ᎤᎾᎴᏅᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏅᎳᎸᏓᏗᏍᎬ ᎤᏂᎷᎯᏍᏗ … ᏥᏙᎪ’Ꮫ ᎠᎩᏂᏴᏐᏅ ᎩᎳ’ᎢᏴ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ,‘Ᏺ ᎭᏫᏂ,’Ᏼ ᎩᎶ … ᏣᎩᏘᏢ ᏗᎦᏄᎶᏨ -- -- ᏗᎦᏄᎵᏥ, … ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏣᏩᏂᎸ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭ ᏥᏙᎪ’Ꮫ aisle … ᎯᎢ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ “DJ, … go down, or get out,” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ … Boy, ᏕᎩᎧᎾᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏍᏚᏗ ᏕᎦ,ᏙᎥ it wasn’t no further than that door right there. ᏥᏙᎬ ᏃᏭ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ “DJ, go down, or get out.” ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᏓᏭᎪ,ᏔᏂᏙᎸ ᎠᎩᏅᎪᏫ,ᏍᏗ -- ᎠᎩᏄᎸᏅ … ᎠᏩᎳᏍᎬᏌ, Scale-Ꭲ ᎠᏭ ᏗᎦᏙᎬ ᏗᏢ, ᏩᎩᎶᏒ’Ꮫ ᎠᎩᏲᎵᎸ Scale ᏥᎨᎲ -- “ᎦᏙᎯ?” ᎤᏛᏅ “I need Jesus” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᏦᎢ, ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏚᏢᏅ’Ꮫ .. ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᎤᎾᎴᏅᎲ ᎬᎩᏲᎵᎲ ᏓᎾᏠᏱᎲ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᏫᏂ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎴ Hesther ᏥᎨᎲ ᏓᎾ,ᏠᏱᎲ … “ᎦᏙ ᎦᏛᎦ,?” ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᏥᏙᎬ’Ꮽ,Ꮫ ᎬᎩᏲᎵᎲ ᎬᎩᏯᏄᎩᏢᏍᎬ “’Ꮩ ᎦᏛᎦ,?” – “What in the world have I done?” ᎨᎵᎲ’Ꮫ … ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ … ᏯᏩᏗᏛᎲ’Ꭱ ᏑᎾᎴ ᎠᎩᎾᏫᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏉᏟ … my guts, ᎩᎶ just ripping them out ᏥᎨᎲ … ᏍᎩᏅ … ᏄᏍᏛ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᏅᎩᏁ ᎢᎦ, ᎠᏩᏗᏛᎲ I was gonna go to work. ᎪᎱᏍᏗ,’Ꮫ ᏣᎩᏲᎱᏎᎸ’Ꮽ ᎡᎵᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᎩᏲᎲ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮦ ᏳᏍᏗ, --ᎠᎩᏲᎱᏎᎸ ᎠᏎᏗ’Ꮓ ᎧᏫ, ᎠᎩ,Ꮭ’Ꮕ ᎠᎦᎾᏬᎯᏍᏗ ᎠᎹ, ᎠᎩᎸ ᏥᎦᎥᏍᎪ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎧᏫ, … ᎠᎩᎷᏤᎸ … Ꮭ ᏯᏪᏍᏓᏁᎮ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏉᏟ ᎠᎭᏂ, Ꮒ,ᏓᏮᏁᎸ ᏗᏬᏰᏂ, Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎾᏫᏍᎨ … ᎩᎳ,’ᏛᏴ ᎠᎩᎵ,ᏙᎲᏒ ᏅᏩᏙᎯᏯ ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏄᏍᏕᎢ … which was strange to me. ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎪ,Ꮧ, ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎮ … ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸᏒ ᎦᎦᏠᏱᎲ, … ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏛᏳᏓᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ,’Ꭱ Ꮎ ᏙᏓᏫᏕᎾ, ᎤᏒ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, … ᏧᎾᎵ,ᏍᎩᏍᏗ ᏕᎦᏁᎳᏅ ᏩᎩᎷᏨ ᏓᎩᏃᎩᏍᏔᏅ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᏙᏓᏩᏍᎬ ᏫᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᎥᏩᏬᎥ … ᏃᏭ ᎠᏤ’Ꮫ ᏗᎦ,ᏘᏯ, … ᎣᎩᎧᎲ ᎮᎾ, ᏗᎦᏃᏣᎵ,Ꮧ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ --ᎥᎦᏬᎥ … ᏃᏭ ᏍᎩᎾ … ᎥᏩᏬᎣᎾ, … “ᏘᏯᏛᏛᏂᏍ … Andy Ꮟ ᎣᏏ ᏱᎩ, ᏱᏕᎭᏁᎶᎲᏍᎦ, Round-Up Club?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ … “ᎾᏩᏗᏔᎲᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᎣᏏ ᎨᏎᏍᏗ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ … ᏙᏳ’Ꮕ ᎠᏪᏅᏒ … ᏙᏥᏃᎩᏍᏗ’Ꭱ … ᏥᏙᎬ’Ꮫ Boy, ᎠᎩ,ᏏᏛᏂᎸ’Ꮫ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ *smack* ᎠᎩᏥᎸᏅ’Ꮫ … ᎯᎢ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ “DJ, what’re you doing here?” ᎤᏛᏅ .. ᏩᏥ ᎦᏙᎥ ᏐᏁᎳ, ᏦᏍᎪᎯ, ᎨᎲ … Boy, ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᏔᎵ, ᎠᏰᏟ ᏩᏥ ᏳᏪᏅᏓ, phew! ᎤᎵ,ᏨᏓᏩᏓ,’Ꮫ ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᎩᎩᏐᏓᏁᎲ ᎤᎴᏅᎮ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᎩᎩᏐᏓᏁᎸ ᏱᎨᎮ Boy, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎠᎩᎩᏐᏓᏁᎲ’Ꮫ … two and half hours, ᎣᎩᏍᏆᏓ’Ꮫ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏆᎾ,ᎪᏔᏅ guitar – case-Ꭲ ᎠᎩᎳᏛ ᏥᏃᏎᎸ Buddy “ᏥᏑᎵ,ᎪᎢ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎦᏙ ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏂᏙᎭ?” ᎤᏛᏅ … “I shouldn’t be here in the first place,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “I joined church,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ Ꮭ ᏱᏥᎦᏔᎮ Ꮎ ᎥᎩ,ᏍᏕᎸᏗ ᎠᏭᏓᎴᏗ ᏥᏲᏎᏗ ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᎠᏩᏠᏒ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏕᎧᏃᏎᎲ “Give him two months, he’ll be back!” ᎤᏛᏅ … ᎠᏩᎵ,ᏣᏙᏅ ᎤᏲᎱᏒ I just about preached at every one of our band members --ᏓᏂᏃᏴᎬ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩᏛ ᏧᎵ,ᏍᏙᏔᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏂᏓᏳᏓᎴᏅᏓ, 1972 ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: Well sgina … tsogina,danetselv hena, tsogina,tsvsdodi … “revival-i inena” awohelv na … tsalagi, dina,dawosgi, una,datlisodi … nowule tsisdawadvsv nvgine usv gehv … doyu, tla yawadulihe awenvsdi asesgini, tsisdawadvsv … na aqua,dvganv ali,tsadohvsgv si … gadanvtesgv si … na unali,sgisdi deganelohvsgv si tsigadanvtesgv ugvwiyusv … sgina J.R. segments.translation: Well, we had made plans to get married. “Let’s go to the revival!" she told me. It’s at the Indian Baptist Church. So, I went with her, it was on a Thursday night. Really, I didn’t want to go, but I went with her. I heard the pastor preaching himself. I was thinking about when I was playing at a dancehall, instead of listening. That J.R. Stodsdill he was a missionary. We were in a big church. He was standing about 60 feet away. Boy! I was looking at him, and he looked like he was looking right at me. He was standing 60 feet away. “He’s going to come over,” I thought. Or I told him. I really don’t know. I bent my head and was hanging onto the chair. He put his arm around me. Gah lee! That really made me mad. I used to really cuss around a lot. He hugged me. I looked at him, boy, I almost cussed him out. I told him, “I ain’t ready. Get out of here!” …. [patting sound] “I’ll be praying for you,” he said. I think that was the first time I heard the gospel and about Jesus Christ dying on the cross for us. Or when a man died and He raised them [from the dead], that’s the first time I heard it. I always heard, “Quit what you’re doing.” Y’know, “Quit doing this, quit doing that,” that’s what the Christian women were saying to me. We got in our pickup and I looked at her and said, “Don’t ever ask me to go to church again.” I was all mad. Then I took her back [home.] Then, we got married in September, on the 10th… no, it was the 17th or actually it happened on the 27th in September. I was under the truck, fixing it. And she said, “Let’s go to church!” I come out from under there and it was like you had burnt my feet with fire. “Didn’t I tell you?” I said, “Don’t ever ask me that again.” “What’s going on there?” I asked. “They’re having a prayer meeting,” she said. And I said, “What is going to happen at the prayer meeting? What can happen at a prayer meeting?” So, I went with her. (Scale?) Wilson was the pastor at Cedar Tree. He preached all in Cherokee. I wasn’t listening to him, I was still thinking about the dance hall. I didn’t want to listen. Then, when he finished singing, they were doing that altar call, I was standing there, hanging on. All of a sudden, it felt like somebody stabbed me in my ribs. It was like something hit me and I was standing in the middle of the aisle. This is what I heard, “DJ, go down or get out,” it said. Boy, I was standing there looking at the door. It wasn’t no further than that door right there, I was standing. That’s when I decided to get out. I couldn’t do it. When I took a step, I just went toward where Scale was standing. I went through there and he shook my hand. “What is it?” he said. I said, “I need Jesus,” three times. He sat me down. They started shaking my hand. They were crying; the late Winn and the late Hester were both crying. “What did I do?” I thought, standing there. They were hugging me, shaking my hand. And I thought, “What did I do?” When I got up in the morning, I used to shake. My stomach, or my guts, it was just like somebody was ripping them out. That’s the way it was. Then, on the fourth day when I got up, I was going to go to work. It felt like I had lost something, so I started looking in the house. I didn’t know what it was that I had lost. I put a coffee pot on the stove, put coffee and water in it. I used to brew my coffee. Then it came to me: my stomach wasn’t hurting. I looked at my hands and I wasn’t shaking. That was when I felt like I was healed. That's how it was, which was strange to me. It was strange to me. I went to work and I was crying. That’s how it happened, that’s where it [my faith] began. But when Saturday night came, the dance hall where I used to play, I went there and I played. Then when Sunday came, I got baptized. We had a new preacher, it was diganotsah,ld, he’s the one that baptized me. Then, after he baptized me, he said, “Are you going to ask Andy if it’s all right for you to be playing round-up club?” “As long as I don’t drink, it’ll be alright,” I told him. So, I went to the club and we were playing. Boy, something slapped me. I was playing and then [slap!] After it hit, it stung. This is what I heard, “DJ, what are you doing here?” it said. I looked at the clock, it was 9:30pm. Boy, but those two hours, it felt like all night to me. I never felt that lonesome before. But I got lonesome then. Two and half hours, then we finished playing. I put up my guitar, I put it in the case. I told Buddy, “I’m quitting.” “What’s going on?” he said. “I shouldn’t be here in the first place,” I said. “I joined church.” I didn’t know how to tell him that it’d help me to let it go. So, I quit the band. I heard him telling the others, “Give him two months! He’ll be back!” they said. I preached when he died. I just about preached to the whole band members when they died. That’s how it all happened, that’s where it started. It was 1972.

segments.translation: How about your preaching, when did you quit and give yourself over?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Well, 1976’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᏓᏩᏓᏲᏒ … two and a half years ᏕᏥᎦᏘᏯ,’Ꮫ Barber … ᏃᏭ ᎩᏔᏲ … ᏔᎵ,Ꮪ’ᏛᎲ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏕᏥᎦᏘᏴ … ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᏓᏩᏥᎳ ᏦᏍᎪᎯ, ᏦᎢ,’Ꮫ ᎨᏎᏍᏗ ᎯᎢ ᎧᎦᎵ, ᎧᎴᏍᏗ, … ᏍᎩᎾ … ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎪ,Ꮧ’Ꮫ ᎣᎩᏂᎪᎰᏅ … --ᎡᎵ ᎢᎦ mission trip ᎠᏇᏅᏒ Venezuela ᏔᎵ, ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, … ᎠᎴ New Mexico … ᎣᎩᏁᏅᏌ, … ᎣᎩᏁᏙᎵᏙᎸ’Ꮫ ᎤᏁᎳᏅ ᎣᏍᏗᏍᏓᏗᏙᎲ
segments.transliteration: Well, 1976’dv tsigehv’dv na dawadayosv … two and a half years detsigatiya,’dv Barber … nowu gitayo … tali,du’dvhv yudetiyvda, detsigatiyv … nowu’nv dawatsila tsosgohi, tsoi,’dv gesesdi hii kagali, kalesdi, … sgina … iga hena, usquanigo,di’dv oginigohonv … --eli iga mission trip aquenvsv Venezuela tali, yuwaga,da, … ale New Mexico … oginenvsa, … oginedolidolv’dv unelanv osdisdadidohv
segments.translation: Well, 1976, that’s when I quit and gave myself over. I pastored for two and a half years at Barber. Then in Cherry Tree, I was pastor there for 12 years. Now, Elm Tree, this February will be 33 years. We have seen many fascinating things. I’ve been on a mission trip to Venezuela two times. And we went to New Mexico. We have been all over, following Jesus.

segments.translation: Well, when we first started, it must’ve been ’73 The Cedar Tree Four started. I helped out until ’77, then I went and pastored. I was called on to pastor, so I gave it up. I wouldn’t have had time to do that and be a pastor. I turned it all to them. Then Hominy started helping them. Then there was the Cherokee Baptist Choir, it was probably ’85 or ’84. The late Svdiwad started gathering up people from our association. He started the Cherokee Indian Baptist Choir. When it began, there were 40 singers. Sanders, McClemore, and all them good singers. And when JB died… Then me…
