segments.text: ᎩᎳᎢᏴ ᏱᏍᏗᏩᏔ, ᏍᎩᎾᏃ … … ᏍᎩᏃ … ᏃᏭ Barber ᏕᏥᎦᏘᏴ … ᎦᎵ,ᏆᏍᎪᎯ, ᏑᏓᎵ, Ꮎ July ᎠᏂᏲᎲ --ᎤᏂᎦ,ᏘᏯ, March ᏗᏩᏓᏲᏒ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᎵ,ᏣᏗ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, July ᏫᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ Barber “ᏱᏨᏍᏕᎳ,’Ꮫ” Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᎲ ᏗᎩᎦ,ᏘᏗᏍᏗ … ᏚᎾ,ᏓᏠᏩᏗᏒ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, … July ᏫᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᎬᎩᏯᏅᎮ to fill in. “Well, I’ll fill in for you until you get a pastor,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎭᏩ” [ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏅ] … ᏃᏭ January ᏫᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, … “ᎡᏥᏲᎯᏧ?” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ “We got one! We got you!” ᎬᏬᎮᎸ’Ꮓ ᏕᎬᎩ,ᏏᏔᏛ’Ꮓ April ’77 ᎠᏓᏂᎳᎨ … ᎢᎾ ᏂᏓᏳᏓᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᏴ
segments.transliteration: gilaiyv yisdiwata, sginano … … sgino … nowu Barber detsigatiyv … gali,quasgohi, sudali, na July aniyohv --uniga,tiya, March diwadayosv gehv awali,tsadi nowu’nv, July winuli,stana, nowu’dv Barber “yitsvsdela,’dv” tla yawadulihv digiga,tidisdi … duna,datlowadisv asesgini, … July winuli,stana, gvgiyanvhe to fill in. “Well, I’ll fill in for you until you get a pastor,” gatsiyohelv “hawa” [una,dvnv] … nowu January winuli,stana, … “etsiyohitsu?” gatsiyohelv “We got one! We got you!” gvwohelv’no degvgi,sitadv’no April ’77 adanilage … ina nidayudalenvhv ayv
segments.translation: Yeah. But you can find that pretty quick. When I was pastor at Barber, it was ’76 in July and they were looking for someone to pastor. In March, I had given up preaching. In July, it was Barber, I told them, “I’ll help y’all.” But I didn’t want to be a pastor. They were congregating. So, in July, they called on me to fill in. “Well, I’ll fill in for you until y’all get a pastor,” I told them. [They said], “Alright.” Then in January, I asked them, “Have you all found one?” They said, “We got one! We got you!” They all put their hand on me in April of ’77, someone who was able. And that’s where it began.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ … Badger Lee’Ꮫ ᏥᎦᏘᏴ Ed Baker D.O.M ᏥᎨᎲ East Central ᏕᎦᏥᏲᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ Ed ᏫᏥᏩ,ᏛᎯᏙᎲ, “Ed, … ᏕᎦᏥᏲᎮᏍᏗ, Badger Lee” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ “ᎠᏎᏅ, month ᏓᎦᏥᏁᎵ, ᎤᏂᏩᏛᏗ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ -- ᏃᏭ “Charlie,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ “you call them back and thell them that you’re already going,” [ᎤᏛᏅ] “Cause if you give them a month, then you’re going to be there a year!” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv … Badger Lee’dv tsigatiyv Ed Baker D.O.M tsigehv East Central degatsiyosv sgina Ed witsiwa,dvhidohv, “Ed, … degatsiyohesdi, Badger Lee” tsiyohehv “asenv, month dagatsineli, uniwadvdi” tsiyohelv -- nowu “Charlie,” tsawohelv “you call them back and thell them that you’re already going,” [udvnv] “Cause if you give them a month, then you’re going to be there a year!” tsawohelv
segments.translation: Me, I was a pastor at Badger Lee and Ed Baker was D.O.M in East Central. I let them go. And then I went and told Ed, “Ed, I let go at Badger Lee. But, I’m going to give them a month to find someone.” “Charlie, you call them back and tell them that you’re already going,” [he said.] “Cause if you give them a month, then you’re going to be there a year!” he told me.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Y’know, his brother died and they’re having his funeral today.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Ed?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: He lived here in Tahlequah.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Clever ᏥᏚᏙᎥ Clever Baker cabinet shop ᏧᏬᏢᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ Ed Baker ᎠᎾᏝᏅᏝ ᏥᎨᎲ Yeah, ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏗᎨᏳᎲ Ed Baker … ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᎣᏍᏗᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎸ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ missions Albequerque, ᏃᏭ’Ꮓ Larue… oh man, in New Mexico.
segments.transliteration: Clever tsidudov Clever Baker cabinet shop tsuwotlvsv sgina Ed Baker anatlanvtla tsigehv Yeah, iga osdigeyuhv Ed Baker … sgi’e osdisdawadidolv’nv, squu missions Albequerque, nowu’no Larue… oh man, in New Mexico.
segments.translation: Clever was his name. Clever Baker. He had a cabinet shop. He was Ed’s brother. Yeah, we really loved Ed Baker. We went with him on missions> Albuquerque, Larue… in New Mexico.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Larue…no. I’m forgetting too.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: But ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎪ,Ꮧ’Ꭱ ᎣᎩᏂᎪᎢᏙᎸ … ᎣᏍᏗᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎲ ᎦᎶᏁᏓ ᏥᏌ
segments.transliteration: But iga hena, usquanigo,di’e oginigoidolv … osdisdawadidohv galoneda tsisa
segments.translation: But we really saw some interesting things. Following Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: He’s the reason why.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: I wouldn’t trade it for nothing in the world.
segments.transliteration: I wouldn’t trade it for nothing in the world.
segments.translation: I wouldn’t trade it for nothing in the world.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏙᏗᏍᏓᏛᏏᏙᎸ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏍᏗᏬᏂᎲ Ꮭ ᎡᏍᏗᎨᏳᏗᏍᎬ, ᏱᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: dodisdadvsidolv tsalagi, sdiwonihv tla esdigeyudisgv, yigehe?
segments.translation: When you all were growing up, were you all talking Cherokee? Or did they not let you all speak it?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: At Briggs? Huh uh, no. Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎣᎩᏅᏍᏓᏕᎸ ᏱᎨᏎᎢ ᏃᏭ, ᎣᏣᏅᎥᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏐᏛ ᏳᎶᏌ, ᎣᏥᏅ ᎠᏎ ᎮᎾ, ᏣᎦ,ᏔᏗ’Ꭱ ᎦᎪ ᎦᏙᎨ you know ᏍᎩᎾᎢ ᏱᏙᏥᎧᎾᏅ ᏱᏙᎩᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ Boy, ᎠᏓᎾᏫ,ᏍᏗᎲ’Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: At Briggs? Huh uh, no. tla ilvhiyu oginvsdadelv yigesei nowu, otsanvvsgv tsalagiha otsiwonisgo tsigehv gilo usodv yulosa, otsinv ase hena, tsaga,tadi’e gago gadoge you know sginai yidotsikananv yidogiyetsi,sgv Boy, adanawi,sdihv’dv
segments.translation: At Briggs? Uh-uh, no. They never got onto us. We would sit down and we’d all be talking in Cherokee. When somebody was walking behind us, they'd stop and then we'd look at him and laugh. Boy, then they’d take off running.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: “They’re talking about me.”

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎥᎥ “ᎬᎩᏃᎮ -ᎬᎩᏃᎮᎭ they’re making fun of me,” ᏩᎾ,ᏗᎰ “ᏗᎬᎩᏍᎩᎾᏗ” ᏃᏭᎴ ᎠᎾ,ᏗᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ ᎠᎩᏂ,ᏏᏂᏙᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ … “ᎯᎳ’Ꮫ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎬᏃᏎᎸ” ᏥᏲᏎᎸ Ms. Baker. “ᎥᏝ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏗᎬᏍᎩᎾᏗᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ” ᏥᏲᎮᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ … We just wanted to know who was behind me, or who was behind us. ᏙᏳ’Ꮕ ᎠᎾᎴᏫᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᎠᎾ,ᏛᏓᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ … ᎣᎩᎾᏫ,ᏍᏙᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ … ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ, ᎣᎩᏰᎸᏒ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: vv “gvginohe -gvginoheha they’re making fun of me,” wana,diho “digvgisginadi” nowule ana,diho tsigehv nowu’dv agini,sinidohv tsigehv … “hila’dv yuwaga,da, gvnoselv” tsiyoselv Ms. Baker. “vtla atsalagiha digvsginadisdi yigi” tsiyoheho tsigehv … We just wanted to know who was behind me, or who was behind us. doyu’nv analewisdisgv ana,dvdasdisgv atsalagiha otsiwonisgv … oginawi,sdodv tsigehv otsiwonisgv … uwoli,di, ogiyelvsv gohusdi,
segments.translation: Yeah, “They’re talking about me. They’re making fun of me,” they said. And they’d say, “They’re cussing at me,” and then they’d go tell on us. Then they punished me. “How many times have I told you?” I told Ms. Baker. “We do not cuss in Cherokee,” I’d tell her. We just wanted to know who was behind me, or who was behind us. Then they said they would stop listening to us speak Cherokee. We were making all kinds of noise speaking Cherokee, laughing.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Were you all speaking good English then?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: No? How about you?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏓᏩᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ ᎨᎵ‘Ꮫ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏙᏳ, ᏱᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ ᏓᏩᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ’Ꭱ
segments.transliteration: vv dawadelo;quav geli‘dv tla squu doyu, yiganvdadi nuli,stanidolv ase’dv ase dawadelo;quav’e
segments.translation: Yeah, I learned it. But I don’t really remember how it happened, but I learned it.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ‘Ꮲ’Ꮫ ᏅᎩ, ᎯᏍᎩ’Ᏼ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎩᎳ, … ᎠᏳᏁᎦ, ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᎦᏁᎵ,ᏗᏍᎬ … ᎾᎥ ᏲᎦᏓᎸ ᎤᏥ ᎨᎲ ᎧᎵ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎤᏙᏗ’Ꮕ, ᎧᎵ ᎠᏳᏁᎦ, … ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎠᏳᏁᎦᎭ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎪᎯ’Ꮕ, ᏥᎩ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏥᏂᏯ, ᏳᏴᏟᏝ, … that’s the first thing he’ll tell you. “ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ DJ ᏥᏰᏲᏅ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ, ᎤᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗᎢ” … ᏍᎩᎾ… and he did!
segments.transliteration: ‘tlv’dv nvgi, hisgi’yv yawadetiyvda, gila, … ayunega, tsiwonisgv awalenvhv ganeli,disgv … nav yogadalv utsi gehv kali atsalagi, udodi’nv, kali ayunega, … asesgini, ayunegaha gawonisgv, udvhistanv atsutsa, gohi’nv, tsigi, ahani, tsiniya, yuyvtlitla, … that’s the first thing he’ll tell you. “ayv’dv DJ tsiyeyonv agilisi, uwonihisdii” … sgina… and he did!
segments.translation: It probably wasn’t until I was four or five, I started speaking English. I started trying. My neighbor, his mom was a full-blood Cherokee and his dad was full-blood white. He had to speak English to raise his son. If he were to walk in today, he would say, “I was the one who taught DJ to speak English.” And he did!

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏥᏓᏩᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ ᎠᎭᏂ, Sequoyah. Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎩᎶ ᎠᏗᏍᎬ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎢᎦᏓ ᎮᎾ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏗᏮᏂ,Ꮧ, ᏍᏊ ᎠᏁᎲ ᎢᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ’Ꭱ ᎣᏤᏙᎰ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv tsidawadelo;quav ahani, Sequoyah. tla yiganvdadi gohu,sdi, gilo adisgv otsiwonisgv tsalagi, igada hena, gohu,sdi, diwvni,di, squu anehv ina nigada’e otsedoho otsiwonisgv
segments.translation: When I went to school here at Sequoyah, I don’t remember if we weren’t supposed to speak Cherokee or not. Some of my kinfolk were there. We were all there and we all spoke.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎯᎳ ᎠᏟᎢᎵᏴ ᏏᏉᏲᏍ ᏕᏣᏕᎶ;ᏆᎡ ᏂᎯ DJ? ᏝᏍ’Ᏺ?
segments.transliteration: hila atliiliyv siquoyos detsadelo;quae nihi DJ? tlas’yo?
segments.translation: When was it? Did you go to school at Sequoyah, too, DJ? No?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Uh-uh, I went to Tahlequah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It was you? [Francis]

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Mm-hm.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꭱ --ᎥᎩᏙ ᏌᏭ Ruby ᏚᏙᎠ, ᎤᎾ Sequoyah ᏧᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ
segments.transliteration: ayv’e --vgido sawu Ruby dudoa, una Sequoyah tsudelo;quav
segments.translation: One of my sisters, Ruby is her name. She went to Sequoyah.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Does she remember if they did not let her speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: She wasn’t kept from speaking.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: See? ᎠᏴ ᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᎩᎶ … ᎤᏣᏘᏂ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᎠᏎ ᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁᎰ … ᎦᏛᎩᏍᎪ … ‘Ꮲ … boarding school ᎨᎲ ᏓᏂᏅᏍᏓᏕᎲ … ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩᏭ ᎢᎦ --ᏍᎩᏭ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎦ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏚᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ᏱᎨᎮ
segments.transliteration: See? ayv squu tla yiganvdadi gilo … utsatini,’dv ase tsuna,deloquasdi ase nana,dvneho … gadvgisgo … ‘tlv … boarding school gehv daninvsdadehv … ayv, hena, sgiwu iga --sgiwu hena, iga otsiwonisgv, tsigehv eduda, hena, tsigehv tla yonega, gawonisgv, yigehe
segments.translation: See? I also don’t remember it like that. I hear there are other places like the boarding school, I hear, that’s what they do. They won’t let them speak. That’s all we spoke back then, at home. My grandpa couldn’t speak English.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is that how it was with your grandparents? They only spoke Cherokee?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: They were all Cherokee.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏲᏟ ᏱᎩ, ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, Ꮭ --ᏗᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏱᎨᎮ … ᏲᏁᎩ ᏗᏢ, ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: sgi’dv yusdi, adelo;quasdi, tsigehv nahiyu ayotli yigi, sgihena, tla --diniwonisgi, yigehe … yonegi ditlv, gehv
segments.translation: That’s what the children had to learn then. There weren’t any English speakers then.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Ꮭ’ᎮᎾ, ᏲᎨᏲᎲᏍᎨ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎣᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎣᏣ,ᏛᎩᏍᎬᏭ, ᎮᎾ,
segments.transliteration: tla’hena, yogeyohvsge tsalagiha ogiwonihisdi otsa,dvgisgvwu, hena,
segments.translation: They didn’t teach us to speak Cherokee, we just heard it.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: But you had to learn it.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏲᎵ, ᎠᏓᎾ,ᏏᏂᏙᎲ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎠᏂ--ᎠᏂᏬᎾ,ᏗᏍᎬ ᏍᎩ’ᏭᏅ, ᏧᎵ,ᏍᏙᏔᏅ ᎣᎦᏛᏒ … ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏣᏁᎶᏂᏙᎲ ᎠᎴ ᎡᏚᏥ, ᎪᎩᏩᏛᎮ, ᎠᎴ ᏙᏥᏩᏛᎮ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ:’Ꮫ ᏣᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, … ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ,’Ꮫ --ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎭᏕ ᏱᎨᏣᎵ,ᏍᎪᎵ,ᏓᏏ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᎣᏥᏲᏟ, Ꮸ,ᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ … ᎩᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏱᎪᎳ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayoli, adana,sinidohv tsalagiha ani--aniwona,disgv sgi’wunv, tsuli,sdotanv ogadvsv … ayv, hena, dotsanelonidohv ale edutsi, gogiwadvhe, ale dotsiwadvhe tsalagiha:’dv tsaniwonisgv sgihena, … asesgini, tsuna,tana,’dv --aniwonisgv hade yigetsali,sgoli,dasi, yigehe otsiyotli, tsv,dvdasdodi … gila yigohida, yigola tsigehv
segments.translation: A baby that’s crawling, they were correcting them all in Cherokee. That’s how it was when we grew up. We were playing around and our uncle would visit us, or we’d visit him, and they talked all in Cherokee. But when the grown-ups talked, they wouldn’t let you listen. Us children. You could get full eating real quick, back then.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: “Y’all go outside!” they’d say.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: “Y’all go play!”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏃᎴ’Ꮕ, ᏲᏣᏟᎢᏙᎲ, ᏃᏭᎴ “ᏫᏗᏣᏁᎶᏄᎦ,” ᏯᎾᏓ, ᏃᏭᎴ “ᎠᏥ,ᎩᎵ,’Ꭱ ᏓᏣ,ᏖᎳ,ᏕᎵ,” ᏲᎪᏌ,’Ꮓ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: nole’nv, yotsatliidohv, nowule “widitsanelonuga,” yanada, nowule “atsi,gili,’e datsa,tela,deli,” yogosa,’no tsigehv
segments.translation: When we were running around, “Y’all go play” [they’d say] and then it’d be, “A booge is gonna join y’all!”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗ ᏍᏗᏭ, ᏃᏭ … ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎩ, ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵᏍᏗ “ᏗᏥᏴᎯ! ᏗᏥᏴᎯ!”
segments.transliteration: nowu’dv gali,sdi sdiwu, nowu … uli,sigi, yini,galisdi “ditsiyvhi! ditsiyvhi!”
segments.translation: Just about when it was getting dark, then they would say, “Come in! Come in!”

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: The boys were talking about this back then.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: “Somethings going to join y’all playing!”

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎢᎾᎨ --ᏱᏙᏣᏁᎶᏂᏙᎳ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ “ᏴᏫ ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᏓᏣᎴᎾᏍᏔᏂ!” ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: inage --yidotsanelonidola, nowu’nv “yvwi tsuni,sdi datsalenastani!” anadiho tsigehv
segments.translation: When we played out in the woods, they would say, “The little people are going to get you all lost!”

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎾᏍᏊ … ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏌᏭ ᏦᏣᏗᏔᏍᎬ … bucket ᏣᏝᎥ ᎠᎹ, ᏌᏭ dipper ᏥᎨᎲ -- Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏲᏤᎵᏍᎨ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ᎠᏎ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏯᎾᏓ, ᏍᎩ ᏱᏅᏛᏁ
segments.transliteration: nasquu … ganvdadisgo tsunilawisdi nigada, sawu tsotsaditasgv … bucket tsatlav ama, sawu dipper tsigehv -- tla gohu,sdi, yotselisge gohi tsigi, ase gohu,sdi, yanada, sgi yinvdvne
segments.translation: I also remember at church, we all drank from the same dipper. There was a bucket and one dipper in it. It didn’t bother us back then. But today they would say something about it, if you’re doing that.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎡᏚᏓ,’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ --ᎠᏆᏙᏍᏔᏅ ‘Ꮲ ᏐᏁᎳ, ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎤᏒᏕᏂ, ᎠᎩᏲᎮᎸ ᏩᎩᎦ,ᏐᏒ ᎠᎹᏳᎵ;Ꮧ, *whistles* ᏗᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎹᏱ ᎧᏬᏄ ᏩᏂᏝ;Ꭺ’Ꮫ ᏅᎩ, ᏕᏥᎸ ᎪᎳ’Ꮕ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏴ, … ᎢᎦᏟ ᎨᎲ ᏩᏩᏚᏅ whoo! [ᎤᏴᏜ, ᎨᎲ] ᎤᎾ,ᏝᏫᏛ ᏥᎦᏥᎦᏙᏍᏔᏅ … ᏕᎦᏓᏩᏛᏅ’Ꮫ … ᏃᏭᎴ ᏦᎢᎭᏯ ᏙᏥᎸ ᏎᎦᏨ ᏕᏥᏃᏢ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏬᏛᏅ’Ꮫ ᎠᎹ, ᎠᎩᏟᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᎷᏨ ᎡᏚᏓ, “ᎦᏙ ᎭᏛᏁ?” – “ᎧᏬᏄ ᎣᏍᏓ, Ꮒ,ᏙᏓᎬᏁᎵ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎠᎻ’Ꮕ, --ᎠᎩᎵᏟ,Ꮫ … “Huh!” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏛᏡᏅ ᎠᏩᎦ,ᏙᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᎩᏟᏍᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎧᏬᏄ ᎠᎢ ᎾᏮᏁᎳ, ᏧᎧᏲᏛ ᏧᎩᏓᏟ, ᏕᎦᏃᎯᎵᏙᎲ ᏃᏭᎴ’Ꮫ ᏏᏭ’Ꮫ ᎤᎧᏲᏛ -- ᎤᏬᏢ’ᏭᏛ ᎠᏩᎦ,ᏙᏍᏛ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏚᎴᏅ ᎠᏰᎵ;ᏍᏗ, ᎤᎸᎲ ᏚᎾᏫᏛᎲ ᏭᏅᎦ,Ꮫ Ꮟ’Ꮫ Boy! ᎪᎯᏴ’Ꮫ *whoom* ᎤᏛᏅ ᏚᏢᏂ--…ᎦᏍᎩᎸ Ꮪ-Ꮪ-…
segments.transliteration: eduda,’dv tsigehv --aquadostanv ‘tlv sonela, yawadetiyvda, gehv usvdeni, agiyohelv wagiga,sosv amayuli;di, *whistles* didihv na amayi kawonu wanitla;go’dv nvgi, detsilv gola’nv, gehv ayv, … igatli gehv wawadunv whoo! [uyvdla, gehv] una,tlawidv tsigatsigadostanv … degadawadvnv’dv … nowule tsoihaya dotsilv segatsv detsinotlv adanelv awodvnv’dv ama, agitlistanv ulutsv eduda, “gado hadvne?” – “kawonu osda, ni,dodagvneli,” tsiyohelv ami’nv, --agilitli,dv … “Huh!” udvnv uli,sdvtlunv awaga,dostanv agitlisdv osda, kawonu ai nawvnela, tsukayodv tsugidatli, deganohilidohv nowule’dv siwu’dv ukayodv -- uwotlv’wudv awaga,dosdv gohiyv dulenv ayeli;sdi, ulvhv dunawidvhv wunvga,dv si’dv Boy! gohiyv’dv *whoom* udvnv dutlvni--…gasgilv du-du-…
segments.translation: My grandpa watched me one time. I was probably about nine years old, and he found me a shotgun. I went down the hill to the creek the ducks were [whistle] [making noise]. They were all over. I would kill four of them. It was winter. (…) I got in the water, whoo! [it was cold.] The ducks flew off, I watched them. I hung the others up, then killed three more. I barely made it home with them. I made a fire, then I put water in. Then my grandpa came “What’re you doing?” he said. “I’m gonna fix these ducks,” I told him. The water was boiling. “Huh!” he said. Then he sat down and watched me. The water was boiling, when I put the duck in and pulled it up the feathers were dry. Then I did it again. And he was just sitting there watching me. So, after a while he got up and took a knife out and took the other ducks with him. Boy! After a while, woom! He…

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: …he put them on the table.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏚᏢᏅ … “Ꭾ! ᎦᏙ Ꮒ,ᏕᎲᎦ,?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏕᏍᎩᏅᏏ!” [ᎤᏛᏅ] ᏥᏅᏁᎸ’Ꮫ ᎩᎳ’Ꮫ ᎠᏰᎸ ᎠᏥᏁᎦᎸᎲ’Ꮫ ᎧᏬᏄ, “Ꮭ ᏱᏍᎩᎯᏏ, ᏱᎨᎮ?!” [ᏥᏲᎮᎸ] – “ᎦᏙ ᏂᏍᎩ,ᏛᏛᏅᎾ,?” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎠᎩᏰᏣ,ᏗᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏚᏗ
segments.transliteration: dutlvnv … “he! gado ni,dehvga,?” tsiyohelv “desginvsi!” [udvnv] tsinvnelv’dv gila’dv ayelv atsinegalvhv’dv kawonu, “tla yisgihisi, yigehe?!” [tsiyohelv] – “gado nisgi,dvdvnvna,?” tsawohelv (uniyetsi,sgv) agiyetsa,diho tsigehv edudi
segments.translation: “Hey! What’d you do with them?” I said. “Give it here!” [he said.] So, I gave it to him. With a knife, he de-feathered the duck. “You didn't tell me!” [I told him.] “Why didn’t you ask?” he said. [laughter] My grandpa used to laugh at me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᎤᏥ ᎤᏮᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎩᏭ’Ꭱ ᏥᏭᎵ,ᏍᏛ ᎤᏁᎩᎵ;Ꮧ, ᎠᏒᎦ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᎬᏂᏍᏛ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᎲ ᏩᏩᏁᎵ;ᏙᏗ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: aya’dv squu na agi,sdayvhvsgi, utsi uwvnistanv sawu yuwaga,da, sgina sgiwu’e tsiwuli,sdv unegili;di, asvga awelisv gvnisdv sgi yusdi, tla squu yawadulihv wawaneli;dodi agisdi
segments.translation: Me too. My wife’s mother cooked duck one time. “It sure smells bad!” I thought. I didn’t even want to try to eat it.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Me too, I never have…

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: -ᎭᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏱᎦᎠᏛᎦ, ᏥᏍᏚ, ᏱᏥᎳ’Ꮫ ᏱᎬᏂᏍᏓ,’Ꭱ ᏌᎶᎵ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎭᏗ ᏱᎦᎬᏂᏍᏗ ᎧᏬᏄ,ᏭᎡ ᎠᏴ ᏕᎬᏂᏍᏗᎰ ᎠᏴ ᎧᏬᏄ, …
segments.transliteration: -hadi gohusdi, yigaadvga, tsisdu, yitsila’dv yigvnisda,’e saloli’le yigi, hadi yigagvnisdi kawonu,wue ayv degvnisdiho ayv kawonu, …
segments.translation: She doesn’t cook. When I kill a rabbit, she will cook it. Also, squirrels, she can’t cook. But if I kill a duck, I do the cooking.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎡᎵᏭ’Ꮫ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏁ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎥᏍᏊ ᏙᎩᏯᎥ ᏥᎨᏳᏣ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ, Ꮭ ᎥᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᏴ ᏱᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏗᎨᎪ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: eliwu’dv nuli,stane eliwu vsquu dogiyav tsigeyutsa, tsigehv nowu, tla vsgi yusdi, ayv yigali,sdayvhvsgo digaduhv digego (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: I think we ate enough of that when I was a little girl. Now, I don’t eat like that, I go to town. [laughs]

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꭱ ᎧᏬᏄ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎩ, ᎤᏪᎸ ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏗᎩᏓ, taste ᏄᏮᎾ, ᎧᏬᏄ … if you like liver, you’ll eat duck. … My niece ᎠᏂᏁᎳ, … ᎠᏋᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᎧᏬᏄ ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏛᏡᏂᏢ “Boy! This is good!” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, … ᏥᏃᎭᎵᏙᎯᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎧᏬᏄ ᏕᏥᏲᎯᎲ ‘Ꮲ ᏅᎩᎭᏯ ᏓᏋᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᏥᎾᏫᏛᎲ ᏌᏭ ᏥᏅᏁᎸ ᎤᏩᏰᏍᏗ, ᎢᎦ ᎤᎸᏉ,ᏔᏅ …but -- ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎦᏰᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᎧᏬᏄ, Ꮎ ᏍᎩᏂ, ᏌᏌ Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᏥᏯᏯᎥ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓᏝᏅᏟ ᏍᎩ Ꮎ Thanksgiving Ꮭ Ꮎ ᎬᎾ, … --ᎣᎩᏯᏯᎥ ᏱᎨᎮ “ᏌᏌ’Ꮫ” ᎠᏗᎲ ᎠᏂᏰᎲ … ᎣᏥᎾᏝᎡ ᏌᏌ ᏍᎩᏅ ᎬᏂᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᎡᏥ Ꮭ--ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, Ꮭ ᏱᎦ--*ᎤᎫᎴᎬ* excuse me-- ᏱᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᏂ,ᏢᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ
segments.transliteration: ayv’e kawonu hena, tsigi, uwelv hena, sdigida, taste nuwvna, kawonu … if you like liver, you’ll eat duck. … My niece aninela, … aquvnistanv kawonu uli,sdvtlunitlv “Boy! This is good!” udvnv nowu’nv, … tsinohalidohiho tsigehv kawonu detsiyohihv ‘tlv nvgihaya daquvnistanv tsinawidvhv sawu tsinvnelv uwayesdi, iga ulvquo,tanv …but -- osda, gayesdi, gehv gelisgo kawonu, na sgini, sasa tla yiganvdadi tsiyayav gehv osdatlanvtli sgi na Thanksgiving tla na gvna, … --ogiyayav yigehe “sasa’dv” adihv aniyehv … otsinatlae sasa sginv gvnisdisgv etsi tla--asesgini, tla yiga--*ugulegv* excuse me-- yiganvdadi nusdv ani,tlvdi gehv sginana
segments.translation: I think duck has a taste kind of like liver. If you like liver, you’ll eat duck. My niece’s husband and I cooked a duck. When he sat down, “Boy, this is good!” he said. I used to hunt ducks, I cooked about four of them. I took one of them and gave it to him to eat. He really liked it. I think ducks are good to eat. But I don’t remember ever eating a goose. My brother’s thanksgiving, we didn’t have turkey, “It was a goose,” he said. They ate it. We had pet geese. My mother cooked them, but… [burps] Excuse me. I don’t remember what they taste like.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꭱ Ꮟ ᏂᏙᎩᎾ,ᏨᏍᏗᎲᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ,Ꭱ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮥ Ꮎ’Ꮫ squash ᎴᏱᎩ, okra ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᎩᎵ’Ꮕ, ᏦᎩᎾᏁᎳᏛ ᎩᎳ, ᏎᎷᎦᏚ ᏥᎩ, ᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎮᎾ, ᏣᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏫᎨᏙᎰ ᏥᏩᏛᎯᏙᎲ ᎮᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ living room-Ꭲ ᎠᏯ’Ꭱ --ᏱᏥᏩ,ᏛᏗ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ kitchen-Ꭲ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏯᏛᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv’e si nidogina,tsvsdihvna, tsigehv tsi,quisdi,e hesdi, gohu,sdi, tla yagilvquo,de na’dv squash leyigi, okra sgi yusdi, hesdi, agilvquo,di, yigehe gili’nv, tsoginaneladv gila, selugadu tsigi, squu tla howa agilvquo,di, yigehe agvyi hena, tsawalenvhv wigedoho tsiwadvhidohv hesdi,’e ilvhiyu living room-i aya’e --yitsiwa,dvdi, yigehe nigohilv kitchen-i gohu,sdi, yadvne tsigehv
segments.translation: Me, before we got married, there were a lot of things I didn’t like, like squash or okra. I didn’t like things like that. Not until we got married. Even cornbread, I didn’t really like it. When I first started seeing her, she was never in the living room. She was always in the kitchen. She was always doing something in the kitchen.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: That’s why an elderly woman makes all the decisions. [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ pork chops ᏱᏚᏮᏂᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ whoo! “’Ᏺ’Ꮫ ᎭᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎭ!” ᏱᎬᏬᎮᎳ, ᎨᎵᎰ ᎨᎲ … ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ, ᎯᎢ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᏥᎬᎲᎦ ᏃᏭ, okra Ꮎ squah, ᎾᏊ zuccinni ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, --ᎬᎩᎩᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: doyu’dv pork chops yiduwvnida, tsigehv whoo! “’yo’dv hali,sdayvha!” yigvwohela, geliho gehv … gohiyv tsigi, hii sgi yusdi yitsigvhvga nowu, okra na squah, naquu zuccinni nigada, sgi yusdi, --gvgigisdi
segments.translation: She would cook pork chops, whoo! “I wish they’d tell me to eat!” I thought. Now, I can eat all the other stuff: okra, squash, and zucchini. I can eat all of those now.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: You like them now.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮕ greens…turnip greens ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, wow! Ꮎ ᏍᎩᏂ, ᏓᏈ,ᏌᏂ, --ᎠᎪᏍᏗ ᏥᎩ, ᎬᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᏍᎩᏂ, Ꮭ -- Ꮟ Ꮭ ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,ᏔᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᎯᎢ ᏍᎩ ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ ᏯᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᎦ, ᎾᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ … squash or fried tomatoes?
segments.transliteration: ayv’nv greens…turnip greens tsigehv tla yagilvquo,dv tsigehv asesgini, gohi tsigi, wow! na sgini, daqui,sani, --agosdi tsigi, gvnistanv sgini, tla -- si tla agilvquo,tana, yigi, hii sgi ase’dv yali,sdayvhvga, nahena, squu … squash or fried tomatoes?
segments.translation: Me, I didn’t like turnip greens. But now? Wow! And now, I can eat turnips raw, but not cooked. I still don’t like them. But this one, she really eats them cooked. And also, squash and fried tomatoes?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Those are good!

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: That’s good eating!

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I could really tear those up!

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎥᎦᏴᎳᎬ ᏓᏓᏁᏟᏴ ᎠᏂ,ᏢᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, … ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, greens, I like greens.
segments.transliteration: vgayvlagv dadanetliyv ani,tlvdi gohusdi, … sgi hena, doyu, hena, gohi tsigi, greens, I like greens.
segments.translation: When you get old, your tastebuds change. But really, nowadays, I really like greens. I like greens.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Last Wednesday, we ate wild onion.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: What is it?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Wild onion.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Ꭳ yeah? Ꮎ’Ꮫ Ꮎ my niece ᎣᎩᏅᏂᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏍᏊ ᎣᎩᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: o yeah? na’dv na my niece oginvnisdanelv squu oginelv
segments.translation: Oh, yeah? My niece cooked some for us and gave it to us.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: It didn’t have that… ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᏐ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ, Ꮭ ᎥᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏱᎨᏎ …
segments.transliteration: It didn’t have that… osda tsigeso agisdi, tla vsgi yusdi, yigese …
segments.translation: It didn’t have that… It used to be good to eat, but it wasn’t like that.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎯᎢ’Ꮫ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗ ᎦᏙ ᎤᏍᏛ’Ꮽ ᏱᎩ, ᎩᎳ ᏫᎦᏛᏗ ᏱᎩ, ᏔᎹᏟ, ᎢᎦ: ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎠᎩᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏴᏜᏗᏍᏗ, ᏱᎦᏢᏅ ᎠᏓᏁᏟᏴᎢ’Ꮫ ᎠᏣᏗ ᏥᎩ, ᏱᏘᏂᏴᎾ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏂ,ᏗᏨᏁᎳ, ᏱᏗᏣ,ᏒᏂᏔᎾ, ᎢᎦ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏗᎦᏰᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ refridgerator-Ꭲ for two hours even, ᎠᏓᏁᏟᏴ’Ꮫ ᎠᏂ,ᏢᏗ ᏗᎦᏰᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: hii’dv nigali,sdi gado usdv’wu yigi, gila wigadvdi yigi, tamatli, iga: osda, agisdi, nowu sgina uyvdladisdi, yigatlvnv adanetliyvi’dv atsadi tsigi, yitiniyvna, osda, yini,ditsvnela, yiditsa,svnitana, iga, osda, digayesdi, nowu’nv refridgerator-i for two hours even, adanetliyv’dv ani,tlvdi digayesdi,
segments.translation: This is the way it is: when you pick something, like a tomato, that just got ripe, that’s the best one to eat. When you put it in the freezer, the taste changes. Like, fish, if you catch some and you fix them up and fried them, then they’re good to eat. But if you put them in the freezer for even two hours, their taste changes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ’Ꮽ ᎣᏂ, ᏗᏢ, ᏙᎩᏂᏩᏛᎲ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ,
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv adanelv’wu oni, ditlv, doginiwadvhv inage ehi,
segments.translation: We found wild onions behind the house.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎤᏠᏱ, ᏄᏍᏗ, daddy ᎤᏤᎵ--ᎤᏤᎵᎪ ᏧᏥᏍᏗ ᏒᎩ, ᎢᎦ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᏍᎬ, ᎢᎾ ᎤᎾ ᎮᎾ, ᎡᎯ, spring ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, ᎡᎯ, ᎠᎹ, ᎤᎾ ᎠᏩᏛᏗ, Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, DJ ᎤᎾ ᏪᏙᎰ
segments.transliteration: utloyi, nusdi, daddy utseli--utseligo tsutsisdi svgi, iga tsi,quisdi, nigali,sdisgv, ina una hena, ehi, spring iyusdi, ehi, ama, una awadvdi, tsi,quisdi, DJ una wedoho
segments.translation: It’s the same way at my daddy’s land. There’s a lot of onion growing, because there’s a spring there. DJ goes over there.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: And I just crawl around. People might think I’m praying. [laughs]

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, Ꮭ -Ꮭ ᎤᏔᎾ, ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗ *ᎯᎢᏭ* ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎰ ᎣᏍᏓ, tender ᏥᎨᎰ
segments.transliteration: asesgini, tla -tla utana, yini,gali,sdi *hiiwu* nigali,sdiho osda, tender tsigeho
segments.translation: But it doesn’t get real big, it gets about this [gestures] big. Just when it’s tender.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎾᏍᏊ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ Ꮎ Ꮟ ᏂᎦᎷᏨᎾ, ᎤᎨᏓᎵᏴ ᎠᎾ ᎦᏅᎪᎩ ᏫᎦᏅᎪ Boy! ᎠᏰᏍᏓᎣ’Ꮫ ᎢᎾ’Ꮫ … ᏕᎦᎵ,ᏂᏩᎸᏗᏙᎰ’Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: nasquu adanelv na si nigalutsvna, ugedaliyv ana ganvgogi wiganvgo Boy! ayesdao’dv ina’dv … degali,niwalvdidoho’dv
segments.translation: At the house, before you get there, there’s a hill where there’s a spring. Boy, it’s all over the grown over. That is where I kneel.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is there watercress there too, at the spring?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Yeah, well… ᏥᎨᏒ’Ꭱ … Ꮎ ᏍᎩᏂ Teresita ᎤᎾ ᏥᏩᏘᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ I like it cooked or raw. ᎠᎬᎭᎷᏴ’Ꮫ ᎤᏗᏞᎦ, ᎪᎢ, ᎠᎻ’Ꮕ ᎢᎦ’Ꮫ ᎤᏖᏗ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, well… tsigesv’e … na sgini Teresita una tsiwatisgo tsigehv sgi’dv I like it cooked or raw. agvhaluyv’dv uditlega, goi, ami’nv iga’dv utedi
segments.translation: Yeah, well, it used to be there. And also, Teresita, I used to find it there. I like it cooked or raw. I like it cut up, put hot grease and salt on it. It’s delicious.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎤᏅᏗ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏬᏥᏢᏍᎬ ᎠᎹᏯ --ᎤᏴᏢ ᏲᏨᏁ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎠᎴ ᏍᏊ ᎪᏢᏅ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎥᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏓᎭ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎦᏓ, ᏓᏂᏁᎸ ice ᏣᏂᏂ,ᏕᏍᎬ if you had an icebox.
segments.transliteration: unvdi squu una tsiwotsitlvsgv amaya --uyvtlv yotsvne tsigesv ale squu gotlvnv gohu,sdi, vsquu na sgi yusdi, tla hena, yudaha hena, igada, daninelv ice tsanini,desgv if you had an icebox.
segments.translation: We used to put our milk in the spring. Also, butter. [To keep them cool.] Some people—if you had an icebox—they were selling ice.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: 50lbs of ice-Ꮫ ᏧᏩᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏦᎢ, ᏧᏒᎯᏓ, ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᎦᏢᏍᎪ’Ꮫ about 3 days, it was gone.
segments.transliteration: 50lbs of ice-dv tsuwasgo tsigehv edoda, tsoi, tsusvhida, yigohida, gatlvsgo’dv about 3 days, it was gone.
segments.translation: My dad used to buy 50lbs of ice. It lasted three days. He’d put it in, then in about three days it’d be gone.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Was it a big block?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: It was a 50lb block of ice.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ --ᎠᏂᏂ,ᏗᏂᏙᎯ, … Ꮎ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ, … … ᏳᏂᏫᏒᎾ, ᎠᏂᏂ,ᏕᎬ, ᏥᎨᏒ ᏣᏁᏙᎰ wagon-Ꭲ
segments.transliteration: nowule --anini,dinidohi, … na osda, ali,sdayv,di, … … yuniwisvna, anini,degv, tsigesv tsanedoho wagon-i
segments.translation: And some people that had gardens with good food, then they would sell it. They would go around in a wagon, selling it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What do you think is going to happen to the Cherokee language?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Well, ᎠᎾᏁᎵ;Ꮧ’Ꮫ … ᎤᎵ,ᏛᏙᏗ ᏂᎨᏒᎾ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᏛᎵ,ᏛᏔᏂ’Ꮫ ᎠᎴ ᎠᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᎩ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏯᏂᏬᏂ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, --ᎤᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, Ꮭ ᎠᎢᏒ ᏱᎨᏎᏍᏗ, … ᏍᏓᏱ ᎮᎾ, ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎰᎢ -ᎠᏉᏟᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎤᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ … Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏯᏂᎦ,ᏔᎭ Ꮎ ᎢᏗᏬᏂᏍᎬ “inflections” ᏣᏃᎮᎰ ᏣᏌᎳ,ᏗᏍᎪ Ꮭ ᏳᎾ,ᏠᏯᏍᏙᎡ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎾᏅᏁᎲᎾ, ᏱᎩ ᎠᏓᏁᏟᏴ ᏄᏍᏗ, ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏢᏍᎬ ᎠᎴ ᏥᏗᏬᏂᏍᎪ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, … ᎢᏗᏁᎬ ᏣᏌᎳ,ᏗᏍᎪ to “expressions” ᏥᏓᏗᎰ “Ᏺ!” ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎰ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎡᏍᎦ, ᏱᏂᎦᏛᏁᎳ, “Ᏺ!” ᏯᎾ,Ꮧ’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ (unintelligible) ᏥᎨᎲ “Haw!” ᏯᏗ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, that “expression” Ꮭ ᏯᏂᎦ,ᏔᎭ,
segments.transliteration: Well, ananeli;di’dv … uli,dvdodi nigesvna, asesgini, dvli,dvtani’dv ale ana,delo;quasgi, gohi tsigi, tla osda, tsalagi, yaniwoni na anigayvla, --uniwonisgi, tla aisv yigesesdi, … sdayi hena, nawali,sdanehoi -aquotlisdi aniwonisgv una,delo;quav … tla hena, yaniga,taha na idiwonisgv “inflections” tsanoheho tsasala,disgo tla yuna,tloyasdoe sgi hena, nanvnehvna, yigi adanetliyv nusdi, aninohetlvsgv ale tsidiwonisgo gohusdi, … idinegv tsasala,disgo to “expressions” tsidadiho “yo!” tsana,diho anigayvla, gohusdi, esga, yinigadvnela, “yo!” yana,di’e tsigehv nowu (unintelligible) tsigehv “Haw!” yadi sgi hena, that “expression” tla yaniga,taha,
segments.translation: Well, they’re really trying for it not to disappear, but it’s going to disappear. And the ones that are learning, they aren’t speaking well. The old way of speaking isn’t going to continue. It is hard for me to understand the ones that have learned it. They don’t know about the “inflections” they call it, the raise. They don’t include them. If they don’t use them, then it changes what they’re talking about. When we talk, we raise our voices in some words. “Expressions.” Some of the old ones, “Yo!” they say. If we were doing something wrong, they’d say, “Yo!” [Yolvg(i)?] would always say, “Haw!” But that “expression” they [the learners] aren’t familiar with it.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎨᏍᏗ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏄᏓᎴ ᏄᏍᏕᏍᏗ, ᎠᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᎠ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎡᎵᏭ, ᎤᏅᏌ, ᎨᏒ ᏧᎾ,ᏛᏒ ᏯᎾᏓᏙᎵ-ᏯᎾ,Ꮣ-ᏯᎾ,-ᏯᎾ,- ᎦᏙ’Ꮫ ᏴᏓ?
segments.transliteration: aniwonisgesdi’dv asenv, nudale nusdesdi, ana,delo;quaa, hena, asesgini, eliwu, unvsa, gesv tsuna,dvsv yanadadoli-yana,da-yana,-yana,- gado’dv yvda?
segments.translation: They’re going to be speaking it, but it’ll be different. They’re learning it, but they will be talking. And maybe the ones from the same generation will…how do you say it?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Be able to understand each other.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Be able to understand each other. Yeah, they’ll be saying things the same way.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Really—

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: --the ones that have just learned it.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: …ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ -- ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᏲᏎ’Ꭱ ᎮᎾ, ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏁᏲᎲᏍᎩ, ᏧᏁᏅᏒ ᏱᏭᏂᎷᏣ, … ᎤᎾ,ᏛᎪᏗ ᏧᏁᏅᏒ … ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, … ᎤᏚᎵ;Ꮧ, … -ᎣᏏᏭ, ᏱᎩ, ᏧᎾ,ᏓᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏱᏓᏂᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎯ, ᏓᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᎬ … ᎾᏂᎦ,ᏔᎲᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ … ᏯᎾ,ᏕᏠᎦ, ᏍᏗᎩᏓ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: …galieliga -- asesgini, yose’e hena, dina,daneyohvsgi, tsunenvsv yiwunilutsa, … una,dvgodi tsunenvsv … iga hena, … uduli;di, … -osiwu, yigi, tsuna,dagayvlige yidanisdawadidohi, dana,delo;quasgv … naniga,tahvna, yigi, uniwonihisdi … yana,detloga, sdigida, uniwonihisdi
segments.translation: But it will be good, what they’re teaching, if they would hear it when they get home, too. It would be good if the parents followed their kids while they’re learning, if they don’t know how to speak. They could learn to speak it a little bit.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎢᏯ,ᎦᏂᏌᏗ, ᎾᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬᎾ, ᏥᎩ, ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏍᏓᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᏧᏣ, … ᎯᏍᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎾᎥ ᏃᏭ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏝᏗ ᏳᏚᎵᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏗᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎤᏛᎪᏗ “ᏞᏍᏛ ᎥᏍᎩ ᏱᏂ,ᏍᎩᏗᏪᏍᎨᏍᏗ” ᎣᎩᏃᏎᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv iya,ganisadi, naniwonisgvna, tsigi, ayv, hena, osdadvhistanv atsutsa, … hisgi,sgohi, nav nowu, yudetiyvda, tladi yudulisgv osdiwonisgv tsalagi, udvgodi “tlesdv vsgi yini,sgidiwesgesdi” oginosehv
segments.translation: It’s our fault they don’t speak it. We raised a boy. He’s about 50 years old. He didn’t want to hear us speaking Cherokee. “Don’t talk to me that way,” he would tell us.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: “Don’t talk to me that way!” ᏣᏗᎲ’Ꭱ
segments.transliteration: “Don’t talk to me that way!” tsadihv’e
segments.translation: “Don’t talk to me that way!” he’d say.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: So, we didn’t teach him.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏃᏭ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, “ᎦᏙ ᎠᏓ, ᎯᎾ?” ᏯᏓ, ᎮᎾ, “ᎡᏙᏓ,” ᎠᏬᎮᎰ
segments.transliteration: nowu, gohi tsigi, “gado ada, hina?” yada, hena, “edoda,” awoheho
segments.translation: Now, today, he’ll say, “How do you say this?” and he calls me “edod(a).”

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, … ᎠᏴ, ᎨᏒ ᏁᎳᎩ, ᏱᏙᎦᏕᏲᏁ ᏱᏓᏤᏞ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏕᎩᎧᎭ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎤᎶᏐᏅ,
segments.transliteration: doyu, hena, … ayv, gesv nelagi, yidogadeyone yidatsetle diniyotli, degikaha asesgini, ulosonv,
segments.translation: I think it would’ve been good if we taught our kids to speak, but it’s too late now.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎢᏧᎵ,ᏍᏙᏔᏅ ᎮᎾ, Bell-Ꭲ ᏱᏭᎷᏣ, ᏱᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏚᏙᎥ ᏳᏂᎪᎠ, “DJ-Ꮝ ᎯᏲᎵᎦ,?” – “Yeah, ᎠᎩᏙᏓ’Ꮫ” ᏣᎳᎩᎭ --ᎠᏂᏬᎾ,Ꮧ… ᎠᏂᏁᎬ Ꮭ ᏯᎦ,ᏔᎲ ᎾᎴ ᏱᎩ, Kenwood ᏱᏭᎷᏣ, ᎠᎪᎵᎦ’Ꭱ ᎨᎲ ᎣᎩᏁᏥ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏃ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ --ᎠᎾᏝᏃᎮᏗᏍᎬ ‘ᏎᏍᎩᏂ, Ꮭ ᏱᎪᎵ,Ꭺ
segments.transliteration: itsuli,sdotanv hena, Bell-i yiwulutsa, yigehv na dudov yunigoa, “DJ-s hiyoliga,?” – “Yeah, agidoda’dv” tsalagiha --aniwona,di… aninegv tla yaga,tahv nale yigi, Kenwood yiwulutsa, agoliga’e gehv oginetsi, gehv sgino tsalagiha --anatlanohedisgv ‘sesgini, tla yigoli,go
segments.translation: It happens. When he goes to Bell, and they see his name they say, “Do you know DJ?” “Yeah, he’s my dad.” Then they’ll start talking to him in Cherokee. He doesn’t know it. He goes to Kenwood and they know who he is, he’s our son, and they talk to him Cherokee. But he doesn’t understand it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They think he’s a speaker.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Yeah. ᏍᎩᏅ ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, … ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏲᎩᏂ,ᏕᏏᏙᎯ, ᎡᎵᏍᏗ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ,…
segments.transliteration: Yeah. sginv ayv, hena, … tsalagiha yogini,desidohi, elisdi, asesgini,…
segments.translation: Yeah. We can throw Cherokee around, but sometimes…

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: We get confused, we don’t realize we’re speaking English.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’ᏛᏲ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏍᏗᏬᏂᏍᎪ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ --ᏯᏂᏂᏱ Ꮎ ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ --ᏣᏁᎳ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏑᏓᎵ, ᏙᎩᏂᎧᎭ, ᏦᎩᎾ,ᏚᎳ,Ꮫ ‘Ᏺ’Ꮕ, “ᎯᎢ, ᏂᏫ!” ᏱᏙᏍᏙᎮᎵ ᏱᎾᏂᏫ, ᎣᏍᏗ’Ꮕ, ‘Ᏺ ᏥᏗᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ᎦᏬᏂ --ᏯᏂᏁᎬ,’Ᏺ ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩ ᎤᏚᎵ;Ꮧ, ᎨᏒ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏍᏊ ᎯᎢ, ᏥᏓᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᎠ, Ꮭ’Ꮕ … ᎠᎾᏁᎵ;Ꮧ’Ꮫ ᏙᏳ, ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮎ ᏥᏓᏂ,ᏘᏃᎯ ᎠᎾ,ᏕᎶ;-- --Ꮭ ᏯᏬᎯᏳᎯ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏓᏂ,ᏑᏰᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏬᎯᏳᎯ, ᎮᎾ, ᏚᏂ,ᏑᏰᏌ, ᏧᏂᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎮᎾ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᎩᎳ, -- ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᏧᏂ,ᏑᏰᏍᏗ, ᏕᎦᏟᎶᏍᏗᏭ ᏌᏭ … ᎠᏩᏓᏚᏥᏴ ᎠᎨᏯ, ᎤᏢᏅ ᏭᏴᎯᏍᏗ ᎡᏧᎵ’Ꮕ, ᏧᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏯᏂᏯᎾ,
segments.transliteration: ayv’dvyo tsalagiha hena, osdiwonisgo aseno tla --yaniniyi na tsuni,sdi --tsanela, yudetiyvda, sudali, doginikaha, tsogina,dula,dv ‘yo’nv, “hii, niwi!” yidosdoheli yinaniwi, osdi’nv, ‘yo tsidiwonisgv, gawoni --yaninegv,’yo doyu hena, sgi uduli;di, gesv asenv, squu hii, tsidana,delo;quaa, tla’nv … ananeli;di’dv doyu, asenv, na tsidani,tinohi ana,delo;-- --tla yawohiyuhi, osda, dani,suyesgv gehv awohiyuhi, hena, duni,suyesa, tsunigayvlige hena, tsalagi, aniwonisgi, gila, -- sgihena, tsuni,suyesdi, degatlilosdiwu sawu … awadadutsiyv ageya, utlvnv wuyvhisdi etsuli’nv, tsugayvlige tsalagiha aniwonisgi, hesdi, hena, yaniyana,
segments.translation: We speak Cherokee all the time, but the kids we adopted, eight years old, we have six of them. But they do not understand it. We can tell them, “Say this,” and they’ll say it alright, they’ll sound like how we talk when they speak. That’s really what is needed. But the ones here that are learning, they are trying, but the ones that they are bringing to go to school I feel like they are not picking the right ones. They should pick ones that have parents that speak the language. For instance, my niece applied and both her parents are speakers, but they didn’t take her.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꭷ ᏙᏳ - Ꮩ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏪᎠ, ᎥᏍᎩ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ,
segments.transliteration: sgi’ka doyu - do osda, niwea, vsgi yuli,sdodi,
segments.translation: You are really telling the truth, that’s how it needs to be.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ - ᏍᎩᎾ ᏂᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᎥᏍᎩ ᏙᏳ’Ꮕ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎨᎵᏍᎬ, ᎤᏴᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ,
segments.transliteration: sgina - sgina nigelisgv vsgi doyu’nv osda, gehv sgina gelisgv, uyvsdi yigi,
segments.translation: So, that’s what I was thinking, that it would be really good if she got in.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏱᏕᎨᏲᎲᎦ, Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎠᏂᏐᎢ, ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏳᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏱᎦᏬᏂᎯ, ᎠᏲᏟ’Ꮽ, ᎨᏒ ᏱᏕᎨᏲᎲᎦ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ --ᏯᎾ,ᏛᎬᎦ,
segments.transliteration: yidegeyohvga, na squu diniyotli, anisoi, uwasa, yunv,ta, yigawonihi, ayotli’wu, gesv yidegeyohvga, gawonisgv --yana,dvgvga,
segments.translation: She could teach the other children, because she knows how to speak. Just because she’s a child, they would listen to her speaking.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎣᏍᏓᎦ,ᏎᏍᏔᎾ, ‘ᏧᏣ, ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎣᎩᎾᏘᏃᎮᏠ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏥ’Ꮕ, ᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ, … ᎠᏘᏃᎯᎲ ᎠᏲᏟ, ‘Ꮲ’Ꮫ ᏔᎵ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓᎦᏎᏍᏙᏗ, ᏃᏭ,’Ꮕ ᏒᎯᏰ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᎠᏥᏯᏅᎯᎲ … ᏭᏓᎪᎾᏔᏅ’Ꮫ ᎤᏟᏍᏗ, ᎤᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎧᏁᎪ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎣᏣ,ᏑᏂᏙᎲ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎢ ᏗᎦᏙᎬ “DJ!” ᏛᏳᏛᏅ “ᎦᏙ ᎤᏍᏗ?” – “ᎬᎨᏳ!” ᏗᏗᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᏍᎩᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏥᏃᏎᎳ, ᏳᏪᏍᏗ Boy! … ᎣᏍᏛ ᎧᏁᎬ
segments.transliteration: na osdaga,sestana, ‘tsutsa, usdi atsutsa, oginatinohetlo tsigehv utsi’nv, dulvwi,sdanehv, … atinohihv ayotli, ‘tlv’dv tali, yudetiyvda, gehv osdagasesdodi, nowu,’nv svhiye yinuli,stana, atsiyanvhihv … wudagonatanv’dv utlisdi, udelo;quav osda, kanego tsigesv otsa,sunidohv hena, ai digadogv “DJ!” dvyudvnv “gado usdi?” – “gvgeyu!” didiho tsigehv … sginv osda, yitsinosela, yuwesdi Boy! … osdv kanegv
segments.translation: We used to babysit a little boy. His mom was working. She would bring him, he was about two years old, for us to watch him, until the evening, then she’d come after him. He really learned well, he learned quickly. He spoke really well, then. We were fishing one time, he was standing way over. “DJ!” he said. “What?” I said. “I love you!” he’d be saying. When I’d tell him to say something; Boy! He spoke it real well.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ ᏦᎢ’Ꮫ ᎠᏎ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏧᏂᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ ᏥᏓᎴᏂᎲ “Amazing Grace” ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏂᎦᏓ, -- ᎧᏃᎩᏍᎬ ᎤᏩᏌ, Ꮭ -Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ;Ꮧ, ᏱᎨᎮ one verse ᎨᎲ ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏛ ᏃᏭ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ᎣᏍᏗᏄᎳᎲᏍᎪ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎤᏗ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᏊ … ᎠᎬᏱ ᎨᏒ … ᎠᏩᎴᏅᏓ, Ꮎ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏓᎵᏆ, … ᎣᏥᏴᎯᎲ Ꮎ classroom “ᏣᎳᎩ,’ᏛᏃ ᏓᏗᏬᏂᏏ, ᏣᎳᎩ,” ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎲ ᎾᎮᎾ, ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎤᎾ,ᏚᎵᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᎨᎲ ᏝᏗ ᎢᎦ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᏍᎬ Ꮎ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏯᎾ,ᏕᎰᏍᎬ, ᎠᏴ, ᎢᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ “ᎦᏙᎨ?” ᏱᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᏳᏓᎭ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᏂ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏛᏴ ᎠᎾᏁᎵ;ᏗᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: nowule tsoi’dv ase yudetiyvda, gehv tsunilawi,sdi tsidalenihv “Amazing Grace” tsalagi, nigada, -- kanogisgv uwasa, tla -tla gohu,sdi, uli,sdelv;di, yigehe one verse gehv gila’wudv nowu gohi tsigi, osdinulahvsgo gohu,sdi, udi nowule squu … agvyi gesv … awalenvda, na tsuna,deloquasdi ahani, daliqua, … otsiyvhihv na classroom “tsalagi,’dvno dadiwonisi, tsalagi,” gatsiyosehv nahena, aniyonega, iga osda, una,dulisgv nowu’nv, anitsalagi, gehv tladi iga nudale nigali,sdisgv na tla yawanv,ta, yana,dehosgv, ayv, igiwonihisdi, uniwonihisdi “gadoge?” yigelisgv yudaha na sgini aniyonega, gila’wudvyv ananeli;disgv
segments.translation: Also, when he was three years old he started singing Amazing Grace in Cherokee by himself in church. He didn’t need any help! He was singing one verse and now we can’t get him to say anything. When I first started school at Tahlequah, we would go in the classroom. “We are going to speak Cherokee now” I told them. And the white ones really wanted to learn. And the Cherokees, they didn’t even care. It was strange, I was thinking. I don’t know if they were ashamed to speak their language. But “Why?” I was thinking sometimes. But then the whites were trying, doing good learning.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎤᎪᏛ ᎤᏟᏍᏛ ᎠᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᎬ ᎾᎮᎾ, during my internship at Sequoyah Elementary, Mrs. Sheets principal ᎨᎲ superintendent-Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, Sally—ᎦᏙ’Ꮫ?
segments.transliteration: ugodv utlisdv ana,delo;quasgv nahena, during my internship at Sequoyah Elementary, Mrs. Sheets principal gehv superintendent-le yigi, Sally—gado’dv?
segments.translation: And they picked up a lot of it, quick. During my internship at Sequoyah Elementary, Mrs. Sheets was the principal or superintendent. Sally… What was it?

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Barnoski.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Barnoski. “DJ, can you come help me out some mornings?” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎭᏩ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏖᏲᏅᎢ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, Amazing Grace ᎤᏂᏃᎩᏍᏗᎢ!” – “’ᏙᏅ?”
segments.transliteration: Barnoski. “DJ, can you come help me out some mornings?” udvnv “hawa” tsiyohelv “teyonvi diniyotli, Amazing Grace uninogisdii!” – “’donv?”
segments.translation: Barnoski. “DJ, can you come help me out some mornings?” she said. “Yeah, I can,” I told her. “I want you to teach the children to sing Amazing Grace in Cherokee,” she said. “What for?” I said.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: And they did learn.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎤᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ ᎤᎿ gym-Ꭲ ᏬᏥᏯᎥ ᏙᏥᏃᎩᎲ ᎤᎶᏐᏅ
segments.transliteration: una,delo;quav uhna gym-i wotsiyav dotsinogihv ulosonv
segments.translation: They learned it. We were in the gym, and we were singing and singing it.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: He was in charge.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Mrs. Sheets ᎤᎴᏫᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᏛᏓᏍᏔᏅ ᏦᎩᏍᏆᏛ “DJ, will you come to my office?” ᏓᏳᏛᏅ intercom “Ꭷ! ᎦᏙ ᎦᏛᎩ?!” ᎨᎵᎰᎢ’Ꮫ ᏩᎩᏴᏟᏢ “You and those kids are on the Christmas program!” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ ᎦᏥᏃᏎᎸ’Ꮫ ᎤᏂᏍᎦᎸ’Ꮫ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, “No, you’re gonna be alright!” Boy! ᎣᏣᎩᏐᏗᎰ’Ꮫ ᏙᏳ,’Ꮓ Christmas program ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏢ --ᎤᎾᎴᏅ’Ꮫ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏚᎾ,ᏗᏍᎪ’Ꮫ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ,
segments.transliteration: Mrs. Sheets ulewistanv udvdastanv tsogisquadv “DJ, will you come to my office?” dayudvnv intercom “ka! gado gadvgi?!” gelihoi’dv wagiyvtlitlv “You and those kids are on the Christmas program!” awohelv (uyetsi,sgv) doyu,’nv gatsinoselv’dv unisgalv’dv diniyotli, “No, you’re gonna be alright!” Boy! otsagisodiho’dv doyu,’no Christmas program nuli,stanitlv --unalenv’dv diniyotli, duna,disgo’dv sdigida,
segments.translation: Mrs. Sheets, she walked by and stopped to listen to it. When we finished, “DJ, could you come to my office?” she said from the intercom. “Come! What did you do?” I thought. I went in there. “You and those kids are on the Christmas program!” she told me. [laughs] So, I told them and they got nervous. “No, you’re gonna be alright!” I told them. Boy! We needed to practice. Then the Christmas program came around. The children stood up with their heads down.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Their parents were sitting there.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏧᏂᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎧᎵ ᎠᏂᏅ gymnasium ᎧᎵ ᎠᏂᏅ Boy! ᎭᏛ ᎰᏩ ᏯᏂᏅᎪᎨ “Come on, kids! Sing!” Boy! ᎤᏂᏍᏆᏛ’Ꮫ *claps* ᏚᎾ,ᎴᏅ’Ꮫ ᏧᎾᏓᎦᏴᎵᎨ “Do it again!” ᏓᏳᎾ,ᏛᏅ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᏗᎩᏗ’Ꮓ ᎠᏍᏓᏯ ᎠᏂᏃᎩᎲ ᏦᎢᏁᎢ’Ꮓ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, Boy! ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ ᎠᏂᎦ,ᏖᏃᎲ ᏓᏂᏃᎩᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, Ꮎ ᎾᎮᎾ, ᎠᏂᏳᏁᎦ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎠᏍᏓᏱ ᏚᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎯ, ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᏗ ᏏᎾ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᎦᏙ’Ꮫ ᏥᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: tsunigayvlige kali aninv gymnasium kali aninv Boy! hadv howa yaninvgoge “Come on, kids! Sing!” Boy! unisquadv’dv *claps* duna,lenv’dv tsunadagayvlige “Do it again!” dayuna,dvnv nowule sdigidi’no asdaya aninogihv tsoinei’no yuwaga,da, Boy! ase’dv aniga,tenohv daninogisgv sgihena, na nahena, aniyunega, diniyotli, asdayi dunilvwi,sdanehi, tsuna,delo;quasdi sina, anitsalagi, iga hena, doyu, hena, gado’dv tsinigali,sdi,
segments.translation: Their parents filled up the gym. It was a full house, they hardly spoke. [the children] The kids sang and when they got through, all their parents stood up, clapping. “Do it again!” they said. They sang a little louder this time. Then the third time, they were singing and were looking around. That’s why those white kids were working so hard to learn it. Really, I don’t know why we are like that.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: I think they don’t want to draw attention to themselves. That’s what I think.
segments.transliteration: I think they don’t want to draw attention to themselves. That’s what I think.
segments.translation: I think they don’t want to draw attention to themselves. That’s what I think.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ ᎠᏎ ᎤᏩᏒᎯ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎾᏩᏍᏗ, (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) … ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, high school ᏕᎦᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᎬ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏱᎨᎮ … ᎠᎩ,ᏛᏛᏅ ᏏᏴᏫ, Barbra Jones’Ꮫ “DJ, what’re you doing now?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “ᏗᏥᎦᏘᏯ, ᏧᏂᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ” – “What?!” ᎤᏛᏅ “We had to drag words out of you when you were going to high school!” “ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᏙᏳ’Ꮕ … ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, we just don’t like to draw attention to ourselves. I think.
segments.transliteration: ayv ase uwasvhi nudale nawasdi, (uyetsi,sgv) … asesgini, high school degadelo;quasgv tla howa tsiwonisgi, yigehe … agi,dvdvnv siyvwi, Barbra Jones’dv “DJ, what’re you doing now?” awohelv “ditsigatiya, tsunilawi,sdi” – “What?!” udvnv “We had to drag words out of you when you were going to high school!” “awohelv doyu’nv … doyu, hena, we just don’t like to draw attention to ourselves. I think.
segments.translation: I guess I’m the only one that’s like that. I’m different. [laughs] But, when I was in high school, I didn’t really speak much. One person would ask me, it was Barbra Jones “DJ, what’re you doing now?” she asked me. “I’m a pastor at a church.” She said, “What!? We had to drag words out of you when you were going to high school!” she told me. Really, I think we just don’t like to draw attention to ourselves. I think.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You all don’t believe that the Cherokee language is going to end?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: It’s going to disappear, I believe.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You don’t think anyone will ever be speaking it?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎪ,Ꮧ’Ꮫ ᎨᏎᏍᏗ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, Ꮭ ᏱᏓᏂᎪᎢ, ᎠᏴ, … Ꮭ ᏱᏓᏂᎪᎢ, … … Ꮒ,ᏗᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ’Ꮫ … ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎧᎵ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᎠᏴ, ᏥᏄᏍᏗ, ᎢᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎤᏪᏘ, ᎠᏎ ᏱᏓᏓ, Ꮭ ᏱᏓᎾ,ᏕᏲᎲᏍᎦ, ᎩᎳ ᎤᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ ᏓᎾ,ᏕᏲᎲᏍᎦ, … ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏥᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ
segments.transliteration: usquanigo,di’dv gesesdi, asesgini, tla yidanigoi, ayv, … tla yidanigoi, … … ni,digali,sdodi’dv … doyu, hena, osda, kali aniwonisgi, ayv, tsinusdi, igiwonihisdi uweti, ase yidada, tla yidana,deyohvsga, gila una,delo;quav dana,deyohvsga, … sgina, tsinigali,sdodi
segments.translation: It will be interesting, but we will not see it. We won’t see it. Because the good, fluent speakers, like how we talk, they are not teaching that. It’s the ones that have learned recently, teaching it. That’s why…

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎾᏍᎩ ᏥᏂᏪᏍᎬ ᎩᎳ,Ꮽ, ᎡᎵᏭ, … ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏲᏟ, ᎥᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏱᏛᏂᏯᏂ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎣᏏ ᏱᎩ, ᏙᏳ ᎣᏏ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎥᏍᎩ ᏳᎾ,ᏕᎳᎰᏌ, ᎩᎶ ᎥᎬᏱ ᎡᏙᎯ, Ꮎ ᏱᎬᏩᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᏱᎩ, ᏃᏭ, ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏱᏛᏂᏯᎾ, --ᏱᏛᏂᏯᏅᎯ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏩᏌ, ᎨᎵ ᎠᏴ, ᎨᏒ ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓ,
segments.transliteration: nasgi tsiniwesgv gila,wu, eliwu, … gayu,la, gawonisgi yigi, ayotli, vsgi yusdi, yidvniyani ahani, osi yigi, doyu osi yigi, asenv, vsgi yuna,delahosa, gilo vgvyi edohi, na yigvwadvne,di yigi, nowu, gayu,la, aniwonisgi, diniyotli, yidvniyana, --yidvniyanvhi ahani, sgi hena, uwasa, geli ayv, gesv yini,gali,sda,
segments.translation: Also, what you were saying a while ago, if there is a child who already speaks it well. They should bring them here, that might be good. That would be good. When they appreciate the ones that are in front and would do it. And if they brought children who are already speakers here. That’s the only thing I think could happen.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏧᎾ,ᏕᏲᏗ ᏧᏂᎪᎲ --ᏳᏂᎪᎲ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏲᏟ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏐᎢ, ᏳᎾ,ᏚᎵ,Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: tsuna,deyodi tsunigohv --yunigohv hena, ayotli, osda, gawonisgv soi, yuna,duli,dv
segments.translation: They need to teach it. When they see a child who can speak already, they will want it.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎥᏍᎩᏂ ᏱᏚᏂᏍᏕᎸᎭ, ᏓᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᎬ ᏳᏂᏍᏆᏓ, ᎥᏍᎩᎾ, ᏓᎾ,ᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ, … ᏙᏳ ᎣᏏ ᎠᏎ ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓ,
segments.transliteration: vsgini yidunisdelvha, dana,delo;quasgv yunisquada, vsgina, dana,deyohvsgi, … doyu osi ase yini,gali,sda,
segments.translation: If they finish going to school, then they could let them teach. That could be really good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏃᏭ,’ᏅᎭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎯᎯᏰᏗ, ᏱᎩ, ᎣᏂ, ᏛᎾᎢ, ᎨᏒ ᎤᏂᏴᏍᏙᏗ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎤᏅ,ᏙᏗ, ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏱᏕᎯᎯᏰᏌ,?
segments.transliteration: nowu,’nvha gohu,sdi, hihiyedi, yigi, oni, dvnai, gesv uniyvsdodi, osda, unv,dodi, ‘do usdi yidehihiyesa,?
segments.translation: If you could leave something for the ones who are coming up, for them to use. What would you leave for them?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Huh. Boy, that’s a tough question. … ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎯᎢ, ᏥᏂᏓᏛᏁᎠ, ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ, ᎣᏏ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ … ᎦᎶᏁᏛ ᏥᏌ, ᎤᏃᎮᏗ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ, ᏂᏗᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᎯᎢ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏔᎵ, ᏧᏒᎯᏓ, -- ᏒᎯ,’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎦᏓᏂᏌᏅ ᏃᏭ, ᏧᏅ,ᎩᎶᏍᏗ, ᏒᎯ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎦᏚ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎤᏩᏌ, ᎤᏓᏢ ᎠᎦᏃᏴᎬ … ᎦᏙᎬ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, ᎤᎾ ᎦᎷᎬ ᎧᏁᏌᎥ ᎠᏠᏱᎲ … Ꮭ ᏯᏆᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎤᏙ ᏱᎩ, … ᏩᎩᎷᏨ ᎠᏠᏱᎲ’Ꮫ … “ᎦᏙ ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎴ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎤᏩᏌ, ᎤᏓᏢ” ᎤᏛᏅ … ᎠᏠᏱᎲ ᏥᏯᏄᎩᏢᏅ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎤᏝᏅ ᎠᏍᎪᎵ, ᎠᏠᏱᎲ ᎦᎶᏁᏓ ᏥᏌ, ᏥᏁᎢᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᎩᏌᏙᏴ … “I don’t want to hear that,” ᎤᏛᏅ … ᎠᏴ, … ᎢᎦ ᎥᎩᏃᏎᎸ’Ꮓ ᎤᎿ ᎤᏃᏴᏨ ᎩᎳ ᏗᎾ,ᏛᏍᎩ, -- teenagers ᎠᏓᎸᏕᏱ,ᏍᏗᏍᎩ, ᏚᏃᎩ,Ꮢ ᎤᎾᏕᏲᎴ … ᏍᎩᏭ ᎮᎾ, ᏄᏍᏗ, ᏚᏭᎪ,ᏗᏓ, ᎡᎶᎯ, Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎨᏐ ᎤᎾ,ᏛᎪᏗ ᏱᎩ, ᎤᎾᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ;ᏙᏗ, ᎠᏓᏅ,ᏙᎯ, ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ;ᏙᏗ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏳᎾ,ᏚᎵ ᎤᎾ,ᏛᎪᏗ ᎾᏍᎩ ᏍᎩᏂ, ᎣᏍᏙ ᎠᏓᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᏗ, …
segments.transliteration: Huh. Boy, that’s a tough question. … ahani, hii, tsinidadvnea, una,dvdasdodi, osi yigi, asesgini, ayv, gehv … galonedv tsisa, unohedi yawaduli, nidigali,sdodi hii nuli,stanv tali, tsusvhida, -- svhi,’dv tsigehv dogadanisanv nowu, tsunv,gilosdi, svhi, tsigehv sgigadu yudetiyvda, atsutsa, uwasa, udatlv aganoyvgv … gadogv ageyutsa, una galugv kanesav atloyihv … tla yaquanv,ta, udo yigi, … wagilutsv atloyihv’dv … “gado uli,sdanele?” tsiyohelv “uwasa, udatlv” udvnv … atloyihv tsiyanugitlvnv ahani, utlanv asgoli, atloyihv galoneda tsisa, tsineistanv agisadoyv … “I don’t want to hear that,” udvnv … ayv, … iga vginoselv’no uhna unoyvtsv gila dina,dvsgi, -- teenagers adalvdeyi,sdisgi, dunogi,sv unadeyole … sgiwu hena, nusdi, duwugo,dida, elohi, tla osda geso una,dvgodi yigi, unali,sdelv;dodi, adanv,dohi, uli,sdelv;dodi gehv tla yuna,duli una,dvgodi nasgi sgini, osdo adanv,dadisdi, …
segments.translation: Huh. Boy, that’s a tough question. This thing that we’re doing, that’s what they need to listen to. But I think they should believe in God. Because this happened two days ago. Yesterday, we had a funeral. Last Friday, we had a funeral for a 15-year-old boy who killed himself. They buried him. And a girl came to the coffin and was there crying, I didn’t know if that was his sister. I went over there and she was crying. “What happened to him?” I asked. “He killed himself,” she said. She cried. I hugged her. She put her head here [gestures] and was crying. I mentioned to her about Jesus and she pushed me away. “I don’t want to hear that,” she said. After the funeral, people told me that these younger kids that use the stuff that makes you dizzy [drugs] they said they went around the grave. That’s just how the world is, things are going to be happening. If they hear and realize they can get help. To help their souls. They don’t want to hear it. But that stuff makes them feel good.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Just for a while.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏚᎾ,ᎦᏛ ᎮᎾ, vodka Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, … ᎠᎱᎵ,ᏒᎬ vodka … ᎢᎦ ᏥᏯᏙᎵᏨ … Ꮭ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᎦ, ᏱᎩ, ᎤᎾᎦ,ᏎᏍᏙᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎨᏎᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏥ ᎤᏩᏌᏭ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎤᏠᏱ ᏫᏛᏛᏁᎵ, ᎤᏙ ᏄᏛᏁᎸ … ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, … What would I leave my children? … The first thing I’d want to leave my children ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,’Ꮫ ᎤᏃᎯᏳ,Ꮧ, ᎦᎶᏁᏓ ᏥᏌ, ᎠᎴ ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ ᎤᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᏗ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᎤᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᏗ ᎤᎬᏩᏟ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, … ᎤᏲ ᎮᎾ, ᏚᏚᎪ,ᏗᏓ, ᎡᎶᎯ, … S nd Gomorrah’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏃᏭ, ᎢᏗᎯᎵ, ᎢᏗᎯᎵ, -- ᎠᏂᏍᎦᏯ ᏓᎾ,ᏓᏨᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᎨᏯ, ᏓᎾ,ᏓᏨᏍᏗ Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᎥᏍᎩ ᎤᏓᏁᏝᏅ ᎤᏁᎳᏅ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ’Ꮕ, ᎠᎨᏯ ᎤᎾᏁᎳ,ᏗᏍᏗ ᎤᏓᏁᏝᏅ ᎤᏁᎳᏅ
segments.transliteration: duna,gadv hena, vodka na ageyutsa, … ahuli,svgv vodka … iga tsiyadolitsv … tla gatsiyoliga, yigi, unaga,sesdodi, hena, gesesdi na ageyutsi uwasawu,’le yigi, utloyi widvdvneli, udo nudvnelv … asesgini, gohusdi, … What would I leave my children? … The first thing I’d want to leave my children gohu,sdi,’dv unohiyu,di, galoneda tsisa, ale gawonihisdi gesv una,delo;quasdi tsalagi osda, uniwonihisdi, una,delo;quasdi ugvwatli sgina iga hena, … uyo hena, dudugo,dida, elohi, … S nd Gomorrah’le yigi, nowu, idihili, idihili, -- anisgaya dana,datsvsdi anigeya, dana,datsvsdi tla hena, vsgi udanetlanv unelanv asgaya’nv, ageya unanela,disdi udanetlanv unelanv
segments.translation: They smelled like vodka, that girl [and them]. Her breath smelled like vodka. I really felt sorry for her. I didn’t know them. They need to look after that girl. Or she’s going to do the same as her brother did. But, what would I leave my children? The first thing I’d want to leave my children is for them to believe in the Lord. And for them to learn to speak Cherokee. For them to learn its meaning. The world is going to be a bad place… Sodom and Gomorrah … that’s where we are headed. The men are getting married and the women are getting married. That is against what the Bible says. Men and women are supposed to get married. That’s what God intended.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᎨᏯ, ᏣᎪᏢᏅ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: sgi hena, yusdi, ageya, tsagotlvnv dohv?
segments.translation: That’s why he made a woman.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s what he made a woman.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right!

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏍᎦᏯ’Ꮺ ᎤᎾ,ᎵᎪ,Ꮧ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏐᎢ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᏯᎪᏢᎾ,
segments.transliteration: asgaya’we una,ligo,di yigehe soi, hena, asgaya, yagotlvna,
segments.translation: If a man was supposed to be with another man, he would've made another man instead.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏙᏳ! ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ … ᏍᎩ ᏱᎨᏎ Ꮭ ᏱᎨᏕᎮ
segments.transliteration: doyu! asesgini … sgi yigese tla yigedehe
segments.translation: That’s true. But, if that’s how it was, we wouldn’t have been here.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They wouldn’t have multiplied.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎤᏅᏅ’Ꮫ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎤᏁᎳᏅ … ᎤᏅᏅ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, Ꮭ … ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎬ --ᏱᏕᏙᎯ, ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎤᏬᏪᎳ, ᏱᎦᏛᏁᎵᏓᏍᏗ “ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏂᏣᏛᏁᎮᏍᏗ ᎣᏍᏗ ᎢᏤᎮᏍᏗ,” ᎤᏛᏅ we can look back, ᎢᎬᏌ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᎩ,ᏑᏰᏒᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ … ᎤᏲᏟ ᎮᎾ, ᏴᏫ, ᏚᏳᎪ,Ꮫ ᏄᏢᎾ, ᏱᎩ ᎤᏓᏅ,Ꮫ Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏚᏳᎪ,Ꮫ ᏱᎬᏩᎢ, ᏏᏴᏫ, ᎤᏩᏌ, ᎤᏓᏅ,ᏖᏗ ᏱᎩ,
segments.transliteration: unvnv’dv gayu,la, unelanv … unvnv gayu,la, tla … uli,sigv --yidedohi, gayu,la, nigada, uwowela, yigadvnelidasdi “sgi yusdi, nitsadvnehesdi osdi itsehesdi,” udvnv we can look back, igvsa, osda, nigi,suyesvna, tsigehv nudale nuli,stanidolv … uyotli hena, yvwi, duyugo,dv nutlvna, yigi udanv,dv tla hena, duyugo,dv yigvwai, siyvwi, uwasa, udanv,tedi yigi,
segments.translation: God has already laid the road out. He already laid the path. We are not in the dark. He already wrote everything we need to do. “If you all follow that, you will have a good life,” He said. We can look back, ourselves, to see when we didn’t do good. When things went a different way. People without a good heart in them, they are worse off. A person can’t go the right way thinking by themselves.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎯᎾ’Ꮂ ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏍᎩᎦᏚ ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ‘Ꮲ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, Ꮭ ᎠᎭ,Ꮒ, ᏱᏁᏙᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᏴ, ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏕᏍᏗ ᎮᎵ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏰᏟ,?
segments.transliteration: hina’hv sgohi, sgigadu tali,sgohi,’le yigi, ‘tlv tsudetiyvda, tla aha,ni, yinedohesdi ayv, ‘do usdesdi heli tsalagi, ayetli,?
segments.translation: How about in about 10, 15, or 20 years from now. We won’t be here. What do you think the Cherokee Nation will be like?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎢᎦ’Ꮫ … ᎯᎢ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏰᏟ, ᏥᏄᏍᏗᏓ, ᎤᎬᏫᏳᎯ ᏣᏯᎠ, … ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎤᏓᏅ,ᏖᏟᏓᏍᏗ … ᎠᎴ ᏚᎦ,ᏎᏍᏗᏕᎬ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᏞᎦᏭ, ᎢᏕᎯ, ᎠᎴ --ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏁᎵ,Ꮧ ᎤᏁᏉᎢᏍᏗ … ᏩᏥᎾ,’Ꮫ ᏙᏓᎫᎪ,ᏔᏂᏙᎵ, Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏱᎦᏕᎷᏗ ᏩᏥᎾ, ᎤᎬᏫᏳᎯ ᎨᏒ ᎠᎹ ᎠᏰᏟ, ᎠᎴ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎣᎦᎳᎰᎻ, ᎾᎮᎾ, Bo Parrish ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᎳᏬᏗ ᎯᎢ’Ꭱ ᏃᏥᏪᏎᎰ Oklahoma “ᏧᏯᏓᏚᎩ”
segments.transliteration: iga’dv … hii tsalagi, ayetli, tsinusdida, ugvwiyuhi tsayaa, … osda, udanv,tetlidasdi … ale duga,sesdidegv anigayvla, asesgini, tlegawu, idehi, ale --atsalagi, gawonihisdi gesv squu aneli,di unequoisdi … watsina,’dv dodagugo,tanidoli, tla hena, yigadeludi watsina, ugvwiyuhi gesv ama ayetli, ale ahani, ogalahomi, nahena, Bo Parrish tsigehv elawodi hii’e notsiweseho Oklahoma “tsuyadadugi”
segments.translation: Really, the way the Cherokee Nation is today. The Chief that’s in office right now, he’s a good decision maker. And he looks after the elders, but we’re not here for long. And he advocates for the language to grow. Washington [D.C.] the President, he is the one that’s going to make the decisions. We are being left out in Washington. America and here, Oklahoma… The late Bo Parrish, from North Carolina, he used to say to us, “tsuyadadugi”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What is it?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏧᏯᏓᏚᎩ Oklahoma “ᎤᎬᏫᏳᏌᏕᎩ, ᎢᎦ ᏓᏟᎯ ᎯᎾ reservation ᏥᏂᎬᏁ,Ꮧ, ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏙ ᏓᏟᎯ” … ᎤᎪᏕᏍᏗ’Ꮫ Ꮭ ᎧᎵ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᏯᏁᎮᏍᏗ, … ᎠᎴ ᎠᏰᏟ, ᎤᏂᎬᎭᏟ, Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏯᏁᎮᏍᏗ, … ᎩᏄᏘ, ᎭᏫᏂ, ᏗᏢ, ᎩᏄᏘ’Ꮽ, -ᏂᎬᏒᎾ,Ꮽ, ᎭᏫᏂ, ᏗᏢ, ᎠᏁᎮᏍᏗ, … Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, … ᎠᏴ, …. ᎢᏗᎦ,ᏔᎭ, ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏅ,ᏖᏟᏓᏍᏗ … ᎦᎪ ᏓᏴᏟᏢ ᎤᎬᏫᏳᏌᏕᎩ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏰᏟ,? … --ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏓᎫᎪ,ᏔᏂᏙᎵ, ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏰᏟ’Ꮄ ᏗᏢ, --ᏫᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏟ, … ᎠᏴ, ᎢᏓᎵ,ᏛᏗ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏴ, ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ, ᎢᏓᎵ,ᏛᏗ ᎮᎾ, ᏕᏗᏲᎱᏍᎦ, … … ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, … ᎢᎦᏛᏅᏖᏍᎪ ᏍᎪᎯ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏃᏭ, ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏰᏟ’Ꮽ ᎢᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ ᎦᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏕᏍᏗ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎠᎹ ᎠᏰᏟ,? … Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏱᎬᏩᏚᎵ, ᎠᏴ, ᏗᎩᎵᏏ, -- ᏗᎩᎵᏏ, ᎬᏩᏕᏁᏗ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏗᏩᏤᎵ, Ꮭ ᏯᏆᏅ,ᏖᏍᏗ, ᏄᏍᏗᏕᎬ
segments.transliteration: tsuyadadugi Oklahoma “ugvwiyusadegi, iga datlihi hina reservation tsinigvne,di, tsinuli,sdo datlihi” … ugodesdi’dv tla kali anitsalagi, yanehesdi, … ale ayetli, unigvhatli, tla howa yanehesdi, … ginuti, hawini, ditlv, ginuti’wu, -nigvsvna,wu, hawini, ditlv, anehesdi, … tla hena, … ayv, …. idiga,taha, nusdv una,danv,tetlidasdi … gago dayvtlitlv ugvwiyusadegi, ahani, tsalagi, ayetli,? … --sgi hena, dodagugo,tanidoli, tsanv,ta, tsalagi, ayetli’le ditlv, --widagali,stanitli, … ayv, idali,dvdi hena, ayv, iditsalagi, idali,dvdi hena, dediyohusga, … … iga hena, … igadvnvtesgo sgohi tsudetiyvda, nowu, gehv tla hena, atsalagi ayetli’wu igadanvtesgo gadohv usdesdi, ahani, ama ayetli,? … tla hena, yigvwaduli, ayv, digilisi, -- digilisi, gvwadenedi diniyotli, diwatseli, tla yaquanv,tesdi, nusdidegv
segments.translation: Tsuyadadugi “Our chief is really fighting for our reservation that we have here.” There will be more non-Cherokees here. Or even the half-bloods, won’t be here. Less than a quarter, the ones that are less than a quarter will be here. We aren’t familiar with the chief's plans for the tribe. Who’s going to be in office here at Cherokee Nation? That’s who’s going to decide for the Cherokee Nation. That’s what’s going to happen. We are fading away. Cherokees like us are fading away, we’re passing on. I think about in about 10 years… I don’t just think about what the Cherokee Nation will be like, but the whole country. I don’t want my children to be giving me grandkids. I don’t know what’s it’s going to be like.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: It’s going to be hard times.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎤᏍᎫᏓᏛ’Ꮽ, ᎮᎾ, ᎢᏗᎪᏩ,Ꮨ Ꮒ,ᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏒ’Ꮓ … ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, … ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᎦᎪ ᏓᏴᏟᏢ, ᎤᎬᏫᏳᏌᏕᎩ,? ᎠᎴ ᏓᏄᎪ,ᏔᏂᏙᎰ? ᎠᏂ-Chinese-Ꮽ ᎤᏂᎬᏫᏳᏌᏕᎩ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ?
segments.transliteration: usgudadv’wu, hena, idigowa,ti ni,dagali,stanisv’no … sgi hena, … doyu, hena, gago dayvtlitlv, ugvwiyusadegi,? ale danugo,tanidoho? ani-Chinese-wu unigvwiyusadegi,’le yigi?
segments.translation: We are only seeing the top of the head. [The beginnings of] Really, who is going to be in office of president? Or what will they be planning. Or maybe the Chinese will take over.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Y’know, ᎠᏴ,’Ꭱ ᏧᎶᏒ … ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ,’ᏭᏛ -- ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏗᎨᎦᎦᎾ,Ꮧ ᎠᎾ,ᎨᏓᏗ --ᎦᏗᏍᎬ, ᎡᎶᎯ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎪᎯ,Ᏼ ᏥᎩ, ᎠᎬᏱ ᎥᎩᎵᏏ, ᎠᎭ,Ꮒ, ᏳᏴᏟᏢ, ᎠᏲᏁᎦ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏴᏟᎦ, ᏱᏍᏕᎵ ᏔᎵᏁᎢ’Ꮕ, ᎥᎩᎵᏏ, ᎤᏠᏱ ᎤᏁᎦ, ᎤᏍᏘᎬ, ᏦᎢ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎠᎩᎧᎭ, Ꮭ’Ꮓ ᏍᎩ Ꮒ,ᎬᎩᏪᏍᏗ, ᏱᎩ, ᏂᏗᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᎠᏭ Ꮎ ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ ᎤᎾᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ;ᏙᏗ,ᏙᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎵᎮᎵᎪ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩ Ꮒ,ᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂ, ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏄᏍᏕᏍᏗ, --ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᎮᎾ, ᏗᎨᎦᎦᎾ,Ꮧ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏭᏟ ᎮᎾ,’Ᏼ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏗ, ᎠᏴ, -Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᎾ,ᏍᏕᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: Y’know, ayv,’e tsulosv … aniyonega,’wudv -- aniyonega, yusdi, digegagana,di ana,gedadi --gadisgv, elohi, asenv, gohi,yv tsigi, agvyi vgilisi, aha,ni, yuyvtlitlv, ayonega,’dv ayvtliga, yisdeli talinei’nv, vgilisi, utloyi unega, ustigv, tsoi, yudetiyvda, agikaha, tla’no sgi ni,gvgiwesdi, yigi, nidigali,sdodi awu na ganaga,ti unali,sdelv;dodi,dodi, gehv sgina aliheligo na ageyutsa, doyu, hena, sgi ni,dagali,stani, sgi’e nusdesdi, --aniyonega, hena, digegagana,di gayu,la, anitsalagi, tsanv,ta, wutli hena,’yv gehesdi, sgi tsinusdi, ayv, -tla sgi yinuna,sdesdi,
segments.translation: Y’know, in the past, I used to say that the white looking is taking over the world. But today, if my grandchild was to walk in, you would think she was white. And the second one is the same; white hair, three years old. I can’t say that now, because they use the Indian hospital. That girl is glad for that. That’s how it’s going to be, we’re going to look white. But they won’t be like us.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Huh uh. ᏃᏭ ᎢᏗᏍᏆᏗᏍᏗᎲ ‘Ꮩ Ꭴ -- ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗᏍ … ᎠᏎᏭ ᎯᎢ ᏱᎦᏪᏍᏗ, ᎠᏩᏚᎵ --ᏱᏍᏕᎵ ᏃᏭ, … ᏍᏓᏝᏅᏓᏓ, ᏱᏍᏗᏪᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: Huh uh. nowu idisquadisdihv ‘do u -- gohu,sdis … asewu hii yigawesdi, awaduli --yisdeli nowu, … sdatlanvdada, yisdiwesdi
segments.translation: Uh-uh. We’re finishing up now. Is there something you all think you want to say? There is time for you to do that.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎨᏒ ᎠᏴ, ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎪ ᏂᎦᏓ, … --ᏥᎩᏍᏕᎵᏍᎪ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏰᏟ ᎢᏕᎲ … ᏧᏂᏢᎩ ᎢᏕᏙᎰ Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏗᎩᎬᏩᎵ;ᏓᏁᎠ, … ᎢᎦ -- Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎦᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎦᏓ, ᏚᎾ,ᏓᏂᎶ Ꮭ ‘ᎸᏢ ᎬᏩᏁᏓᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎰ Ꮭ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᏱᏚᏂᏠ --ᎠᏂᏴᏫ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᎴ … ᎥᏍᎩ ᏗᏢ, ᏂᎨᏒᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏴ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎢᎦ ᎢᎦᏁᎳᏅ ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎳ, ᏃᏭᎴ … ᏓᏂᏍᏕᎵᏍᎬ ᏴᏫ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎠ,
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv gesv ayv, galieligo nigada, … --tsigisdelisgo tsalagi, ayetli idehv … tsunitlvgi idedoho tla gohu,sdi, digigvwali;danea, … iga -- tla hena, igada, hena, igada, duna,danilo tla ‘lvtlv gvwanedasdi, tsigeho tla adela, yidunitlo --aniyvwi, anitsalagi, ale … vsgi ditlv, nigesvna, yigi, ayv, sgina, iga iganelanv iga osda, nigadvnela, nowule … danisdelisgv yvwi, osda, nanadvnea,
segments.translation: Me, I am appreciative of all the help we get through Cherokee Nation. Like, using the hospital. They don’t charge us. There are a lot of people who get sick and don’t have money. And they can come to the clinic. That’s how much the Lord has blessed us. They are helping people, they’re doing good.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, … … ᏍᏓᏱ Ꮒ,ᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂ, ᏞᎩᏭ, … ᏩᏥᎾ, ᎢᎦ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᏓᏤᏩᎠ, … ᏍᏆᏂᏱ, ᏗᏁᎲ ᏓᏂᏍᏕᎸᎯᏙᎰ ᏱᏚᎾᎵ,ᏦᎲᎾ, ᏕᎩᎦ,ᏘᎴᎪ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, -- ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎯᎾ -- ᏧᏂᏢᎩ, ᎤᏁᏓᏍᏗ, ᎢᎦ’Ꮫ ᎤᎵᎮᎵᏍᏗ, … ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎳ, ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, … ᏗᏩᏘᏲᏢ … ᎾᎮᎾ, ᎠᏂᏰᎯᎶᏍᎬ ᏓᎩᎴᏴ,ᏗᏍᎪᎢ … ᎤᎾ ᎠᏬᏢ --ᏥᎦᏘᏴ ᎥᎩᏯᏅ,Ꮧ … ᎠᏴᏫᏯ ᎤᏬᏢ Ꮭ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏱᎨᎮᎢ ᎧᏰᎯ,ᎶᏍᎪ’Ꮫ --ᎧᏳᎶᏍᎪ’Ꮫ ᏥᏆᎾ,ᏘᏢ “Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏱᏗᏣᎬᏩᎳᏁᎠ,!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏓᏩᎵ,ᎬᏩᎳᏁ’Ꮫ!” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎦᏣᏈᏗ ᏱᎩ, ᎯᏅᎪ! ᎤᏣᏘᏂ, ᏪᎾ!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎡᎵ’Ꮫ ᎠᏩᏈᏗ,” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏪᏌ, ᏗᏰᏥᏯᏅᎲ, … ᏔᎵ, ᏧᎾ,ᏛᏐᏅ ᎤᎾ ᏯᎾᏁᎯᎮ ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏃᏭᎴ’Ꮕ ᎾᎯᏳ -Ꮭ ᏗᏆᏁᎵ;Ꮧ, ᏱᎨᎮ’Ꮓ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᎤᏪᏘ --ᏧᏂᏢᎩ, ᎤᎾᏂ,ᏢᏗ ᏥᎪᏢᏒ Ꮎ college ᎾᎥ ᎠᏬᏢ ᏥᎦᏘᏴ … ᎥᎩᏯᏅ,Ꮧ ᎠᏭ, ᏧᏬᏠ’Ꮫ ᎧᏰᎯ,ᎶᏍᎬ ᎠᏫᏄᏥ, ᎧᏰᏓᏍᎩᎾᏗᏍᎪ’Ꮫ Ꮎ “ᎠᏂᎦᎾᎦᏘ, Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏯᏂᎦ,ᏔᎭ” ᏗᏗᎰ’Ꮫ Boy! ᏓᎩ,ᏖᎢᏍᏔᏅ’Ꮫ ᏓᏩᎴᏅ ᎤᏬᏢ ᎠᏩᎴᏂᏢ “ᎣᏝᏪ ᎨᏎᏍᏗ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ … “ᏱᏓᏤᏢ ᎠᏭ ᏱᏫ,ᏣᏅᎪᏣ, ᏱᏣᏂᎩᏌ, … ᎡᎵ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏌᏄᎵ, ᏯᏥᎪᏩᏔ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎥᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏱᏰᎯᎶ ᎠᎭᏂ, --ᏚᏃᏢ ᎠᏂᎦᎾᎦᏘ, ᎤᎾ ᎮᎾ!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ Ms. Carter ᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎮ E.R. “Tell him again, DJ!” ᏗᏳᏛᏅ ᎤᏁᎦ, ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᎬᏛ ᏓᎵ,ᏏᏛᏂᎲ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ down the hallway. ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ,’Ꮫ ᏓᎩᏍᏇᏅ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏱᏚᎴᏁᏭ, ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏱᏥᏴᏂᎴ ᏃᏭ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏯᎩᎸᏂᎴ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎣᏝᏪ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᏗᏍᏔᏅ ᏃᏭ ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ, Dr. Malabrigo ᎠᎩᏯᏅᎲ “ᏂᎯᏍ ᎨᎮ ᏥᏂᏪᏏ,?” – “ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ” *patting ᎤᏃᏴᎬ* Then he patted me on the back. But ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᎪᎱ:ᏍᏗ ᎢᎩᏰᎯᎶᏍᏗ, ᏱᎩ, Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏱᏗᎦᎬᏩᎳᏁᎰ ᏅᏬᏘ, ᏥᎩᏍᎪᎢ … [‘Ꮫ] ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏱᏓᏩᎬᏩᎳᏁᎰ ᎥᎩᎪᎵᏰᏍᎬ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏱᏓᏩᎬᏩᎳᏁᎰ ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏯᏪᎾ, ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ I plan on staying 2 or 3 hours.
segments.transliteration: doyu, hena, … … sdayi ni,dagali,stani, tlegiwu, … watsina, iga adela, datsewaa, … squaniyi, dinehv danisdelvhidoho yidunali,tsohvna, degiga,tilego sgi hena, -- asesgini ahani gehv hina -- tsunitlvgi, unedasdi, iga’dv ulihelisdi, … nigadvnela, iga hena, … diwatiyotlv … nahena, aniyehilosgv dagileyv,disgoi … una awotlv --tsigatiyv vgiyanv,di … ayvwiya uwotlv tla atsalagi, yigehei kayehi,losgo’dv --kayulosgo’dv tsiquana,titlv “tla gohusdi, yiditsagvwalanea,!” tsiyohelv “dawali,gvwalane’dv!” udvnv “gatsaquidi yigi, hinvgo! utsatini, wena!” tsiyohelv “eli’dv awaquidi,” udvnv nahiyu sgi nuwesa, diyetsiyanvhv, … tali, tsuna,dvsonv una yananehihe asenv, tla yawanv,ta, nowule’nv nahiyu -tla diquaneli;di, yigehe’no sgina na uweti --tsunitlvgi, unani,tlvdi tsigotlvsv na college nav awotlv tsigatiyv … vgiyanv,di awu, tsuwotlo’dv kayehi,losgv awinutsi, kayedasginadisgo’dv na “aniganagati, tla gohusdi, yaniga,taha” didiho’dv Boy! dagi,teistanv’dv dawalenv uwotlv awalenitlv “otlawe gesesdi” tsiyohelv … “yidatsetlv awu yiwi,tsanvgotsa, yitsanigisa, … eli gilo yusanuli, yatsigowata,” tsiyohelv “vsgi iga yiyehilo ahani, --dunotlv aniganagati, una hena!” tsiyohelv Ms. Carter dulvwi,sdanehe E.R. “Tell him again, DJ!” diyudvnv unega, nuli,stanv ugvdv dali,sidvnihv ulenvhv down the hallway. gayu,la,’dv dagisquenv asenv, yidulenewu, una’dv agvyi yitsiyvnile nowu nahiyu yagilvnile asesgini, otlawe nuli,stanv udistanv nowu ganaga,ti, Dr. Malabrigo agiyanvhv “nihis gehe tsiniwesi,?” – “ayv’dv tsigehv” *patting unoyvgv* Then he patted me on the back. But iga hena, tla gohu:sdi igiyehilosdi, yigi, tla gohusdi, yidigagvwalaneho nvwoti, tsigisgoi … [‘dv] gohusdi, yidawagvwalaneho vgigoliyesgv tla gohusdi, yidawagvwalaneho doyu, hena, yawena, ganaga,ti I plan on staying 2 or 3 hours.
segments.translation: Really, it’s going to be hard times soon. The government is wasting money. They are helping people overseas. If we get fat, he gets onto us. But here, the sick can go for help at a hospital. It’s a really good thing we’ve got going. I have really fussed about some things. These people that sit there and gripe, burns me up. I was sitting there waiting to be called. An Indian man was sitting there, but he wasn’t Cherokee, and he kept fussing around. I got mad at him. “This place is not costing you a thing!” I told him. “It is costing me!” he said. “If you are able to pay, then get out and go somewhere else!” I told him. “I think I can pay,” he said. And then when he said that he got called. There would’ve been two old men fighting, but I don’t know… Then another time, I wasn’t in church then, I was at that old hospital that was by the college. I was sitting there waiting to be called. There was a young man sitting there fussing and cussing around. “The doctors don’t know anything!” he was saying. Boy, it just burned me up! I got up and went to stand where he was sitting. “Just be quiet!” I told him. “It would be best if you just walk out and go home. Someone might get called quicker,” I told him. “If you are griping that much here. They have other doctors’ offices. Just go over there!” I told him. Ms. Carter was working in the E.R. “Tell him again, DJ!” she said [from a distance]. His face turned white. People in the hallway started clapping. I had already had my fists ready. If he got up, I probably would’ve hit him first and he probably would’ve whooped me. But he just got quiet and put his head down. Then Dr. Malabrigo called me. “Was that you who said that to him?” [he asked me.] “Yeah, it was me,” I said. [patting sound] Then he patted me on the back. But really, we don’t have anything to gripe about. They don’t charge us anything. And I get my medicine there; it doesn’t cost me anything. I see a doctor there, but it doesn’t cost me anything. When I go to the doctor, I plan on staying two or three hours.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ ᎤᏣᏘᏂ,’Ꮲ ᎦᎾ,Ꭶ,Ꮨ, ᏱᏤᎾ, ᎠᏎ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᏃᏭᎴ’Ꮫ Ꮎ Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏯᏁᎵᏍᎪ ᎠᎾᏈᏱᏍᎪ ‘Ꮲ ᎤᏣᏘᏂ, ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ ᎢᎨᏓᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: nowule utsatini,’tlv gana,ga,ti, yitsena, ase yinuli,stana, nowule’dv na tla gohu,sdi, yanelisgo anaquiyisgo ‘tlv utsatini, ganaga,ti igedasdi,
segments.translation: Then if you have to get a referral somewhere else, they don’t care [I.H.S], they still pay for us to go somewhere else for care.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎥᎾ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏍᏗᎦ,ᏘᏲ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎣᏍᏗᏃᎮᎲ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎪ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎢᎦᏓᏁᎳᏁᎸ ᎢᎦᏁᎳᏅ ᏍᎩ ᎤᏓᏅ,ᏖᏟᏙᎯ, Ꮭ ᏴᏫ, ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏅ,ᏖᏟᏙᎯ, ᏱᎩ, ᎤᏁᎳᏅ’Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: vna squu osdiga,tiyo tsigeho osdinohehv asesgini, galieligo nusdv igadanelanelv iganelanv sgi udanv,tetlidohi, tla yvwi, una,danv,tetlidohi, yigi, unelanv’dv
segments.translation: We were talking about it while we were waiting. But I appreciate everything the Lord has blessed us with. That’s who decides everything, not man, it’s Him.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᏊ … ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᎠᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᎠᏪᏙᎸ Ꮭ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᎩᏗ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᏥᏯᏘᏂᏙᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎢᎦᏓ, … ᎢᎦᏓ’Ꮫ truck-Ꭲ load --ᎠᏂᏰᏍ Ꭼ -- ᎠᏂᎩᏍᎪ -- ... ᎤᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ … ᎢᎦ ᎨᏒ ᎣᏍᏓ, Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏱᏚᎾ,ᎬᏩᎴᏁᎰ
segments.transliteration: nowule squu … ali,sdayv,di anigisgv awedolv tla sgina agigidi yigi, asesgini, tsiyatinidoho yudaha igada, … igada’dv truck-i load --aniyes gv -- anigisgo -- ... unali,sdayv,di … iga gesv osda, tla gohusdi, yiduna,gvwaleneho
segments.translation: Also, I have been where they give food, but I haven’t gotten any. But I take some people to get theirs, and some of them get a whole truck-load of food. It’s really good. And it doesn’t cost them a thing.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎣᎩᎾᏁᎵ;ᏔᏅ ᎣᎩᏂᏢᏅ ᎪᏪᎵ, a few years ago,’Ꮲ -- “You’re two dollars over,” [ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏅ] (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎾᎯᏳ ᎣᏂ ᎣᎩᎾᏁᎵ;ᏔᏅ
segments.transliteration: oginaneli;tanv oginitlvnv goweli, a few years ago,’tlv -- “You’re two dollars over,” [una,dvnv] (uyetsi,sgv) nahiyu oni oginaneli;tanv
segments.translation: A few years ago, we applied for that program. “You’re two dollars over,” [they said.] [laughs] We never tried again.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: “Just save two cans for me,” you should’ve told them.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: It’s a blessing!

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Yeah. ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ … ᎠᎭᏂ,’Ꮫ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᎦᏛᎿ, … ᏭᏓᎪᎾᏔᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᎦᏛᎿ, … Venezuela ᏩᏪᏙᎸ mission trip … ᎠᎩᎪᎲᏅ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, Boy, ᏯᏩᏚᎵ, ᏓᏩᏥᎳ ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏝ,Ꭼ ᎦᏥᏯᏘᏃᎯᏍᏗ, --ᎤᏂᎪᏛᏗ ᏴᏫ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏄᏂᎲᎾ, ᎨᎲ … ᎠᏴ, ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏴᎦᏛᏁᎵ ᏂᏗ Ꮟ ᎢᏓᏰᎯᎶᏍᎪ … That’s just mankind now, ᏍᎩᏭ ᏴᏫ, ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏅ,ᏖᏟᏓᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: Yeah. asesgini … ahani,’dv osda, nigadvhna, … wudagonatanv osda, nigadvhna, … Venezuela wawedolv mission trip … agigohvnv gohusdi, Boy, yawaduli, dawatsila una,datla,gv gatsiyatinohisdi, --unigodvdi yvwi, gohusdi, nunihvna, gehv … ayv, iga osda, yvgadvneli nidi si idayehilosgo … That’s just mankind now, sgiwu yvwi, una,danv,tetlidasdi
segments.translation: Yeah, we got it made here. We really are in good shape. I went to Venezuela on a mission trip. I saw a lot of things. I would like to bring Elm Tree Church members so they can see these people who don’t have anything. Here we are, almost everything is done for us and we still are griping. That’s just mankind now, people’s mindset.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎢᏗᏍᏆᏗᏍᎬ --ᏓᎬᏯᏛᏛᏂ, Ꮭ ᏱᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ, ᎨᎲ “echo?”
segments.transliteration: idisquadisgv --dagvyadvdvni, tla yitsanv,ta, yusdi, tsalagi, gvdi, gehv “echo?”
segments.translation: This will be what we finish on. I’m going to ask you, you don’t know what to call an “echo?”

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Echo? … ᎾᎥᏂᎨᏍᏗᏭ, … ᎨᏒ ᎤᎦ,ᏔᏂ “ᎦᎸᏩᎵ;Ꮧ,” ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏱᏁᏣ, ᏥᏣᎷᏨ to repeat it ᎠᏴ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎦᏓ,
segments.transliteration: Echo? … navnigesdiwu, … gesv uga,tani “galvwali;di,” gohusdi, yinetsa, tsitsalutsv to repeat it ayv gehv sgi yigada,
segments.translation: Echo? The closest thing I can think of is “galvwal(i)d(i)” When you say something and it comes back for you to repeat it. That’s what I would say. “galvwal(i)d(i)

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Like when you’re playing music?

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Galvwal(i)di.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: And to me, that’s the only word that I can [think of]. ᎤᏠᏱ ᏱᎦᏪᏍᏗ, “ᏦᏰᎵᏍᎪᎢ” ᏱᏓᏗ ᎮᎾ, “ᏦᏰᎵᏍᎪᎢ”
segments.transliteration: And to me, that’s the only word that I can [think of]. utloyi yigawesdi, “tsoyelisgoi” yidadi hena, “tsoyelisgoi”
segments.translation: And to me, that’s the only word that I can [think of]. Another way to say it, “tsoyelisgoi” we’d say “tsoyelisgoi”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᏅᎲ ᎪᏪᎳ, ᎮᎾ,’Ᏺ Bible-Ꭲ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ, “ankle.” ᏂᎯᎾᎲ ᎤᏪᏘ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎨᎲ Ꮭ Ꮳ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏱᎩ, ankle ᎨᎲ?
segments.transliteration: nanvhv gowela, hena,’yo Bible-i tsalagi, gvdi, “ankle.” nihinahv uweti, tsalagi, gehv tla tsa,dvganv yusdi, yigi, ankle gehv?
segments.translation: And how about, it’s written in the Bible in Cherokee, “ankle.” How about you? You haven’t heard an older way of saying “ankle?”

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: Ankle?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Huh uh, if I did, I couldn’t pronounce it.
segments.transliteration: Huh uh, if I did, I couldn’t pronounce it.
segments.translation: Uh-uh. If I did, I couldn’t pronounce it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s what they say. They say, “It’s hard to pronounce.”

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ, ᏧᎧᏏᏟ, Dorothy Ice ᏣᎩᏃᏎᎸ ᎮᎾ,
segments.transliteration: nahena, tsukasitli, Dorothy Ice tsaginoselv hena,
segments.translation: That Tsukas(i)tli, Dorothy Ice, she told me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, Ana Wright – Jay ᎦᏁᎳ, “Ana Ꮭ ᏱᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ‘ankle’?” ᎩᎳᏭ’Ꮫ ᏥᏄᏪᏒ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏣᎳᎩ, Ꮎ’ᎡᏲ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎪᏪᎳ, Ꮎ … ᎠᏕᎳ, ᏣᏚᎳ,ᏗᏍᎨ ᏈᏗ, ᏣᏂ, ᏥᏭᏂᎷᏤ ᎤᎾ ᎮᎾ,’Ᏺ ᎪᏪᎳ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ankle ᎨᎲ --ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎠᏮᎨᏩ, Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏍᏊ ᏱᏂ,ᎦᏥᏫ, ᎨᏒ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv sawu yuwaga,da, Ana Wright – Jay ganela, “Ana tla yitsanv,ta, yusdi, gehv ‘ankle’?” gilawu’dv tsinuwesv yusdi, gehv tsalagi, na’eyo tsalagi gowela, na … adela, tsadula,disge quidi, tsani, tsiwunilutse una hena,’yo gowela, yusdi, ankle gehv --tsalagi, gvdi, asenv, awvgewa, tla ilvhiyu squu yini,gatsiwi, gesv
segments.translation: Me, one time, Ana Wright, she lives in Jay. “Ana, do you know how to say ‘ankle?’” And she said it right away. But it is written in Cherokee. When he was begging for money, he went to Peter and John. That’s where the word for ankle is written, but I’ve forgotten it and I couldn’t say it.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: Is it? Okay, I’ll have to look that up.
segments.transliteration: Is it? Okay, I’ll have to look that up.
segments.translation: Is it? Okay, I’ll have to look that up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Well, I appreciate you all coming and talking.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: It was good. I learned something.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Me too.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.translation: We were really shaking, “What are we going to say?” we were thinking.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: No, ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎪ’Ꮫ ᏱᎬᏩᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᎨᏒ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏰᏟ ᎤᏍᏕᎸᎯᏓᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ … ᎢᏓᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗ…
segments.transliteration: No, galieligo’dv yigvwadvne,di gesv iga atsalagi, ayetli usdelvhidasdi gesv … idadadolisdi…
segments.translation: No, I’m glad. I’m all ready to do anything for the Cherokee Nation. Let’s pray…

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Hawa.

segments.speaker: dj-mccarter
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏯᏁᎳᏅᎯ ᎦᎶᏁᏓ ᏥᏌ ᏥᏍᎩᏍᏕᎵᏍᎩ ᎢᏨᎵᎡᎵᏤᎰ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏍᎩᏯᏓᏁᎳᏁᎸ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏰᏟ ᎣᎦᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ;ᏙᏗ, ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎮᎾ, ᏣᏓᏁᎳᏅ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏓᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎢᏨᎵᎡᎵᏤᎰᎢ ᏍᎩᏅ ᏍᎩᏰᏲᏂᏙᎮᏍᏗᏭ ᏂᎦᎥ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, --ᎢᏍᎩᏯᏓᏁᎳᏁᎸ ᎤᎵᎮᎵᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᏒ ᎣᎦᏓᏅ,ᏖᏟᏓᏍᏗ ᎣᎩᎷᏤᎰ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏍᎩᏯᏛᏁᎲᎢ ᎠᎴ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏧᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎯ, … ᎦᎯᏝᏫ,ᏍᏗᏕᎨᏍᏗ ᎦᎯᎳᏂᎪᎯᏗᏕᎨᏍᏗ ᎠᎴ ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᏗᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏗᏍᎬᏭ ᎨᏎᏍᏗ ᎠᎴ ᎠᏁᎮᏍᏗ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏁᎲᎢ ᎣᏍᏓᏭ ᏳᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᏗ ᎨᏎᏍᏗ ᏙᏓᏣᏲᎯᏎᎵᏭ ᏫᎦᎶᏁᏛ ᏥᏌ ᏍᎩᏯᏁᎳᏅᎯ ᏍᎩᏙᏓ ᏙᏓᏣᏲᎯᏎᎵ ᎠᎺᏂ
segments.transliteration: sgiyanelanvhi galoneda tsisa tsisgisdelisgi itsvlielitseho nusdv sgiyadanelanelv ahani atsalagi ayetli ogali,sdelv;dodi, gayu,la, hena, tsadanelanv yuli,stanidasdi sgina itsvlielitsehoi sginv sgiyeyonidohesdiwu nigav gohusdi, --isgiyadanelanelv ulihelisdiwu gesv ogadanv,tetlidasdi ogilutseho osda, nisgiyadvnehvi ale ahani, tsunilvwi,sdanehi, … gahitlawi,sdidegesdi gahilanigohididegesdi ale iga hena, digali,sdadisgvwu gesesdi ale anehesdi sidanelv anehvi osdawu yunali,sdanedi gesesdi dodatsayohiseliwu wigalonedv tsisa sgiyanelanvhi sgidoda dodatsayohiseli ameni
segments.translation: Our Father, Jesus Christ, helps us. We are thankful for all you have blessed us with in the Cherokee Nation. For our use, you have already planned what is to happen, we are grateful to you for that. Just be teaching us to do what you will us to do. We appreciate doing what you have planned for us to do. And the ones working here, just be with them and strengthen them and really something is going to happen. And their families, let good happen to them. We just turn it over to you, Lord. Lord, our Father, we turn it all over to you. Amen.

segments.speaker: francis-mccarter
segments.translation: Amen.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Amen. Amen.
